000cafc482ea6cd4.title: Projective curves and Peano Arithmetic
000cafc482ea6cd4.speaker: Alessandro Berarducci
000cafc482ea6cd4.abstract: Joint work with Francesco Gallinaro. Addressing a question of Marcus Tressl, we study the structure Var(C) given by the incidence relation between points and irreducible complex projective curves. We show that Var(C) is bi-interpretable with the polynomial ring C[x] and therefore it has an undecidable theory, as it interprets both C and the subring Z of integers. Nevertheless Var(C) is tame modulo the integers, in the sense that a copy Z of the ring of integers is stably and conservatively embedded in Var(C), all types are controlled by the integers, and the theory of Var(C) is recursively axiomatizable over the complete theory of Z. By contrast, we do not know whether Var(R) is undecidable, or whether it interprets R, where R is the real field and Var(R) is defined like Var(C) but considering only the real points. Replacing C with the field K of complex algebraic numbers yields a structure Var(K) that is not elementary equivalent to Var(C) but it is again recursively axiomatizable over Z. Our results depend on a bi-interpretation of Var(C) with the two-sorted structure (C,Fin(C)) consisting of the field C and a sort for its finite subsets, with the membership relation between the two sorts.

003ccbf4ca3f631a.title: Combinatorial tools for posets topology and simplicial complexes
003ccbf4ca3f631a.speaker: Lucas Pouillart
003ccbf4ca3f631a.abstract: Topological theory of posets originates from a simple observation : the Möbius function of an interval of a poset P can be interpreted as the Euler characteristic of a simplicial complex. It turned out that in a lot of cases, these complexes hold a lot more information on P and that a lot of interesting examples satisfy the (homotopy) Cohen-Macaulay property, which gives both nice topological and algebraic properties. A lot of techniques were developed by combinatorialists to prove the Cohen-Macaulay property and give interpretations of algebraic and topological problems for posets as enumeration problems, and I will present some of them in this talk.

00b094a68b6cb8a6.title: Scattering and smoothing for the two-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
00b094a68b6cb8a6.speaker: Muyuan Lyu
00b094a68b6cb8a6.abstract:
Scattering theory describes the large-time behavior of nonlinear evolution equations through comparison with a linear flow. This raises a further question: can the nonlinear correction to the asymptotic state be smoother than the initial data?
I will begin with an introduction to scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, highlighting several developments that motivate this question. I will then present a deterministic smoothing result for the two-dimensional cubic equation. Assuming that a solution scatters in the harmonic Sobolev space (\mathcal H^s), with (s>0), the difference between its scattering state and its initial datum belongs to (\mathcal H^{s+\sigma}) for every (0<\sigma<\min{2s,1}). The proof combines the lens transform, which turns the large-time problem into a finite-time endpoint problem, with bilinear Strichartz estimates and harmonic spectral analysis. The emphasis will be on the mechanism behind the regularity gain. The talk is intended for graduate students in analysis, with no prior familiarity with nonlinear scattering required.
00b094a68b6cb8a6.department: GT des doctorants ANH et ANEDP
00b094a68b6cb8a6.series_name: GT des doctorants ANH et ANEDP

017389cb74557221.title: Exposés de Marco Di Marco et Jean-François Babadjian
017389cb74557221.abstract:
Marco Di Marco :
Title: Quantization of measures in Carnot groups
Abstract: The aim of the talk is to present a sub-Riemannian analogue of the celebrated Zador theorem, a cornerstone of the theory of quantization of measures. After a brief introduction to sub-Riemannian geometry and Carnot groups, I will outline the key ideas behind the proof of the Euclidean Zador theorem and its sub-Riemannian version. Talk based on a joint work with Mikaela Iacobelli.
Jean-François Babadjian :
Titre : Energies de surfaces anisotropes, courbure et approximation champ de phase
Résumé : Dans cet exposé, je présenterai des résultats obtenus en collaboration avec Blanche Buet (LMO, Orsay) et Michaël Goldman (LAMA, Créteil) concernant les effets régularisants de termes de type courbure moyenne pour les modèles avec interface en présence d'anisotropie. Lorsque la tension superficielle est une fonction convexe de la normale, l'anisotropie est dite faible. Ceci assure généralement la semi-continuité inférieure de l'énergie associée. En revanche, si la tension superficielle dépend de la normale de manière non convexe, cette forte anisotropie peut engendrer des instabilités liées à l'absence de semi-continuité inférieure de la fonctionnelle. Nous étudions les effets régularisants de l'ajout d'un terme d'ordre supérieur de type Willmore à l'énergie. Nous considérons deux types de problèmes : une généralisation anisotrope non convexe du périmètre et une fonctionnelle aux discontinuités libres de Mumford-Shah, anisotrope non convexe. Dans les deux cas, nous établissons les propriétés de semi-continuité inférieure des énergies, ainsi qu'une approximation par Gamma-convergence par des modèles de champ de phase. L'un des aspects originaux de notre travail dans le cadre des problèmes à discontinuités libres est le traitement des énergies de points qui repose sur un résultat de type Gauss-Bonnet pour les varifolds.

0320d26b64efe087.title: Height pairing over arithmetic function fields
0320d26b64efe087.speaker: Juan Felipe Castro-Cardenas
0320d26b64efe087.abstract:
Since the foundational work of Néron and Tate in the 60s, various conjectural definitions of the height pairing for homologically trivial algebraic cycles on smooth, projective varieties over a number field, or more general global fields, have been proposed by Belinson, Bloch, Gillet-Soulé and Schneider, among others. The related concept of height functions on sub-varieties was extensively developed by Faltings and, in the early 2000s, extended by Moriwaki to varieties defined over finitely generated extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$, also called arithmetic function fields. More recently, Bruno Kahn has used algebraic intersection theory to give a geometric construction of a ``refined" height pairing over the function field of a smooth, projective variety $B$, taking its values in $\textrm{Pic}(B)$.
In this talk, I will present an Arakelov-geometric analogue of this construction over an arithmetic function field $K$, taking its values in the arithmetic Picard group of a normal arithmetic variety whose function field is $K$. The construction is in two parts: first, Kahn's definitions are extended and adapted to arithmetic varieties using the intersection theory on regular schemes of Gillet-Soulé, and then the Archimedean term is added by considering generalized Green currents satisfying some ``admissibility" conditions, inspired by the original work of Arakelov. If time allows, I will discuss the connection with Moriwaki's work and with the work of Brosnan and Pearlstein on the degeneration of the Archimedean height pairing.

04020acb99e057eb.title: Centre des super-algèbres de Lie affines et des opérateurs pseudo-différentiels
04020acb99e057eb.speaker: Shigenori Nakatsuka
04020acb99e057eb.abstract:
Dans la théorie des représentations, le centre des algèbres
elles-mêmes joue un rôle fondamental. Par exemple, le centre des
algèbres enveloppantes des algèbres de Lie réductives a été décrit par
Harish-Chandra, permettant la décomposition en blocs de la catégorie O.
Dans le cas affine, Feigin et Frenkel ont identifié le centre à
l’algèbre des fonctions sur l’espace des opérateurs différentiels.
Frenkel et Gaitsgory l’ont ensuite utilisé pour décrire la catégorie O
sphérique, l’un des premiers résultats de la correspondance de
Langlands géométrique locale.
Dans mon exposé, je présenterai des résultats sur les super-algèbres
de Lie affines, en particulier pour le cas gl(n|m). Dans ce contexte,
les opérateurs pseudo-différentiels apparaissent naturellement. Si le
temps le permet, j’expliquerai également l’intérêt de considérer le
cadre super et le cas en général.
Ce travail est basé sur des collaborations avec D. Adamović et B. Feigin.

05360b5228778ddf.title: Automath! À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? Maths + IA Controversy Workshop
05360b5228778ddf.abstract:
À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? En deux ans à peine, les mathématiques semblent être passées du statut de frontière de l’IA à celui de territoire de l’IA, du statut d’idéal cognitif servant à tester les capacités de raisonnement des modèles d’IA, à celui d’infrastructure de connaissance, productive et mobilisable de façon en partie automatisée. C’est en tous cas le message envoyé par OpenAI (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture d’Erdős), Anthropic (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture jacobienne), Google DeepMind (e.g. AlphaProof) ou encore la DARPA avec le programme ExpMath. Si le moment se veut historique, la suite n’est pas écrite pour autant. La communauté mathématique se prépare et s’interroge : À quel endroit faut-il résister ? Et à quel autre faudrait-il plutôt s’adapter ? À quelles conditions ? Comment souhaitons-nous voir se dessiner les trajectoires de l’IA et de la recherche mathématiques ? L’équipe Inria SIRA, le LFPC et le collectif Automath invitent la communauté mathématique élargie à se saisir collectivement de ces enjeux lors d’une journée de workshop (ai4sciencecontroversy.com)
Comme en témoigne la Déclaration de Leiden [1.] ou le formule Terence Tao dans une publication récente [2.] : « How should the mathematical community respond to the advent of modern AI technologies, and their real and/or claimed capabilities to perform mathematical tasks? (…) It is a metamathematical question. »

0621e7a3e9e91c61.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
0621e7a3e9e91c61.speaker: Marc Burger
0621e7a3e9e91c61.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

06382073817a5fcb.title: Les polygraphes réguliers et leur théorème de recollement homotopique
06382073817a5fcb.speaker: Clémence Chanavat
06382073817a5fcb.abstract:
Je commencerai par présenter deux (ou trois) manières de régulariser les polygraphes, que j'appellerai méthode-Hadzihasanovic, méthode-Steiner et, si le temps le permet, méthode-Henry.
J'expliquerai pourquoi la méthode-Hadzihasanovic ne produit pas toujours des polygraphes, à moins que l'on impose aux ∞-catégories strictes des lois d'échange supplémentaires, dictées par des égalités de topologie combinatoire.
Je terminerai par un théorème de recollement, issu de mes derniers travaux, qui assure que certains de ces polygraphes sont librement générés en un sens homotopique, ce qui signifie que ce sont aussi des polygraphes dans la théorie des (∞, n)-catégories.

0917917e9d99d041.title: Maximal functions, Nikodym sets and local smoothing estimates
0917917e9d99d041.speaker: Chen Mingfeng
0917917e9d99d041.abstract:
Séminaire d'Analyse
I will discuss some recent works related to maximal operators and Nikodym sets in the plane. Nikodym constructed a measure-zero Borel set in the plane that contains a line segment passing through each point in the unit square. Fenton and Falconer asked whether a similar construction is possible when “lines through a point” are replaced by ”circles with a prescribed center.” This was answered in the negative by Bourgain and Marstrand. We study a generalization of this question, in which “lines through a point” or “circles with prescribed center” are replaced by general analytic families of plane curves.
Using decouping, we prove new maximal function and local smoothing estimates for families of curves satisfying a multi-parameter analogue of Sogge's cinematic curvature condition. Combining with a recent nonlinear generalization of Falconer's prescribed projection theorem to construct Nikodym-type sets, we characterize when Nikodym-type sets exist for analytic families of plane curves.

0c236cc43e34da37.title: Automath! On the Origin of False Proofs by Means of Bugs in Proof Assistants, Yannick Foster
0c236cc43e34da37.abstract:
Proof assistants have entered mainstream mathematical discourse so fast that now they are almost silently accepted as the ultimate guardians of correct proofs. Both the recent forced Euler blowup result by Buckmaster and Alpöge and the solution to the Navier-Stokes problem announced by OpenAI come with proofs verified in the Lean proof assistant, with code almost entirely written using LLMs. Only six months ago an experiment led by Tristan Stérin showed that LLMs are effective at finding bugs in proof assistants: several bugs were found both in Lean and the Rocq proof assistant. As a demonstration, Ramana Kumar has published a proof of the Collatz Conjecture in Lean, making use of a bug. These experiments have been followed by a flurry of bugs in Lean and Rocq found by Daniel Selsam at OpenAI. In this talk, I will discuss the tension between proof assistants as guardians for LLM-coded proofs and as vulnerable target for LLM-guided bug search. In this talk I will discuss what a false proof is, what a bug in a proof assistant is, and give a genealogy of bugs that have been found this year, focusing on what features of proof assistants they usually occur in. I will conclude with some thoughts on how we can have and increase trust in results developed in proof assistants.

0ce8f3485edf456e.speaker: Andrea Guerrieri
0ce8f3485edf456e.abstract:
In this talk I will discuss an attempt of unifying under a simple geometric picture, the plethora of crossing symmetric dispersion relations existing in literature.
Each dispersion is valid on a different finite window in energy, but none of them could be extended to infinity.
I will explain how they can all be understood from a simple choice of a foliation of the kinematics space.
This geometric viewpoint also suggests the existence of a particular (but not so nice) foliation that naturally covers all energies. Unfortunately, this example turns out to be impractical for phenomenological and bootstrap applications. I will comment why, and what teaches us about the dual bootstrap.

0d498cd40a8129cc.title: Autour de la localisation des racines d’un polynôme après dérivation
0d498cd40a8129cc.abstract:
Dans cet exposé nous étudierons plusieurs questions autour du problème de la localisation des racines d’un polynôme dérivé par rapport aux racines de ce polynôme.
Tout d’abord nous rappellerons quelques résultats déterministes classiques autour de ce problème. Puis nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle probabiliste en nous demandant où se situent les racines du polynôme dérivé lorsque les racines du polynôme initial ont été tirées de manière indépendante et identiquement distribuée dans le plan complexe. Pour finir, nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle d’analyse en expliquant comment ce dernier peut mener à l’étude d’une équation aux dérivées partielles non linéaire et non locale obtenue après passage à une limite champ moyen
.

0f301c233516e3fe.title: Aicha Ben Dhia (CFM) et Théo Leblanc (Ceremade)
0f301c233516e3fe.abstract:
Aicha Ben Dhia (CFM): Prédire les futures vagues de chaleur grâce à un simple ajustement statistique
Résumé : Pour savoir à quels types de phénomènes météorologiques extrêmes nous devrons faire face avec la hausse des températures, on s’appuie généralement sur des modèles de circulation générale. Ces modèles climatiques sont l’outil le plus complet et le plus fiable pour décrire la complexité des phénomènes climatiques. Mais cette complexité a des inconvénients importants : ces modèles sont très lourds en calcul, lents à exécuter et exigent un haut niveau d’expertise pour être manipulés. Au Resilience Lab, nous avons adopté une approche radicalement différente et construit des prédictions simples en extrapolant des séries temporelles de température. Nous parvenons ainsi à estimer la probabilité d’atteindre 50 °C à Paris dans les années à venir, ainsi que dans plusieurs autres endroits du monde. Nous réalisons plusieurs étapes de vérification pour tester la « robustesse » de ces résultats.
Théo Leblanc (Ceremade) : Introduction aux séries temporelles et à leur estimation statistique
Résumé : Dans cet exposé nous introduirons les principaux concepts nécessaires à la modélisation des séries temporelles, avec un intérêt particulier pour les processus AutoRégressifs (AR). Nous présenterons différentes méthodes d’estimation des paramètres caractérisant ces processus, ainsi que les principales composantes et propriétés des séries temporelles. Nous aborderons notamment les outils permettant d’estimer et d’analyser les dépendances temporelles présentes dans les données.

0fa27aa0d99704ee.title: Hidden symmetries of modular geodesics
0fa27aa0d99704ee.speaker: Alain Valette
0fa27aa0d99704ee.abstract:
The dihedral group of order 4 acts on the conjugation classes of hyperbolic elements of $PSL_2(\mathbf{Z})$: by passage to the inverse, by conjugation by an element of $GL_2(\mathbf{Z})$ of determinant -1, and by the product of the 2. Via the dictionary (which will be recalled) between closed hyperbolic and geodesic conjugation classes of the modular surface, the same group acts on modular geodesics, which can therefore acquire non-trivial symmetries by being fixed under one of the 3 involutions above. We will characterize these invariant geodesics and we will see that there is a strong link with Gauss' reciprocal, ambiguous and inert quadratic forms. It is a joint work with C.-L. Simon (Rennes)

1015b3e268727771.title: Condensed homotopy types in algebraic geometry, arithmetic geometry, and logic
1015b3e268727771.speaker: Peter Haine
1015b3e268727771.abstract:
Let X be a locally topologically noetherian scheme. In their paper on the proétale topology, Bhatt and Scholze defined the proétale fundamental group π1proét(X). The profinite completion of π1proét(X) recovers the usual étale fundamental group. Moreover, π1proét(X) agrees with π1ét(X) when X is normal, but π1proét(X) has the better property that it classifies Qp-local systems. In this talk, we’ll explain how to use condensed mathematics to define a “condensed homotopy type” whose fundamental group refines the proétale fundamental group. We’ll also talk about two related “condensed homotopy types”: one for adic spaces and one in the setting of logic. All three are special cases of a more general invariant of ∞-topoi. For adic spaces, the fundamental group refines the de Jong fundamental group, and in logic, the fundamental group recovers the Lascar group of a complete first-order theory.
These results come from several projects, carried out jointly with Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Martini–Wolf, Achinger–Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Wolf, and Damaj–Zhang.

108bbe056f400b03.title: Advances in Quantum Cryptography, Paris
108bbe056f400b03.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on mathematical developments in Advances in Quantum Cryptography (QCRYPTO).
September 13th to December 10th, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
** REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE **
Deadline for financial support request is March 15, 2027
Presentation of the programme
Quantum cryptography lies at the intersection of cryptography, quantum information, and computational complexity. Quantum technologies offer new cryptographic possibilities, while also changing our understanding of which security guarantees and computational tasks are achievable. Recent developments have revealed deep connections between these areas, but many fundamental questions remain open.
This programme will bring together researchers from theoretical computer science, mathematics, cryptography, and quantum information. It will explore three closely connected directions: information-theoretic foundations, including quantum communication, nonlocality, randomness, and device-independent security; complexity-theoretic foundations, including quantum proofs, verification, reductions, and computational assumptions; and computational and interactive primitives, including commitments, zero knowledge, secure computation, and protocols involving quantum devices.
Through an introductory school, seminars, focused workshops, informal discussions, and extended research visits, the programme aims to develop a common language across neighboring communities. It will provide opportunities for sustained collaboration between senior and junior researchers, encourage new research partnerships, and help identify important directions for the next stage of quantum cryptography.

11bdf66a7d726fe3.title: 2-catégories de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes et invariants quantiques homotopiques
11bdf66a7d726fe3.speaker: Matthew Cellot
11bdf66a7d726fe3.abstract:
À la fin du XXe siècle, les travaux remarquables de Jones, Drinfeld,
Witten et Kontsevich ont permis la construction de nouveaux invariants de
variétés, appelés invariants quantiques, obtenus notamment à partir de certains
groupes quantiques. L’un des premiers succès dans cette direction est l’invariant
de Turaev-Viro-Barrett-Westbury des 3-variétés, défini comme une somme d’états
à partir de la donnée d’une catégorie de fusion. Plus récemment, Douglas et
Reutter ont construit des invariants de 4-variétés par somme d’états, en utilisant
des 2-catégories de fusion.
Cet exposé porte sur les invariants quantiques homotopiques, c’est-à-dire les
invariants quantiques de variétés munies d’une structure supplémentaire codée
par une application vers un espace topologique. Plus précisément, nous
généralisons la construction de Douglas-Reutter pour obtenir des invariants des
3-fibrés plats sur les 4-variétés ou, de manière équivalente, des 4-variétés
munies d’une classe d’homotopie d’applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie.
Les structures algébriques utiles pour cette construction sont les 2-catégories
de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes, où le 3-groupe modélise le 3-type
d’homotopie. Dans ce cadre, les applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie sont
codées par des triangulations coloriées. En démontrant une généralisation
coloriée du théorème de Pachner, nous obtenons que ces invariants sont
indépendants de la triangulation choisie.

131473e6f96dac79.title: Braid group invariance of quantum tori and applications
131473e6f96dac79.speaker: Francesca Paganelli
131473e6f96dac79.abstract:
A well-known fact in classical Lie theory is that the Weyl group W associated with a simple, complex, finite-dimensional Lie algebra g acts by isometries on the dual of the Cartan subalgebra. In particular, the symmetric bilinear form defined on the weight lattice is invariant under the W-action.
In this talk, I will present an analogue of this invariance phenomenon for skew-symmetric bicharacters in the context of quantum affine algebras. Specifically, we will consider the groups of fundamental and pre-fundamental l-weights (which can be viewed as affine analogues of the fundamental weights of g). By results of Chari and Frenkel–Hernandez, the braid group B associated with g acts on these groups of l-weights. We then introduce the skew-symmetric bicharacters on the groups of l-weights defined by Nakajima and Hernandez, and extended by Bittmann and myself. I will show that these bicharacters are invariant under the B-action on l-weight groups, and present an application concerning quantum QQ-systems in the theory of shifted quantum groups.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

French-Japanese Conference on Arithmetic Geometry in Honor of Takeshi Saito and Takeshi Tsuji
May 31 - June 4, 2027 at IHES - Marilyn and James Simons Conference Center
How to get to IHES
This conference, which is part of a long-standing tradition of French-Japanese collaboration in arithmetic geometry, will honor two leading figures of this partnership: Professor Takeshi Saito, on the occasion of his retirement, and Professor Takeshi Tsuji, on the occasion of his 60th birthday.
The main topics of the conference will include:
p-adic Hodge theory, including the p-adic Simpson correspondence, geometric Sen theory, p-adic Galois representations and (φ,Γ)-modules, prismatic cohomology, and their applications;
Ramification theory, including singular support and characteristic cycles of l-adic étale sheaves (in equal and mixed characteristic), compatibility with proper higher direct images, Swan conductors, and epsilon-factors;
Geometric Langlands theory, l-adic, p-adic, and for modules with integrable connections, in characteristic p and in characteristic 0.

13e82dee4c5aba9f.title: Multi-scale modeling and analysis of signal processing in neurons
13e82dee4c5aba9f.speaker: Claire Guerrier
13e82dee4c5aba9f.abstract: In this talk, I will present models for signal propagation in neurons, ranging from the macro- to the micro-scale, with various applications to neuronal signalling. The first application concerns myelin plasticity, and the influence of neuronal myelin geometry on signal transmission. We investigate the evolution of the maximum of a signal in a damped heat equation on x>0, with a Dirichlet boundary condition representing the signal, which models signal transmission in a myelinated internode. We derive an expression of the solution, and derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator at x=0. We then investigate the max. At a more refined scale, to investigate signal summation in the neuronal dendritic tree, we consider the Poisson-Nernst Planck system of equations representing ionic electrodiffusion in an electrolyte. This system expresses a sharp boundary layer of the size of the Debye length at the boundary, where the extra-charges accumulates. In particular, we derive an asymptotic approximation of the solution at steady state, in the regime of small Debye length.

14b6db91ed022655.title: Sur l´homologie asymptotique des graphes Lagrangians. (Avec Alfonso Sorrentino)
14b6db91ed022655.speaker: Rafael Ruggiero
14b6db91ed022655.abstract: Nous demontrons que les directions homologiques asymptotiques des orbites dans un graphe Lagrangien invariant par un flot Hamiltonien de Tonelli dans le tore au dessus du niveau critique de Mañé sont contenues dans un cône positif dans la norme stable autour d´un vecteur dans le premier group d'homologie à coefficients réels. En dimension 3, nous trouvons un rapport entre l´homologie asymptotique d´un graphe Lagrangien invariant et l´ensemble de rotation de Misiurewicz-Ziemann. Comme application, nous demontrons qu´il n'existent pas de graphes de Hedlund dans le 3-tore, ceux-ci sont des graphes avec exactement 3 orbites périodiques dont l´homologie engendre le premier group d´homologie.

1537f1b99bdaf0ae.title: Mass in almost Kähler geometry
1537f1b99bdaf0ae.speaker: Partha Ghosh
1537f1b99bdaf0ae.abstract:
In this talk, I present an explicit formula for the ADM mass of asymptotically
locally Euclidean (ALE) almost Kähler manifolds. The formula expresses the mass in terms of
the total Hermitian scalar curvature and topological data associated with the underlying almost
complex structure, extending a result of Hein and LeBrun in the Kähler ALE case. The proof is
based on a spin-c adaptation of Witten’s proof of the positive mass conjecture in the spin case
and is therefore distinct from previous complex-geometric methods. In dimension 4, I show that
one can prove a positive mass theorem and a Penrose-type inequality for asymptotically Euclidean
(AE) almost Kähler manifolds using this formula.

166b8544bc7b6165.title: Mosquito borne disease outbreak : Climate change impact to Physics Informed Neural Network use
166b8544bc7b6165.speaker: Aniket Banerjee
166b8544bc7b6165.abstract:
Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are expanding across new
territories as their vector, the tiger mosquito _Aedes albopictus_,
tracks a warming climate. Forecasting where and when outbreaks will
occur requires models that are both mechanistically faithful to mosquito
ecology and disciplined by real observational data — yet the
biological parameters that govern transmission, such as the biting rate,
the extrinsic incubation period and mosquito survival, are precisely the
ones we cannot measure directly in the field.
In this talk, I present a national -scale furcating framework that
couples a mechanistic _Aedes albopictus_ population model, in the spirit
of the Arbocarto approach, to a vector-to-human transmission layer, and
the use of Neural Network use to predict diffusion pattern in
epidemiological systems. I will explain the modelling choices behind the
population and transmission layers, the structure of the inverse
problem, and how PINNs let a mechanistic model "speak" to messy,
heterogeneous data.

1a3c2db8bdf64cb8.title: The Spectral Gap for the Steklov Problem
1a3c2db8bdf64cb8.speaker: Asma HASSANNEZHAD
1a3c2db8bdf64cb8.abstract: We study the spectral gap for the Steklov problem on a Riemannian manifold. When a manifold has only one boundary component, it is known that the geometry of a boundary collar alone can provide a lower bound on the spectral gap. We therefore focus on manifolds with at least two boundary components. We show how the interior geometry can influence the spectral gap and establish a new connection between Steklov spectral gaps and the Neumann eigenvalues of interior subdomains. We then discuss applications of this connection to negatively curved manifolds. It is based on joint work with Tirumala Chakradhar and Bruno Colbois.
1a3c2db8bdf64cb8.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

1b6482bf56f6c80c.title: Origami Tori
1b6482bf56f6c80c.speaker: Richard Schwartz
1b6482bf56f6c80c.abstract:
An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R3. It is surprising that these things exist, but thanks to the work of Burago and Zalgaller in 1960 they do. 30 years later, B&Z proved that every flat torus is realized as an origami torus. In 2023, Lazarus and Tallerie proved that you can realize all flat tori using a single underlying triangulation with about 2500 vertices.
The question remained: how many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In this talk I will prove that the minimum number of vertices needed is 8. I will also discuss joint work, with Peter Doyle, proving that almost every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. Finally, I will explain work-in-progress with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel, which shows that in fact every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. If I have time, I will also discuss hyperbolic versions of this business.

1c56a31b769064af.title: Eliminating imaginaries in perfect, bounded, multi valued PAC fields
1c56a31b769064af.speaker: Bryan Gonzalez Leandro
1c56a31b769064af.abstract: Elimination of imaginaries is a fundamental structural property in model theory, which roughly means that definable equivalence classes can be coded by tuples of elements from the structure, allowing us to treat them as ordinary elements of the structure. In the context of valued fields, significant progress was initiated by Haskell, Hrushovski, and Macpherson, who described a language in which the theory ACVF eliminates imaginaries. Building on this foundation, Rideau-Kikuchi and Montenegro proved elimination of imaginaries for bounded pseudo p-adically closed fields equipped with finitely many independent valuations. In this talk, I will explain how their techniques can be adapted to prove weak elimination of imaginaries for perfect bounded PAC fields equipped with finitely many independent valuations. The strategy combines an extension theorem for types to invariant types with an amalgamation result.

1f1458617ffc520d.title: Sur la probabilité qu’un entier possède un diviseur de la forme $p-1$ dans un intervalle donné
1f1458617ffc520d.speaker: Rebecca Abi Abdallah
1f1458617ffc520d.abstract: Dans cet exposé, nous étudierons la fonction qui compte les entiers naturels inférieurs ou égaux à $x$ possédant, dans un intervalle $(y,z]$, un diviseur de la forme $p-1$, où $p$ est premier. En analysant le comportement asymptotique de cette quantité dans les différents régimes de $z=z(y)$, nous mettrons en évidence une transition de phase qui révèle les dépendances entre ces événements de divisibilité en fonction de la longueur logarithmique de l’intervalle $(y,z]$. Notre résultat généralise un théorème de Ford correspondant au cas $z=x$. Ceci est un travail en collaboration avec V. Kovaleva, J. Schlitt et N. Tardy.

209c607116a6625d.title: Verso Blueprint: Reimagining Blueprints for the AI Era
209c607116a6625d.speaker: Emilio Gallego Arias
209c607116a6625d.abstract:
Large-scale formalization projects have long needed tools to
coordinate contributions, track dependencies, and connect mathematical
exposition with formal proofs. A key example is Lean
Blueprint. Introduced in 2020 for the sphere eversion project, Lean
Blueprint extends plasTeX to provide a shared map of statements,
dependencies, Lean declarations, and progress. Lean Blueprint's model
has been quite influential and has helped shape how mathematicians and
formalizers work together on large-scale formalization projects.
This talk presents recent work on Verso Blueprint, a Lean-native
implementation of the Lean Blueprint concept built on Verso, Lean's
official markup language. Designed for close integration with Lean,
Verso Blueprint maintains a three-layer database linking source
material, informal statements, and their formalized counterparts. The
database is populated from Verso documents, analysis of Lean
declarations, and other user-provided data. Interactive HTML views
provide navigation and previews, connecting mathematical exposition
with the formal development. We have now largely reached our original
goal, with functionality comparable to Lean Blueprint or Lean
Architect.
But matching that functionality is no longer enough: this is an
extraordinary moment for formalisation. The practice is radically
chaining even as we build its tools.
When we began this project, our central use case was for humans to
write detailed statements and dependencies to guide
formalization. Today, coding agents are increasingly writing and
interacting with the blueprints themselves in an autonomous
fashion. Blueprints are taking on the reverse role: not just guiding
the construction of formal proofs, but making AI-generated proofs
intelligible to humans. At the same time, dependency tracking and
organizational information remain essential for coordinating
large-scale autoformalization. For example, Prove2Me, a theorem
database with dependency tracking, played a key coordination role in
the recent Fermat's Last Theorem auto-formalization milestone.
What comes next for blueprints in this extraordinary moment? We are
redesigning Verso Blueprint around the idea of "programmatic
blueprints": human-readable, machine-actionable objects synchronized
with formal developments. Our ambition is for blueprints to become a
*foundational harness for AI-assisted formalization*, maintaining the
shared state of a project and coordinating what happens next across
mathematicians, formalizers, code repository workflows, and agents.

2329424545630694.title: Left Structures and Purity
2329424545630694.speaker: Kevin Schlegel
2329424545630694.abstract:
Under mild assumptions on a small additive category, we establish a one-to-one correspondence
between its exact structures and certain closed subsets of the Ziegler spectrum of the ind-completion
of the category. This is based on a newly developed connection between exact structures and the theory
of purity. In fact, our results also apply to left structures, which vastly generalize exact structures.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.
2329424545630694.organizer: J. Alev, D. Hernandez, B. Keller, Th. Levasseur, et S. Morier-Genoud.

2441fff651625374.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
2441fff651625374.speaker: Tyler Franke
2441fff651625374.abstract: Braided module categories are module categories over braided monoidal categories equipped with extra structure providing an action of the braid group of the annulus on endomorphism spaces. In this talk, I will define a small braiding on an inclusion of monoidal categories, which provides a braiding between objects in these categories. Small braidings give certain tensor ideals the canonical structure of a braided module category. Quantum groups are a natural source of small braidings, and from this we construct concrete examples of braided module categories and quantum moment maps. I will outline how we plan to use these examples in skein-theoretic realisations of double affine Hecke algebras and certain modules thereof. Based on joint work-in-progress with Ingo Runkel and Volker Schomerus.

25f6fa5329055aa8.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
25f6fa5329055aa8.speaker: Serge Cantat
25f6fa5329055aa8.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.

28f2104b1eca4107.title: Cohomologie étale des algèbres de Stein.
28f2104b1eca4107.speaker: Olivier Benoist
28f2104b1eca4107.abstract: Les variétés de Stein sont les analogues, en géométrie analytique complexe, des variétés algébriques affines. Je présenterai une version du théorème de comparaison d'Artin dans ce cadre : la cohomologie singulière à coefficients finis d'une variété de Stein est isomorphe à la cohomologie étale de son algèbre de fonctions holomorphes globales. Comme application, je montrerai que toute classe de cohomologie entière de degré au moins 2 sur une variété de Stein est supportée sur un sous-ensemble analytique strict. Les preuves combinent des outils de géométrie algébrique et de géométrie analytique.

2c0d38068fdfcb8e.title: Conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland et applications
2c0d38068fdfcb8e.speaker: Vanja ZULIANI
2c0d38068fdfcb8e.abstract:
Les conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland nous permettent d’étudier les espaces de modules d’objets dans une catégorie dérivée et de décomposer chaque objet en facteurs plus “simples". Cette thèse examine deux applications de la théorie des conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland. Dans la première partie, on étudie la géométrie d’une variété de Fano de dimension 8 et d’indice 3, définie comme une sousvariété lagrangienne d’une variété hyperkählérienne ; on étudie une dégénérescence semistable et on en déduit ses nombres de Hodge. En particulier, on observe que la structure de Hodge est de type K3 et que le rang de Picard est égal à un.
La deuxième application de la théorie des conditions de stabilité concerne l’étude du programme des modèles minimaux non commutatifs. On montre que les décompositions semiorthogonales standard sur les grassmanniennes, les quadriques et les hypersurfaces cubiques de dimension 3 et 4 sont induites par des chemins quasi-convergents dans la variété de stabilité, dont la charge centrale est donnée par la cohomologie quantique. Une partie du dernier chapitre est basée sur un travail en collaboration avec Tomohiro Karube et Antonios-Alexandros Robotis.

2f6a7dba6a4ac654.title: The Liquid Drop Model: From Minimizers to Non-Spherical Equilibria
2f6a7dba6a4ac654.speaker: Monica Musso
2f6a7dba6a4ac654.abstract:
Speaker: Monica Musso, University of Bath
Abstract for the mini course: Introduction to the Liquid Drop Model: Minimizers, Stability and Nonexistence
The liquid drop model, introduced by Gamow to describe atomic nuclei, is a classical problem in the calculus of variations involving the competition between surface tension, which favours compact shapes, and Coulomb repulsion, which favours spreading and fragmentation.
In this introductory lecture, I will present the mathematical formulation of the model and review some fundamental results concerning the existence and geometry of energy minimizers. Particular attention will be given to the role of balls, their minimality and stability properties, and the nonexistence of minimizers for sufficiently large masses. I will discuss the main mathematical ideas behind these results, as well as some open questions.
Abstract for the talk: Beyond Minimizers: Constructing Non-Spherical Equilibria
While balls are stationary configurations for the liquid drop energy at every volume, the existence of other critical points is a much more delicate question.
In this talk, I will discuss recent results on the existence and construction of smooth, compact, non-spherical equilibria of the liquid drop model, in both the small- and large-mass regimes. For small masses, I will describe the construction of configurations consisting of two nearly spherical regions connected by a very thin catenoidal neck. For large masses, I will present equilibria resembling necklaces of pearls, whose geometry is related to Delaunay unduloids. I will also discuss bifurcation phenomena from spherical equilibria, which give rise to further families of non-spherical stationary configurations.
The emphasis will be on the geometric ideas and analytical techniques behind these results, particularly singular perturbation methods and Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction. Together, these constructions reveal the richness of the critical point structure of the liquid drop energy, far beyond the theory of minimizers.
This work is in collaboration with M. del Pino, F. De Regibus, R. Frank, M. Grossi and A. Zuñiga.

2fa116d313ddc82a.title: The Pentagram Map and Ramifications
2fa116d313ddc82a.abstract:
October 12-15, 2026
at IHES - Marilyn and James Simons Conference Center
How to get to IHES
This workshop explores the mathematics connected to the pentagram map and its generalizations.
With 3 talks per day, spread out over 4 days, leaving time for individualized interactions, it will not be confined to the special topic of the pentagram map, but rather an exploration of the kind of mathematics that it relates to: integrable systems, algebraic dynamics, projective geometry and cluster algebras.
The pentagram map is a geometrically flavored dynamical system defined on polygons by a simple and projectively natural straight-line construction.
Starting with a polygon, one intersects the shortest diagonals in cyclic order to produce a new polygon with the same number of vertices.
Though quite elementary to define, the pentagram map turns out to have a deep structure connected to completely integrable systems, symplectic geometry, cluster algebras, dimers, algebraic dynamics, and moduli spaces.
The same goes for the many generalizations of the pentagram map, some of which are still quite mysterious.

3346e36d97318869.title: Centre des super-algèbres de Lie affines et des opérateurs pseudo-différentiels
3346e36d97318869.speaker: Shigenori Nakatsuka
3346e36d97318869.abstract:
dans la théorie des représentations, le centre des algèbres elles-mêmes joue un rôle fondamental. Par exemple, le centre des algèbres enveloppantes des algèbres de Lie réductives a été décrit par Harish-Chandra, permettant la décomposition en blocs de la catégorie O. Dans le cas affine, Feigin et Frenkel ont identifié le centre à l’algèbre des fonctions sur l’espace des opérateurs différentiels. Frenkel et Gaitsgory l’ont ensuite utilisé pour décrire la catégorie O sphérique, l’un des premiers résultats de la correspondance de Langlands géométrique locale.
Dans mon exposé, je présenterai des résultats concernant les super-algèbres de Lie affines. Dans ce contexte, les opérateurs pseudo-différentiels apparaissent naturellement. Si le temps le permet, j’expliquerai également l’intérêt de considérer le cadre super. Ce travail est basé sur des collaborations avec D. Adamović et B. Feigin.

364676bd1455fdad.title: Équations diophantiennes et cohomologie galoisienne
364676bd1455fdad.abstract:
Le point de départ de cet exposé est d’expliquer comment classifier les surcorps non-commutatifs d’un corps K (par exemple, R a un surcorps non-commutatif donné par le corps des quaternions H, qui est de dimension 4 sur R).
L’idée clé derrière cette classification est la notion de « descente galoisienne » : informellement, elle consiste à dire que les objets définis sur un corps K viennent d’objets définis sur la clôture algébrique de K qui sont munis d’une action d’un certain groupe qu’on appelle le groupe de Galois absolu de K.
La classification de tels objets fait naturellement intervenir des groupes de cohomologie associés à ce groupe de Galois absolu, appelés groupes de cohomologie galoisienne. Ces groupes sont intimement liés aux propriétés diophantiennes du corps K : si certaines équations homogènes sur K avec beaucoup de variables ont des solutions, alors ces groupes de cohomologie ont tendance à s’annuler à partir d’un certain degré.
Pour rendre compte de ce phénomène, Lang a introduit la notion de corps C_i et a conjecturé que les corps C_i avaient une cohomologie triviale en degré > i. Cette conjecture est ouverte pour i>2 et on sait que sa réciproque est fausse. Si le temps le permet, je parlerai des conjectures de Kato et Kuzumaki qui raffinent la propriété C_i pour tenter d’avoir une condition diophantienne qui caractérise l’annulation de la cohomologie du corps en degré >i.

368086fb50b1a547.title: Origami Tori
368086fb50b1a547.speaker: Richard Schwartz
368086fb50b1a547.abstract: An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R^3. It is surprising that these things exist, but they have been known to exist since 1960. How many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In my talk, I will explain my proof that you can do it with 8 but not with 7. I will also explain why almost every flat torus is isometric to an origami torus -- this is joint work with Peter Doyle. If time permits I will also explain why, in fact, every flat torus is isometric to an 8-vertex origami torus. This is upcoming work with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel.

3725e6d2e1bc26a0.speaker: Jean-Philippe Burelle
3725e6d2e1bc26a0.abstract: Motivated by a family of examples constructed by R. Schwartz based on Pappus's theorem, we explore constructions of representations of discrete groups arising from incidence theorems in projective spaces. Schwartz recently proved that his construction parametrizes the boundary of a connected component of Anosov representations in a certain moduli space of representations of PSL(2,Z) into Isom(SL(3,R)/SO(3)). Weisman. This is joint work in progress with W. Dimoune.

37fdfc02835bbede.title: Géométries de Wasserstein slicées et hiérarchiques : flots de gradient et analyse variationnelle
37fdfc02835bbede.speaker: Christophe Vauthier
37fdfc02835bbede.abstract: Dans cette thèse, nous analysons la géométrie induite par deux variantes de la distance de Wasserstein en transport optimal: la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et la distance Wasserstein sur Wasserstein. Dans la première partie de cette thèse, nous nous focalisons sur la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et nous examinons les propriétés de convergence et les points critiques de sa forme semi-discrète. Puis, nous définissons un cadre général pour l'étude de points critiques de fonctionnelles définies sur des espaces de mesures de probabilités, que nous utilisons pour démontrer que les points critiques en contexte semi-discret sont un cas particulier d'un type spécifique de mesures critiques que nous appelons points critiques lagrangiens. Nous étudions ensuite les propriétes des points critiques lagrangiens de la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, notamment leur existence et leur stabilité. Enfin, nous étudions la quantification de la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et nous dérivons de nouvelles bornes sur son erreur de quantification uniforme. Dans la deuxième partie de cette thèse, nous nous concentrons sur le cas particulier du transport optimal où l'espace sous-jacent est lui-même un espace de probabilités. Nous construisons en particulier une structure de type riemannien sur l'espace de mesures de probabilités sur des mesures de probabilités $\cPP{\R^d}$, muni de la distance Wasserstein sur Wasserstein, nous permettant de considérer des flots de gradient Wasserstein sur cet espace. Nous montrons ensuite comment ce cadre théorique peut être appliqué à divers problèmes de machine learning, par le biais de flots de jeux de données représentés par des éléments de $\cPP{\R^d}$. Enfin, dans la troisième et dernière partie, nous étendons cette théorie à toute la suite d'espaces $\cPn{n}{\cM} = \cP_2(\ldots\cP_2(\cM)\ldots)$ obtenue en itérant l'opération $\cP_2$ sur une variété riemannienne $\cM$. Nous montrons que ces espaces peuvent à nouveau être munis d'une structure de type riemannien d'une façon systématique, nous permettant d'analyser leur géométrie, de caractériser leurs géodésiques et de définir le gradient de fonctionnelles.

3996e8437440b208.title: Characterizing totally geodesic manifolds in negative curvature
3996e8437440b208.speaker: David Fisher
3996e8437440b208.abstract: The talk centers around the question of what invariant sets for Anosov flows and diffeomorphisms can look like. It is known that closed invariant sets can be arbitrarily bad and for example be fractals of arbitrary Hausdorff dimension. An old and interesting question, first raised by Hirsch in 1968 is what closed invariant submanifolds can look like. There are many surprising rigidity results in this direction, some quite old, and recently Rose Eliott Smith and I proved a new one, giving a dynamical characterization of totally geodesic submanifolds in negative curvature. I will explain the theorem and both the classical motivation and some more contemporary motivation. If time permits I will give some hints about the proof and particularly how it uses very old results from Smale and Mane.

39d41dbc5a696086.title: Markov triples and tropical geometry
39d41dbc5a696086.speaker: Mikhail Shkolnikov
39d41dbc5a696086.abstract: Markov triples forming an infinite set of triples of natural numbers were introduced by Markov as a part of his study of relation between real binary quadratic forms and the square lattice. Frobenius conjecture, remaining open for more than one hundred years, has acquired numerous reformulations in various contexts; in its original formulation, it states that the maximal element of a Markov triple determines the remaining two numbers in this triple. In my talk, i will tell about two other equivalent statements in the tropical context recently obtained by Kevin Calderon: the first one is given via tropical cotangents of angles formed by two tangents to Markov hyperbolas, and the other one is a conjectural statement about tropical wave fronts of Markov triangles.

3a6b8cafc8ff9b85.title: (Annulé) The Hecke orbit conjecture and $p$-adic monodromy of Tate-linear varieties
3a6b8cafc8ff9b85.speaker: Livia Grammatica
3a6b8cafc8ff9b85.abstract: If $A$ is a $g$-dimensional principally polarized abelian variety over $\mathbb{C}$, it is not hard to show that the Hecke orbit of $A$ (the set of principally polarized abelian varieties which are isogenous to $A$) is dense in $\mathcal{A}_g(\mathbb{C})$. This fails in positive characteristic because Hecke orbits are confined to Newton strata, the loci of $\mathcal{A}_g$ where the Newton polygon of the abelian variety is constant. The Hecke orbit conjecture, now a theorem of Chai-Oort, thus asks whether Hecke orbits are dense in their respective Newton strata over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. In the first part of the talk, we will explain Chai's strategy for proving the Hecke orbit conjecture, and we will present the recent results in $p$-adic monodromy that led to a proof, by D'Addezio and van Hoften, of the Hecke orbit conjecture for all Shimura varieties of Hodge type. In the second part we present a refinement of these $p$-adic monodromy techniques, with an application to the rigidity of Tate-linear varieties, which are central objects in Chai's work.

3be960b59aed7c34.title: Combinatorics, Arithmetic and Geometry working group: Shkolnikov, Kartas, Wang
3be960b59aed7c34.abstract:
11:30-12:20: Mikhail Shkolnikov (ICMS Sofia)
Title: Combinatorial and Geometric aspects of Tropical Optics
Abstract: This talk is dedicated to an introduction and an overview of the current status of the theory of tropical wave fronts and their caustics seen from toric perspective. Particular emphasize will be made on the ongoing finite-time analysis of the structure of critical events in the tropical wave front propagation operating on convex polyhedra and the role of corresponding algebro-geometric singularities in the character of this canonical evolution as being developed in joint project with Grigory Mikhalkin. We will finish with discussing the fundamental open problem of understanding possible pre-final moments of such an evolution, which is fully resolved only in dimension 2, with final moments now being classified in all dimensions.
15:00-15:50: Konstantinos Kartas (Université de Paris-Saclay)
Title: Taming perfectoid algebras
Abstract: The almost purity theorem is a foundational result about perfectoid algebras which, as the name suggests, holds only in an "almost" sense. We show that suitable completeness hypotheses on the algebras allow us to remove the "almost". More precisely, spherically complete perfectoid algebras satisfy non-almost purity for Galois p-extensions and countably saturated perfectoid algebras satisfy non-almost purity for all finite étale extensions. Joint work with Franziska Jahnke.
16:00-16:50: Yiyu Wang (Ohio State University)
Title: Grothendieck weight on permutohedral varieties and matroids
Abstract: Minkowski weights provide a combinatorial model for the Chow ring of smooth toric varieties. In this talk, I will introduce their K-theoretic analogue, the Grothendieck weights, and describe them explicitly for permutohedral varieties. Our results include a balancing condition and a product rule for Grothendieck weights. These results give a concrete way to work in the K-ring of the permutohedral variety.
I will then discuss applications to matroids, where many naturally occurring K-classes admit simple descriptions in terms of Grothendieck weights. In particular, I will explain how the motivic Chern class of a hyperplane arrangement complement in its wonderful model only depends on its underlying matroid.
If time permits, I will briefly mention some further applications of Grothendieck weights to positivity questions in matroid K-theory.

3c401f304354fdf9.title: Introduction to circle-packings
3c401f304354fdf9.speaker: Jules Duhamel
3c401f304354fdf9.abstract:
Le séminaire des doctorants se propose de fournir aux doctorants une occasion de s'ouvrir aux autres domaines des mathématiques que le leur. A chaque séance, un intervenant réalise un exposé sur un fait standard de leur domaine d'étude, de niveau adapté à l'ensemble des doctorants.
Introduction aux empilements de cercles
Le théorème des empilements de cercles (circle-packings) est un théorème très amusant et dont la preuve est élémentaire. Il permet d'associer un empilement de cercles à toute triangulation simple et planaire. Ce théorème a été découvert indépendamment à trois reprises, à chaque fois pour des motifs différents. Ce n'est qu'après une conférence donnée par Thurston en 1985 que la communauté mathématique se saisit des empilements de cercles. L'objectif de l'exposé est de présenter une preuve du théorème et quelques-unes de ses multiples applications.
----
The PhD students seminar aims to provide PhD students with an opportunity to explore other areas of mathematics beyond their own. At each session, a speaker gives a presentation on a standard topic in their field of study, at a level suitable for all phd students.
The circle-packing theorem is a very fun theorem whose proof is elementary. It associates a circle-packing to any simple planar triangulation. This theorem was independently discovered three times, each time with different motives. In 1985, Thurston gave a talk on the subject which is responsible for the growth of interest for circle-packings in the mathematical community. The goal of the talk is to give a proof of the theorem together with a few of its numerous applications.

3c972f7a7651e0fe.speaker: Shunsuke KANO
3c972f7a7651e0fe.abstract:
The skein algebra of a surface S is defined using isotopy classes of curves in the thickened surface SxI, where I is the unit interval, subject to local relations involving crossings and their smoothings. Qiu pioneered the use of decorated marked surfaces as a geometric framework for studying the derived category of the Ginzburg dg algebra associated with a triangulation of a marked surface. In this talk, I will introduce the skein algebra of a triangulated decorated marked surface and discuss its connections with the derived Hall algebra of the perfectly valued derived category of the corresponding Ginzburg dg algebra. This is a report on ongoing joint work with Denis Lyskov.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Instiut Henri Poincaré.

The Jacobian conjecture states that for any polynomial map from to itself, if it is everywhere a local diffeomorphism, then it admits a polynomial global inverse. In this talk, I will present the three-dimensional counterexample to this conjecture posted by L. Alpöge on and credited to Claude.
After stating the conjecture and the counterexample, I will explain the geometric interpretation of the counterexample which was posted by A. Jiang and credited to ChatGPT. Finally I will give some observations about the history of the conjecture and its significance.
We answer this problem coming from representation theory using topological tools. On the representation theory side we define extensions of Habiro type rings. On the topological side, we construct a universal Jones link invariant and a universal Alexander link invariant. Putting these together, our universal invariants of geometrical nature take values in the extended Habiro rings that we construct.

4201edc0ce8aedc6.title: A homotopy-theoretic approach to representation stability
4201edc0ce8aedc6.speaker: Nicolas Guès
4201edc0ce8aedc6.abstract:
In a series of papers from the 2010s, Church, Ellenberg and Farb developed the notion of representation stability, aimed at understanding the asymptotic behavior of natural sequences of representations of the symmetric groups S_n, particularly those arising from homological invariants. Such phenomena typically occur for FI-modules, i.e., functors from FI (the category of finite sets and injections) to abelian groups.
In this talk, I will propose a homotopical refinement of representation stability: a derived version adapted to (co)FI-spaces. This viewpoint sheds light on how the phenomenon of representation stability can arise from the high (co)cartesianity of certain cubical diagrams. With this point of view, I will show how one can deduce polynomial growth results for the homotopy groups of ordered configuration spaces on closed manifolds, recover the best known bounds on their cohomology, and generalize stability results of Palmer concerning moduli spaces of submanifolds.

420f8bb1d8144cf4.title: Diffuse Interface Models and their Sharp Interface Limits
420f8bb1d8144cf4.speaker: Helmut Abels
420f8bb1d8144cf4.abstract:
CANCELED – For personal reasons, Helmut Abels has unfortunately been forced to cancel his seminar. – CANCELED
Speaker: Helmut Abels (Universität Regensburg)
Interfaces separating two or more species or components of a material are omnipresent in applications in the sciences. Nowadays there are two main classes of models to describe interfaces, both from a theoretical and practical point of view: In classical so-called « sharp interface models » the species or components under consideration fill disjoint domains that are separated by lower dimensional surfaces of a certain regularity. On the other hand in « diffuse interface models » a partial mixing of the species or components on a small length scale is taken into account, which leads to an interfacial layer of small but positive thickness. This has the advantage that the interfaces do not need to be resolved explicitly and singularities in the interfaces can be described consistently.
In the first part of the talk we will give an overview of some basic diffuse interface models with applications to material sciences. Moreover, we will discuss some analytic results on the relation between diffuse and sharp interface models, when the interfacial thickness of the diffuse interface tends to zero. The analysis is based on formally matched asymptotic expansions (in a rigorous manner) together with uniform estimates for the linearized operator. In this part we will focus on the Allen-Cahn equation as basic model.
In the second part we will discuss a Navier-Stokes/Allen-Cahn system, which describes the flow of two macroscopically immiscible viscous incompressible fluid, separated by a diffuse interface. We will present some recent results on novel higher-order estimates for the sharp interface limit of this system. With the aid of a suitable weight taking the distance to the interface and the interfacial thickness into account we obtain optimal regularity estimates, which are uniformy in the interfacial thickness. This enables to improve previous convergence results in two space dimensions significantly and extend results to three space dimensions. This is a joint-work with Mingwen Fei, Yadong Liu, and Maximilian Moser.
Helmut Abels

456ce1bf0416a7ce.title: The Diederich–Fornæss index and global regularity of the $\overline{\partial }$-Neumann prblem
456ce1bf0416a7ce.speaker: Bingyuan Liu
456ce1bf0416a7ce.speaker_affiliation: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
456ce1bf0416a7ce.abstract: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^{n} $ be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain. The $\overline{\partial }$-Neumann problem is Hodge theory with boundary on Ω. Its solution operator $N_{q}$ is globally regular, i.e. preserves $C^{\infty}(\Omega)$ , on strongly pseudoconvex domains (Kohn), but not on the worm domains (Christ). Since the 1990s it has been conjectured that global regularity follows when the Diederich–Fornæss index of $\Omega$ equals 1. This index is the supremum of $η \in]0,1]$ such that $-(-ρ )^{η}$ is plurisubharmonic near $b\Omega$ for some defining function ρ. I will present joint work with Emil Straube. Suppose that, for some $1\leq q_{0}\leq n-1$, the $q_{0}$-sums of the Levi eigenvalues are comparable, and the index is 1. Then $N_{q}$ and the Bergman projections $P_{q-1}$, for $q_{0}\leq q\leq n,$, are continuous in every Sobolev space $W^s(Ω)$. In particular, the conjecture holds in $C^2$, and there having index one is preserved under biholomorphisms. The key point is that index one gives a self-bounded gradient condition, which is weak pointwise but suffices in an integrated $L^2$ form.

49b03c6a0f17eb48.title: Near-horizon Collisions at the Extreme: Naturalness and Observability of Critical Near-horizon Collisions around Near-extremal Black Holes
49b03c6a0f17eb48.speaker: Delilah Gates
49b03c6a0f17eb48.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In principle, rapidly rotating black holes could naturally act as particle colliders because geodesics particles that collide can exhibit center-of-mass (CM) energies that diverges in the limit that the black hole approaches extremality and the collision radius approaches the horizon, provided that one particle has a critically tuned angular momentum. In this talk, I present work to understand the naturalness and observability of these critical-particle collisions around near-extremal BHs. I will highlight 1) the landscape of conditions under which these critical-particle collisions occur, 2) the CM energy achievable for critical-particle collision where one particle falls from in from infinity and the other particle is part of an accretion disk, and 3) the observability as measure by the escape probability and expected energy of emission born of a critical-particle collision.

4b4b6dae159dc939.title: Diameters and box spaces
4b4b6dae159dc939.speaker: Alain Valette
4b4b6dae159dc939.abstract:
Le séminaire d'algèbres d'opérateurs aura lieu à l'IHP le temps du trimestre "algèbres d'opérateurs : approximation, ridigité et dynamique"
Résumé : Consider a sequence $(X_k)_{k>0}$ of finite, connected, d-regular graphs with size going to infinity. It is known that, if $(X_k)_{k>0}$ is an expanding sequence, then the diameter of $X_k$ is exactly logarithmic in the number of vertices of $X_k$. On the opposite, for $0<\alpha \leq 1$, say that $(X_k)_{k>0}$ has property $D_\alpha$ if the diameter of $X_k$ grows at least like $|X_k|^\alpha$: this is a strong form of non-expansion. For a finitely generated, residually finite group $G$, let $(N_k)_{k>0}$ be a filtration of $G$. The box space associated with $(N_k)_{k>0}$ is the sequence of finite Cayley graphs $(Cay(G/N_k,S))_{k>0}$ where $S$ is a fixed finite generating set of $G$. It turns out that property $D_\alpha$ for a box space is related to interesting algebraic properties of $G$, and we will survey results by Breuillard-Tointon, Khukhro-Valette, and Guo-Tointon. Now, assuming that $G$ can be realized as a subgroup of $GL_n(A)$, where $A$ is a unital, commutative ring, we have filtrations given by congruence subgroups, giving rise to arithmetic box spaces. Sometimes the growth of the diameter is more constrained on arithmetic box spaces then on general box spaces, i.e. non-arithmeticity can be detected purely metrically. We will illustrate this with lamplighter groups $L_F:=F\wr\Z$, where $F$ is a finite abelian group. This is joint work with Etienne Grezet.

(but well-known and welcoming international researchers) Seminar, or papers that were not
necessarily in final form and could even stay forever in an almost unfinished state. This journal
was the Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux, that became later a more
classical journal, the Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux.
Among the many papers that were not in a final form in the Séminaire (and that were
not necessarily followed by a "real paper'' appeared later elsewhere), one can find a quite
modest paper entitled "Suites infinies à répétitions bornées'' (in the 1983--1984 issue).
In that paper there was a short study of the number of cycles of a family of permutations
related to the Toeplitz transform of sequences.
Up to notation the number of cycles of the same family of permutations appeared in 2021 in
a paper by Y. Guo, G. Han, and W. Wu about "apwenian sequences''.
The formulas given in these two papers were distinct, though---of course---equivalent.
Thus it was tempting to prove directly their equality.
This possibly frivolous question lead to unexpected discoveries: the family of permutations
above or a variation of it are linked to numerous subjects, not only in mathematics (combinatorics
of words, dynamical systems, number theory, correcting algorithms), but also in card-shuffling,
juggling, change-ringing, poetry, and music composition.
The details can be found in a paper by J.-P. A., M. Stipulanti, and J.-Y. Yao, appeared in
The Mathematical Intelligencer in 2026.

4d7eec8a6e9177c1.title: Sur les points fixes des sous-groupes de Moy-Prasad dans les représentations admissibles irréductibles de groupes réductifs p-adiques (Travaux en cours avec Marie-France Vignéras et Rachel Ollivier)
4d7eec8a6e9177c1.speaker: Guy Henniart
4d7eec8a6e9177c1.abstract:
Soit p un nombre premier et F une extension finie de Q_p.
Soit G un groupe réductif connexe sur F, et C un corps algébriquement
clos. Dans une C-représentation admissible irréductible π du groupe
G(F), les points fixes par un sous-groupe ouvert K forment un C-espace
vectoriel de dimension finie d(K, π). Si π est de dimension infinie,
il est intéressant de savoir comment d(K, π) croît quand K devient de
plus en plus petit. Par exemple, on peut partir d’un sous-groupe de
Moy-Prasad G_x,r (pour x dans l’immeuble de G sur F et r un nombre
réel positif), et faire croître r. Grâce à des résultats de
Harish-Chandra (1978) et T.-C.Tsai (2025), nous prouvons que si la
caractéristique de C n'est pas p, alors pour tout entier n assez grand,
d(G_x,r+2n, π) a la forme P(p^n), où P est un polynôme à
coefficients rationnels, dépendant de x, r, et π. Nous soupçonnons
que cela reste vrai si C est de caractéristique p, mais seul le cas où
G est GL₂ et F=Q_p est connu. Pour G général, même le cas
particulier où π est la représentation de Steinberg de G(F) est
difficile. Cependant, nous obtenons un résultat asymptotique plus
faible, valable pour tout π. Au passage, nous examinons la condition
que G_x,r soit un pro-p groupe uniforme.

4da9456f5a8ed2e4.title: Plongements conformes de surfaces de Riemann
4da9456f5a8ed2e4.speaker: Alaa Mohamed BOUKHOLKHAL
4da9456f5a8ed2e4.abstract: Étant donnée une surface riemannienne, il n’est pas toujours possible de la plonger isométriquement dans une variété riemannienne donnée M, notamment en raison de contraintes telles que la courbure. Cependant, la situation devient beaucoup plus flexible si l’on cherche un plongement conforme. Dans cet exposé, on montre l’existence de plongements conformes dans le cas où M est une variété pseudo-riemannienne. De plus, on montre que l’inclusion de l’espace des immersions lisses et conformes dans l’espace des immersions induit une bijection entre les composantes connexes par arcs de ces deux espaces.

4dac8adbfe225827.title: Marco Plazzogna - Endogenous Dynamic Networks for Heteroscedastic Outcomes
4dac8adbfe225827.abstract:
Many economic and financial systems are naturally represented as networks: the outcome of one unit may depend on those of other units through relationships that evolve over time. A central difficulty is that these relationships need not be exogenous. The network itself may react to the same shocks that affect the variables of interest, creating an endogeneity problem that cannot be addressed by treating network weights as fixed or predetermined.
We study a dynamic spatial model in which the interaction network is time-varying and generated by an auxiliary formation process. Dependence between innovations driving network formation and the structural outcome shock is explicitly incorporated through a control-function approach.
The framework is further extended to allow for conditional heteroskedasticity. In particular, we distinguish between two potentially different dynamic networks: one governing the transmission of outcomes in the conditional mean, and another governing the propagation of past shocks in the conditional variance. This makes it possible to separate network effects on the level of the process from network effects on its risk and volatility.
The resulting model provides a framework for studying systems in which both interactions and uncertainty evolve endogenously over time.

4e8b508ceb426af1.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
4e8b508ceb426af1.speaker: János Pach
4e8b508ceb426af1.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
4e8b508ceb426af1.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?

55607a7d512a37dc.title: Système d’Euler biparti pour les points de Drinfeld–Heegner
55607a7d512a37dc.speaker: Yichao Tian
55607a7d512a37dc.abstract:
Le système d’Euler biparti classique associé aux points
de Heegner a été introduit par Howard, basé sur des travaux pionniers
de Bertolini et Darmon. Il est un outil puissant pour l’étude de
l’arithmétique des courbes elliptiques sur le corps des nombres
rationnels.
Dans cet exposé, on expliquera un analogue de ce système d’Euler
biparti pour les points de Drinfeld–Heegner sur les courbes de
Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler, qui sont des analogues des courbes de
Shimura sur un corps global de fonctions (i.e. le corps de fonctions
d’une courbe projective lisse sur un corps fini). Ces résultats
pourraient avoir des applications à l’étude des groupes de Selmer
des courbes elliptiques non isotriviales sur de tels corps. Comme un
ingrédient technique de la démonstration, on obtient également un
analogue du lemme d’Ihara classique pour les courbes de
Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler.

55a678e9c2da4d53.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
55a678e9c2da4d53.speaker: Amnon YEKUTIELI
55a678e9c2da4d53.speaker_affiliation: Ben Gurion University, Israel et Université Paris 7
55a678e9c2da4d53.abstract:
The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms f_0, f_1 : A --> B.
Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings Cyl_q(B), which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring Cyl(B). For q=1 this recovers Keller's original construction.
The sets SHom_q(A,B) of DG ring homomorphisms A \to Cyl_q(B) form the simplicial Hom set SHom(A,B). Our main result is that when A is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set SHom(A,B) is a Kan complex.
We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B), including invariance under quasi-isomorphism B' \to B, and that the automorphism groups are abelian. We also indicate some applications of this work, including to DG categories.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

56258b78a2e0566c.title: A mathematical perspective on Transformers
56258b78a2e0566c.speaker: Borjan GESHKOVSKI
56258b78a2e0566c.abstract: Physics has long supplied mathematics with some of its central equations. I will argue that Transformers, the engine of large language models, are becoming a source of the same kind. Starting from raw code, under various scaling assumptions, one can interpret Transformers as an interacting particle system in continuous time; tools from PDE and kinetic theory then explain empirically observed phenomena such as representation collapse and “lost in the middle”. Unlike in physics, however, the laws here are designed rather than given, so mathematical understanding can be written back into the architecture. I will close with some thoughts on what this two-way exchange means for applied mathematics.
56258b78a2e0566c.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

565a9a9df1453759.title: Singularities of the critical wave equation and the Keller-Segel system formed by the collision of collapsing solitons at a point
565a9a9df1453759.speaker: Charles Collot
565a9a9df1453759.abstract: Critical evolution PDEs may have solutions forming a singularity in finite time with anomalous self-similarity. There are now numerous examples where a soliton (here a stationary state or a traveling wave) collapses at a point due to its interactions with the remainder of the solution. Much less is known about singularities formed by several solitons collapsing simultaneously at a single point, especially in the non-radial case. The first example was constructed for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation by Martel-Raphael [Ann. Sci. ENS 2018]. I will present examples of such solutions for the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system in two dimensions [joint work with Ghoul-Masmoudi-Nguyen 2024] and for the cubic wave equation in four dimensions [ongoing joint work with Li to appear]. The associated patterns are caused by different effects for each equation: the solitons' own dynamics, their interactions, and their interactions with the remainder of the solution which is affected by the presence of the multiple nearby potentials from the solitons. I will present ideas for the construction of an approximate solution, and its stability analysis based on the control of its modulating parameters and of suitable norms for the remainder, adapted to the multiscale feature of the problem.

56b6da91a344dc66.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
56b6da91a344dc66.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
56b6da91a344dc66.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

587da5bbe15d97a3.title: David Bessis – La chute de l’économie du théorème
587da5bbe15d97a3.speaker: REPORTÉ
587da5bbe15d97a3.abstract:
Si les machines démontrent les théorèmes, que reste-t-il aux humains ? En quelques mois, les progrès des modèles d’IA ont fait entrer la recherche mathématique mondiale dans une crise sans précédent, remettant à la fois en cause ses critères de valeur, son organisation pratique et son image publique. En dépit de sa nouveauté radicale, la crise actuelle nous confronte à des questions anciennes, jamais résolues, dont les mathématicien(ne)s ont longtemps cru qu’elles étaient purement théoriques : que sont les mathématiques ? Comment créent-elles de la valeur ? Quel rôle jouent-elles dans la cognition humaine ?
