b21032da43b2e91e.title: Informative Trains: A Memory-Efficient Journey to a Self-Stabilizing Leader Election Algorithm in Anonymous Graphs
b21032da43b2e91e.speaker: Sylvain Gay
b21032da43b2e91e.abstract:
We study the self-stabilizing leader election problem in anonymous n-nodes networks. Achieving self-stabilization with low space memory complexity is particularly challenging, and designing space-optimal leader election algorithms remains an open problem for general graphs. In deterministic settings, it is known that Ω(log log n) bits of memory per node are necessary [Blin et al., Disc. Math. & Theor. Comput. Sci., 2023], while in probabilistic settings the same lower bound holds for some values of n, but only for an unfair scheduler [Beauquier et al., PODC 1999]. Several deterministic and probabilistic protocols have been proposed in models ranging from the state model to the population protocols. However, to the best of our knowledge, existing solutions either require Ω(log n) bits of memory per node for general worst-case graphs, or achieve low state complexity only under restricted network topologies such as rings, trees, or bounded-degree graphs.
In this paper, we present a probabilistic self-stabilizing leader election algorithm for arbitrary anonymous networks that uses O(log log n) bits of memory per node. Our algorithm operates in the state model under a synchronous scheduler and assumes knowledge of a global parameter N = Θ(log n). We show that, under our protocol, the system converges almost surely to a stable configuration with a unique leader and stabilizes within O(poly(n)) rounds with high probability.
Our algorithm is inspired by the uniform constant-state leader election protocol in [Vacus and Ziccardi, PODC 2025] for the beeping model (without self-stabilization). A novel component of our approach is the introduction of an information train mechanism that propagates O(log n)-bit information across the network while requiring only O(loglog n) local memory per node. We believe this mechanism may be of independent interest for the design of space-efficient self-stabilizing distributed algorithms.

b22eaa44c92b9f1a.title: Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables
b22eaa44c92b9f1a.abstract:
La Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables aura lieu le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à l'Institut Henri Poincaré.
Titles and Abstracts
Mini-course (2x1h) by Cédric Boutillier
Title:
Abstract:
Seminar talk (1h) by Elia Bisi (Università degli Studi di Firenze)
Title: Matrix Whittaker processes
Abstract: The log-gamma polymer is a prominent integrable model in the KPZ class: the law of its partition function is a marginal of a Whittaker measure, a positive-temperature analogue of the Schur measure. I will present a non-commutative generalisation, in which the “particles” are positive definite matrices. These evolve as interacting multiplicative random walks with inverse Wishart increments, arranged in a triangular array with push-and-block interactions. Using intertwining relations, we show that, for suitable random initial configurations, the bottom edge of the array evolves as an autonomous Markov process, with a kernel built from Whittaker functions of matrix arguments. For a singular initial state, its fixed-time law is a matrix Whittaker measure. Consequently, the matrix log-gamma polymer partition function is distributed as the first marginal of this measure.
Joint work with Jonas Arista and Neil O’Connell.

b3a1f693246fd183.title: Séminaires de doctorants
b3a1f693246fd183.speaker: Marius Kjaersgaard, Changjiang Du, Lucrezia Bertoletti, Marc Coulomb
b3a1f693246fd183.abstract:
14h - 14h25: Marius Kjaersgaard
Title: Local constancy of the Betti automorphic category over the moduli of curves
Abstract: Nadler and Yun have defined a relative notion of Betti automorphic sheaves and conjectured that they form a locally constant sheaf of categories over the moduli space of curves. We give a brief overview of the conjecture and work in progress, joint with Joakim Færgeman, towards proving the conjecture.
14h30 - 14h55: Changjiang Du
Title: Multivariable (phi,Gamma)-modules associated to p-adic Galois representations
Abstract: Let K be a finite unramified extension of Q_p. In a series of works by Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra, and Schraen, a multivariable coefficient ring A was constructed, together with two functors: D_A^{\otimes}, which sends mod p Galois representations to étale (phi,Gamma)-modules over A, and D_A, which sends admissible smooth mod p representations of GL_2(K) to étale (phi,O_K*)-modules over A. In this talk, we will explain how to construct the p-adic analogue of D_A^{\otimes}. This construction relies on two descent arguments: the pro-étale descent for perfectoid spaces and the Frobenius descent for phi-modules.
15h - 15h25: Lucrezia Bertoletti
Title: Finite length for unramified GL2: beyond multiplicity one.
Abstract: For K a finite unramified extension of Qp, a natural place to look for a conjectural mod p Langlands correspondence for GL2(K) are Hecke eigenspaces in the mod p cohomology of a tower of Shimura curves, which are expected to be a direct sum of copies of a representation (i.e. depending only on the input at p of the global setting) of GL2(K). The expected number of copies, called the multiplicity, should then be computed by counting Serre weights in the socle.
In the multiplicity one case, a recent work of Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra and Schraen establishes the finite length of the above Hecke eigenspaces, under mild genericity assumptions.
In this talk we will discuss how to extend this finite length result when the multiplicity one assumption is removed.
15h30 - 15h55: Marc Coulomb
Titre : Développement asymptotique explicite et matrices de Stokes des E-fonctions hypergéométriques.
Résumé : La famille des E-fonctions hypergéométriques généralise les fonctions de Bessel, de Kummer, et est liée à de nombreuses fonctions spéciales. Le résultat principal est une formule close, explicite, donnant le développement asymptotique de ces fonctions dans tout grand secteur angulaire autorisé. De cette formule découlent la sommation explicite de Borel-Laplace des fonctions hypergéométriques divergentes, ainsi que les matrices de Stokes associées.

b50629e2ea8e03dc.title: Une inégalité isopérimétrique quantitative dans l'espace
b50629e2ea8e03dc.speaker: Gisella Croce
b50629e2ea8e03dc.abstract:
Dans ce séminaire nous allons étudier un problème de stabilité pour l'inégalité isopérimétrique dans $\mathbb{R}^3$, faisant intervenir une asymétrie de type Hausdorff. Pour un corps convexe $F \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ de volume $4\pi/3$ (c'est-à-dire le volume de la boule unité dans l'espace), nous considérons la fonctionnelle \[ Q^*(F) := \frac{\delta(F)\log\bigl(\delta(F)+\delta(F)^{-1}\bigr)P(F)^3} {\lambda^*(F)^2}, \] o\`u $\delta(F)$ d\'esigne le déficit isop\'erim\'etrique, c'est-à-dire la différence entre le périmétre $P(F)$ et le périmètre de la boule unité, et $\displaystyle \lambda^*(F):=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^3} d_H(F,B+x)$
la distance de Hausdorff à la famille des boules unit\'es. Le facteur logarithmique reflète l'échelle capacitaire optimale au voisinage de la boule en dimension trois, tandis que le facteur $P(F)^3$ assure la coercivité. Notre résultat principal est l'existence du minimum de $Q^*$ dans la classe des corps convexes de volume $4\pi/3$.
Ce travail est en collaboration avec S. Bove et G. Pisante.

b535918fd371b710.title: A Cartan Geometry from a Correspondence Space in Riemannian Geometry
b535918fd371b710.speaker: Rodrigo MORÓN SANZ
b535918fd371b710.abstract: Cartan geometries are curved analogues of homogeneous spaces, and the correspondence space construction produces, from a Cartan geometry of one type, another of a different type over a larger base manifold. The unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is, in this language, a Cartan geometry of type (Euc(n), O(n-1)) obtained in this way; we study Cartan geometries of this type in general, whether or not they arise as correspondence spaces. We show that every such geometry induces on its base manifold an almost contact metric structure, together with an orthogonal splitting of the tangent bundle and a compatible linear connection; conversely, these data determine the geometry, so that the correspondence is a bijection. Moreover, we single out a distinguished Cartan connection, which we call normal, by a condition on its torsion formulated in terms of the Spencer differential. This normalization is dictated by the correspondence space construction: the Cartan connection induced on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is normal.
b535918fd371b710.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

b55a4e6cb646027e.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
b55a4e6cb646027e.speaker: Marc Burger
b55a4e6cb646027e.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

b5a6c6683d78c1da.title: Amal Omrani - Explicit Computation of Super-Hedging Prices and Strategies under Transaction Costs
b5a6c6683d78c1da.abstract: In markets with transaction costs, can super-hedging prices and strategies be explicitly characterized and computed directly from real market data, without relying on dual formulations? This talk presents a constructive approach based on conditional supports and dynamic programming, leading to explicit recursive formulas for super-hedging prices and strategies. The approach is illustrated using real market data.

b5c4e29174571cbe.title: Well-typed program generation, with prenex polymorphism
b5c4e29174571cbe.speaker: Gabriel Scherer
b5c4e29174571cbe.abstract:
Fuzzing” is a popular testing approach where we throw random inputs at a program and check that it respects some expected properties on all inputs. Fuzzing a metaprogram such as a compiler requires producing random input programs. To exercise interesting behaviors of the compiler, we want our input programs to be well-formed in a strong sense, in particular to be well-typed. Generating random well-typed program is difficult when the type-system is powerful, there is a whole scientific literature on the topic, see for example [Testing an Optimising Compiler by Generating Random Lambda Terms, Pałka, 2012].
Most existing generators integrate a large part of the implementation of a type-checker, “inverted” to assist in top-down random term generation by efficiently discarding choices that result in ill-typed programs. Scaling this approach to a full language would result in implementing two sophisticated type-checkers, once in the compiler and once in the program generator. This is one type-checker too many!
We present preliminary work on reusing the constraint-based type inference approach [The Essence of ML-based type inference, Pottier and Rémy, 2004] to write a single type-checker that can be used for both purposes: to check types of user-provided programs, and to efficiently guide a random program generator. This only requires a fairly simple modification to constraint generators: parametrizing them over a search monad. We have succesfully implemented a generator of simply-typed terms in this style, and are in the process (almost done) of scaling it to Hindley-Milner type inference.
(Relevant previous work is [Making Random Judgments: Automatically Generating Well-Typed Terms from the Definition of a Type-System, Fetscher, Claessen, Pałka, Hughes, Findler]. They start from Redex, a Racket DSL to implement simple type systems, and derive a random program generator. The limitation of this approach is that Redex only works with fairly simple type systems, in particular we do not expect it to scale to ML-style type inference with polymorphism, which is the part that hand-crafted generators also struggle on.)
Note: I gave a Formath talk on a preliminary version of this work in March 2024. At the time my prototype only supported the simply-typed lambda-calculus. The extension to Hindley-Milner is follow-up joint work with my 2025 intern Hugo Barreiro. I will also discuss optimizations to the search monad that are necessary to effectively generate terms of larger size.

b767edfc4e552ec3.title: F-CohFTs, their Givental group and tautological relations
b767edfc4e552ec3.speaker: Paolo Rossi
b767edfc4e552ec3.abstract: F-CohFTs are the natural generalization of cohomological field theories (CohFTs) when moving from the Deligne- Mumford compactification of the moduli space of stable curves given by nodal stable curves to the partial compactification given by curves with only separating nodes. They are natural under various viewpoints and were inspired by integrable systems considerations. As it happens for CohFTs, F-CohFTs can be used to probe the cohomology of this partial compactification, based on an analogue of the Givental-Teleman classification of semisimple CohFTs and similar nonsemisimple limiting techniques.

ba7528b34045622d.title: Séparer les composantes des variétés algébriques réelles par des invariants cohomologiques.
ba7528b34045622d.speaker: Samuel Lerbet
ba7528b34045622d.abstract: Si X est une variété algébrique complexe, il suit du théorème de comparaison de M. Artin que X et son lieu complexe X(C) ont le même nombre de composantes connexes, la première pour la topologie de Zariski, le second pour la topologie analytique ou forte. Au contraire, si X est une variété algébrique réelle connexe, son lieu réel X(R) est disconnexe pour la topologie forte en général. On peut néanmoins se demander si l'on peut séparer les composantes connexes de X(R) par des invariants algébriques de X. On peut pour cela utiliser des invariants de nature cohomologique : ainsi, E. Witt a montré que le signe des classes dans le groupe de Brauer d'une courbe algébrique réelle lisse séparent les composantes connexes de son lieu réel. La possibilité d'une telle séparation par un invariant cohomologique de degré donné dépend cependant de la relation entre ce dernier et la dimension : cela motive l'étude de l'optimalité de ce degré pour une dimension donnée. Le but de l'exposé est d'expliquer des résultats autour de cette question pour la séparation par la cohomologie et par son raffinement non ramifié et, si le temps le permet, des applications à la signature globale des formes quadratiques. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Olivier Benoist.

bd3fba0cb87bd7c8.title: Curve counting through intrinsic mirror symmetry
bd3fba0cb87bd7c8.speaker: Michel van Garrel
bd3fba0cb87bd7c8.abstract: According to Mirror Symmetry, the generating function of curve counting Gromov-Witten invariants of a Calabi-Yau threefold is conjectured to equal the integral over the positive real locus of a mirror-dual family of Calabi-Yau threefolds. In this joint work with Siebert, we prove that this conjecture holds as stated in the case of the canonical bundle of the projective plane with its mirror family constructed via the intrinsic mirror construction of Gross-Siebert. A key feature of the proof is that at no point do we calculate any invariants. Instead, we work with the punctured Gromov-Witten invariants that govern the intrinsic mirror construction.

bddfccf00e52b245.title: Torseurs sur la droite affine sous des groupes lisses
bddfccf00e52b245.speaker: Alexis Bouthier
bddfccf00e52b245.abstract:
Si G est réductif sur un corps, un théorème de Raghunathan-Ramanathan énonce que
tout G-torseur sur la droite affine, trivial sur la clôture séparable, est trivial.
Le cas non-réductif avait été écarté d'emblée par les auteurs comme "rather complicated".
On montre qu'un tel énoncé vaut pour tout k-groupe lisse (et même pas lisse du tout).
On discutera également d'autres extensions et généralisations à l'étude des G-torseurs sur des espaces affines.
Travail en commun K. Cesnavicius et F. Scavia.

beb708d5ed3076f7.title: Representation theory of quantum aﬃne algebras via tensor products of modules over hereditary algebras
beb708d5ed3076f7.speaker: Elie CASBI
beb708d5ed3076f7.abstract:
We introduce new families of monoidal structures suited to categorifying important invariants arising in the representation theory of quantum affine algebras and in the theory of cluster algebras. Our framework builds on Auslander--Reiten theory and higher homological algebra; namely, for each finite acyclic quiver QQQ, we construct a monoidal category RQ\mathcal{R}_QRQ​ whose indecomposable objects are tensor products of modules over the path algebra of QQQ. We show that to each indecomposable object XXX in RQ\mathcal{R}_QRQ​ corresponds a (unique up to homotopy) chain complex C∙(X)C_{\bullet}(X)C∙​(X) satisfying remarkable homological properties. These complexes are constructed using some iterated mapping cone procedure, which yields a collection of distinguished triangles in the bounded homotopy category of RQ\mathcal{R}_QRQ​. We then prove that in the case where QQQ is a Dynkin quiver, the Euler characteristics of (the image under a suitable functor of) C∙(X)C_{\bullet}(X)C∙​(X) can be identified with the (truncated) qqq-character of a standard module over the quantum affine algebra Uq(gQ^)U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}_Q})Uq​(gQ​​). We also show that the above mentioned distinguished triangles categorify certain exchange relations in the finite type cluster algebra AQ\mathcal{A}_QAQ​. If time allows, we will discuss perspectives towards monoidal categorifications of more general cluster structures.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.
beb708d5ed3076f7.organizer: J. Alev, D. Hernandez, B. Keller, Th. Levasseur, et S. Morier-Genoud.

becf056d0121d7e5.title: Can you compute the operator norm in group C*-algebras?
becf056d0121d7e5.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
becf056d0121d7e5.abstract:
A paper by Fritz, Netzer, and Thom from 2012, titled "Can you compute the operator norm?", in essence initiated the computable structure theory for C*-algebras. The primary question involved is: given some "standard" presentation of a C*-algebra, is there an algorithm for computing the norm on the algebra? In this talk, I will focus on the case of C*-algebras arising from groups. In fact, most of the talk will focus on the case of the following four group C*-algebras: C^*(F_2), C^*(F_2\times F_2), C^*_r(F_2), C^*_r(F_2\times F_2). Here, for a group G, C^*(G) and C^*_r(G) denote the universal and reduced group C*-algebras associated to G, and F_2 denotes the free group on two generators. The answers to the question about computability of the norm for these four group C*-algebras turn out to be: yes, no, yes, and yes. The first is a result of FNT, the second a result due to myself and Thomas Sinclair from a year ago (answering a question of FN,T using recent results from quantum complexity theory), and the third and fourth recent results of mine (answering a question of Sinclair). Time permitting, I will discuss a potential generation of the latter results to wider classes of groups.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

c02b8c5019c87888.title: Limit of archimedean heights and Ceresa cycles
c02b8c5019c87888.speaker: Souvik Goswami
c02b8c5019c87888.speaker_affiliation: IISER - Indian Institute of Science Education and Research
c02b8c5019c87888.abstract: For a smooth, projective and complex variety $X$, and a pair of algebraic cycles $Z$ and $W$ that are homologous to zero and are in complementary codimensions, the archimedean height pairing is a real number that can be interpreted as a secondary intersection pairing that measures how far a certain cohomology group of the pair $(X\setminus |Z|, |W|)$ is from being real split. This interpretation makes it suitable for variational study: Let $\Delta := \{t\in \mathbb{C};\,|t|<1\}$, and $\Delta^{\ast}=\Delta\setminus \{0\}$. Given a family $\{X_t\}_{t\in \Delta}$ of projective and complex varieties that are smooth for $t\in \Delta^{\ast}$, while $X_0$ is a simple normal crossing divisor, and a family $\{Z_t, W_t\}_{t\in \Delta^{\ast}}$ of algebraic cycles in complementary codimensions that are homologous to zero, the function $h := \Delta^{\ast}\to\mathbb{R}$, with $h(t)$ being the archimedean height pairing of the pair $(Z_t, W_t)$, is smooth. But $h$ does not extend to $t=0$. R.~Hain, G.~Pearlstein, P.~Brosnan et al. have shown that the asymptotic function $\widetilde h(t)= h(t)+\mu \log|t|$ extends continuously to $t=0$, where $\mu\in\mathbb{Q}$ depends on the monodromy of the variation of mixed Hodge structures associated with these pairings. Fixing a parameter $t$, one can ask if $\widetilde h(0)$ is given by the archimedean height pairing of algebraic cycles associated with the central fiber $X_{0}$. In a joint work with Dr. Irene Spelta, I have shown that this question has an affirmative answer in case of height pairings of Ceresa cycles (arxiv.org/abs/2604.01842). The purpose of this talk will be to explore this result and some interesting questions that still remains unanswered.

c08df0626f41e567.title: Combinations of Non-Archimedean Discrete Groups
c08df0626f41e567.speaker: Konstantinos Tsouvalas
c08df0626f41e567.abstract: Chatterji and Venkataramana, motivated by Nori's problem, asked for a real algebraic semisimple Lie group G and a simple Lie subgroup H of G, whether a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup of G, intersecting H in a lattice, is itself a lattice in G. After discussing what is known related to this question and Nori's problem, we will address a similar version of this question for the k-points of semisimple groups defined over a non-Archimedean local field k, and provide examples for which a positive answer fails. This is based on a combination theorem for discrete subgroups of matrix groups over discretely valued fields. We will also discuss a construction of non-Fuchsian hyperbolic groups that quasi-isometrically embed as subgroups of matrix groups over a discretely valued field.

c1f9ef6befcf4e98.title: An affirmative solution to the generalized Busemann-Petty problem with subspaces dimensions 2 and 3
c1f9ef6befcf4e98.speaker: Cheng Lin
c1f9ef6befcf4e98.abstract: The generalized Busemann--Petty problem asks whether two origin-symmetric convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ having larger volume of all $m$-dimensional sections necessarily have larger volume. When $m\geq 4$, this is known to be false, but the cases $m=2, 3$ for $n\geq 5$ have remained open since the 1990s. In this work, we resolve these cases. Together with the known results, the generalized Busemann--Petty problem is completely solved: the answer is affirmative for $m=1, 2, 3$, and negative for $m\geq 4$. This talk is based on the joint work with Yu-de LIU and Ge XIONG.

c364de33b1bcf9f9.speaker: Robin Zhang
c364de33b1bcf9f9.abstract:

c4864fa17f638a07.title: Zeta values as moments: A random matrix theory
c4864fa17f638a07.speaker: Hartmut Monien
c4864fa17f638a07.abstract: Values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be obtained as moments of a certain probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in representation theory of the symmetric group.

c511733100dec7a5.title: A Two-Scale System and Ambient Constructions
c511733100dec7a5.speaker: Mikhail MARKOV
c511733100dec7a5.abstract: Geometric structures can often be understood by realising them in a higher-dimensional space. The Fefferman–Graham ambient construction in conformal geometry and the Eisenhart–Duval lift in nonrelativistic mechanics are two examples of this idea. In this talk, I will describe a common framework for these constructions based on a conformal metric and two scales satisfying the almost-Einstein equation. Besides bringing familiar constructions into a common setting, this approach leads to an ambient description of the spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. I will discuss the geometry behind this description and explain how conformal compactification also brings null infinity into the picture.

c5e5cda85abd7fa5.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
c5e5cda85abd7fa5.speaker: Sergei Nechaev
c5e5cda85abd7fa5.abstract: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual tread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, they observed a logarithmic increase in the transverse span, D, of a thread with its length, N. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is an intermediate one, and sufficiently long threads exhibit topological localization, where span D approaches a finite limit at N >> 1. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints, giving rise to topological microphase separation. We study braids within a locally free approximation and confirm the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group LF_n which approximates the braid group B_{n+1}. We conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, n ~ 3 -- 5, the span, D, grows algebraically with N (N>>1), as D ~ N^{1/4}. By contrast, for large n, each thread in a long braid asymptotically localizes, approaching D ~ const.
c5e5cda85abd7fa5.organizer: Ilia Gaiur, Vasily Golyshev, Vladimir Rubtsov

c699519255a59a3d.title: Combinatoire des mots, combinatoire énumérative et combinatoire algébrique autour de la forme normale alternante des tresses
c699519255a59a3d.speaker: June Roupin
c699519255a59a3d.abstract:
Les tresses sont des objets topologiques qui possèdent de très bonnes propriétés combinatoires, et peuvent en particulier être représentées et étudiées comme des classes d’équivalence de mots sur l'alphabet des transpositions. Un concept naturel dans ce contexte est la notion de forme normale : le choix d’un représentant unique pour chaque tresse. La forme normale alternante, dont l’étude a initialement été motivée par ses liens avec l’ordre standard des tresses, associe à chaque tresse sur n fils une séquence unique de tresses sur n-1 fils, appelés des blocs, permettant de définir récursivement un unique représentant.
Dans cet exposé, je vais présenter quelques propriétés combinatoires et algébriques importante de la forme normale alternante, notamment la régularité et l'automaticité du langage associé. Je vais ensuite aborder plusieurs applications de ces résultats couvrant divers domaines de combinatoires : énumération des tresses ; bon ordre totale sur le monoïde de tresse ; généralisations aux monoïdes d'Artin-Tits.

c9e0f6e753a79da8.title: Gelfand-Kirillov dimensions and the p-adic Langlands program
c9e0f6e753a79da8.speaker: Reinier SORGDRAGER
c9e0f6e753a79da8.abstract:
This thesis' main results are upper bounds to the Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of certain p-adic representations and some applications of such bounds.
The Gelfand-Kirillov dimension is a generalization of the Krull dimension of modules ovef commutative rings to modules over completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups -- also known as Iwasawa algebras. These Iwasawa algebras act on the duals of p-adic Banach representations or smooth mod p representations of such groups.
The main result is, for p>2 a prime number, that an admissible p-adic Banach representation of GL_2 of a p-adic field K has Gelfand-Kirillov dimension at most the degree [K:Q_p] as soon as its locally analytic vectors admit an infinitesimal character.
The second main result is a generalization of this statement to families of Banach representations with infinitesimal characters in families in the sense of Dospinescu-Paškūnas-Schraen. This result yields a generalization of the GK-bound of Breuil-Herzig-Hu-Morra-Schraen beyond K unramified for the smooth mod p representation given by a Galois isotypic component in the mod p cohomology of Shimura varieties.
The method of proof for both results is much in the spirit of the filtrations of fixed ``radius of analyticity'' of Schneider-Teitelbaum on the duals of the representations and the study of their associated gradeds. The second main result required a generalization of these filtrations to double radii.
Finally, this thesis has two more results. The most important one being that (in the setting of K unramified, only needing the results of Breuil-Herzig-Hu-Morra-Schraen) the GK-bound for mod p cohomology of Shimura varieties allows one, via miracle flatness of the patched module over R_\infty, to compute the derived pro-p Iwahori invariants of the mod p representation as complex over the non-derived pro-p Iwahori Hecke algebra, up to quasi-isomorphism. This derived module turns out to depend only on the mod p Galois representation (and a multiplicity) and not on the global choices that go into the construction of the smooth mod p representation of GL_2.

ca840c48a45a8c70.title: Grid Minors in planar graphs
ca840c48a45a8c70.speaker: Eileen Robinson
ca840c48a45a8c70.abstract:
In 1984, Robertson and Seymour showed that the treewidth of a planar graph with no t × t grid as minor is bounded by a function g(t). Together with Thomas, they later proved that g(t) can be taken to be linear. The current best known bound, due to Gu and Tamaki (2012), is g(t) ≤ 9/2 t − 11/2. In this talk, I will show an improved bound of g(t) ≤ 4t + O(1), which is within a factor 2 of optimal.
This talk is based on joint work with Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Quentin Claus, Gwenaël Joret, Robin Petit and Jean-Florent Raymond.

cd93bd9dd7a3b7b1.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette : « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
cd93bd9dd7a3b7b1.abstract:
Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle.
Cette conférence gratuite, sera suivie d’une discussion informelle autour d’un verre de l’amitié

cf8ea3f8eb51a096.speaker: Kevin Kwan
cf8ea3f8eb51a096.abstract: There is no universally agreed definition of special functions, but they are generally viewed as the useful functions that arise frequently and naturally in mathematics and broader sciences, with numerous tabulated identities that help solve practical problems. Efforts to bring structure to this seemingly chaotic world have varied in scope and success. In this talk, based on joint work with Akshay Venkatesh and Griffin Wang, I will discuss yet another (partial) attempt that brings geometry and arithmetic of algebraic groups into the study of special functions.

d29de5a33174494b.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
d29de5a33174494b.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
d29de5a33174494b.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.

d580d28367a23858.title: Dynamics of singularity surfaces for the compressible viscous fluids.
d580d28367a23858.speaker: Marcel Zodji
d580d28367a23858.speaker_affiliation: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry
d580d28367a23858.abstract:
The motion of a compressible viscous fluid is described by the Navier-Stokes system.
It is a system of hyperbolic-parabolic mixed-type PDEs. In this talk, we will study
the so-called density patch problem: \emph{If we are given a density that is initially "regular"
on both sides of a hypersurface across which it is discontinuous, will this structure
be preserved over time?}
An important quantity in the mathematical analysis of this system is the so-called effective flux,
which was discovered by Hoff and Smoller (1985). More precisely, the mathematical properties
of this quantity play a crucial role in the study of the propagation of oscillations in
compressible fluids [Serre, 1991], in the construction of weak solutions [P-L Lions, 1996] or the
propagation of discontinuity surfaces [Hoff, 2002], to cite just a few examples.
In the case of density-dependent viscosities, the behavior of the effective flux degenerates,
which renders the analysis more subtle.

d6abdef27a847498.title: Élise Devey - A Frank–Wolfe-Type Algorithm for High-Dimensional Stochastic Control Problems with Non-Exchangeable Agents
d6abdef27a847498.abstract: Abstract : This paper presents a Frank--Wolfe type algorithm for computing approximately optimal distributed stochastic controls in a large population of $N$ agents cooperating to minimize a convex cost functional. The cost includes a heterogeneous pairwise interaction term between the agents' controls, which rules out a direct treatment by the classical Mean Field Control framework. Working directly at finite $N$ rather than through a mean-field limit, we prove that the distributed controls returned by our algorithm are $N^{-1/2}$-optimal for the original problem, with an explicit rate in the number of iterations $K$ and in a measure of interaction heterogeneity, $\Delta_{\mathrm{spread}}$, that we introduce. The algorithm avoids the curse of dimensionality: at each iteration, the coupled $N$-agent problem is linearized and decomposed into $N$ independent, low-dimensional subproblems. We illustrate the approach on a linear-quadratic benchmark, for which we derive a closed-form Riccati-type characterization of the optimal control, and validate the predicted convergence rate numerically. Interaction structures of this heterogeneous, pairwise-penalized type arise naturally in applications such as electricity grid flexibility management, where local storage units are coupled through shared transmission-line capacity constraints.

d81014a2a5bc192e.title: Extended regulators of flat bundles on quasiprojective varieties
d81014a2a5bc192e.speaker: Carlos Simpson
d81014a2a5bc192e.abstract: This is joint work with Jaya Iyer. We recall that to a flat bundle one can associate the regulator or secondary Chern class invariants in $H^{2p−1}(X, \mathbb{C}\backslash\mathbb{Z})$. Reznikov showed that if $X$ is a smooth projective variety then these invariants are torsion. Following suggestions of Deligne, given a flat bundle over a quasiprojective variety $X=\overline{X}\backslash D$ with unipotent monodromy around the snc divisor $D$, we define secondary Chern classes in $H^{2p−1}(X, \mathbb{C}\backslash\mathbb{Z})$ using patched connections whose curvature forms are nilpotent. We follow Reznikov’s strategy to show that these invariants are torsion, using Mochizuki’s theorem on deformation to a VHS. This requires defining the extended patched classes in K-theory. It follows that the Deligne Chern classes of the Deligne canonical extended bundle on $X$ are torsion

d92642e141c04a00.title: Geometric group theory and 19th century moduli spaces
d92642e141c04a00.speaker: Alex Wright
d92642e141c04a00.abstract: Moduli spaces of smooth complex algebraic curves have been intensively studied since the 19th century from many points of view. Their fundamental groups, being mapping class groups, are among the best understood groups in mathematics. In this talk I will give a historical overview of the geometric study of these groups, and explain how new work with Daniel Allcock (arxiv.org/abs/2609.14416) extends much of this geometric understanding to the fundamental group of another 19th century moduli space, namely the moduli space of smooth complex cubic surfaces. The proof also applies to some other moduli spaces, and gives many new corollaries. Most of the talk will be devoted to motivation and background (some from the "What is..." article https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15410), and connections to different areas of mathematics will be highlighted.

d9a234bed29da1d4.title: Gravitational Sommerfeld Effects: Framework and Applications
d9a234bed29da1d4.speaker: Chia-Hsien Shen
d9a234bed29da1d4.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
Sommerfeld effects describe long-distance corrections to radiation emitted by a short-distance source. They play an important role in atomic physics and dark matter phenomenology, but the same mechanism also arises in gravitational-wave radiation from compact binaries. In this talk, I will develop a systematic framework for gravitational Sommerfeld effects by combining worldline effective field theory with black hole perturbation theory. A key advantage of this framework is that it organizes high-order perturbative calculations without requiring any nontrivial loop integration, allowing us to compute the waveform to tenth order in the perturbative expansion and beyond. The formulation also reveals an exact connection between the radiation waveform and Compton scattering, as well as the underlying structures of the classical renormalization group of the multipoles and tidal Love numbers. I will conclude by discussing how these results can be incorporated into waveform resummation models for gravitational-wave signals. This talk is based on arXiv:2604.14112 with Chih-Hao Chang and Zihan Zhou, and work in progress.

d9bcf76e37ae75a2.abstract: Recently, there has been a surge in new results on the digital properties of numbers. In this talk, we discuss some recent results on palindromes, numbers which are the same backwards and forwards (e.g. 12321 or 7887) in a fixed base. Despite being elementary objects of study, in order to prove deep results about their multiplicative properties we need to turn to powerful estimates on exponential sums. For this talk, we focus particularly on a recent result of Bryce Kerr and myself, establishing the infinitude of square-free palindromes.

da1ea5e189434a8a.title: Biased random walk on dynamical percolation
da1ea5e189434a8a.speaker: Nina Gantert
da1ea5e189434a8a.abstract:
As an example for a random walk in random environment, we
study biased random walk for dynamical percolation on the
d-dimensional lattice. We establish a law
of large numbers and an invariance principle for this random walk
using regeneration times.
Moreover, we verify that the Einstein relation holds, and we
investigate the speed of the walk
as a function of the bias. While for d = 1 the speed is
increasing, we show that in general this
fails in dimension d ? 2. As our main result, we establish two
regimes of parameters, separated
by a critical curve, such that the speed is either eventually
strictly increasing or eventually
strictly decreasing. This is in sharp contrast to the biased
random walk on a static supercritical
percolation cluster, where the speed is known to be eventually
zero.
Based on joint work with Sebastian Andres, Dominik Schmid and
Perla Sousi.

db81df2932aa5612.title: From Inference to Generative Diffusion: How Deep Networks Uncover Structure in Hierarchical Data
db81df2932aa5612.abstract:
Our understanding of how neural networks learn from structured data is caught between two extremes: theory largely relies on high-dimensional random data, which lacks any structure, while experiments rely on real-world benchmarks, whose structure is not understood. This talk takes the middle road and works with a synthetic data model that is simple enough to be controlled yet rich enough to be informative. Sequences are generated by a branching process on a tree, so that elements inherit nested correlations across all scales, in a manner reminiscent of language or images, while the Bayes-optimal predictor remains known exactly. This provides a ground truth against which trained models can be compared, both in what they learn and in what they produce. In a first part, we ask how the structure is learned. Using a filtering procedure that controls the range of correlations, we show that transformers recover the exact inference algorithm, incorporating larger scales sequentially, in time during training and in space across attention layers. In a second part, we ask whether the structure, once learned, can be reproduced. Turning to diffusion models, we identify a phase of biased generalization, during which the test loss keeps decreasing while generated samples drift anomalously close to the training data. We quantify this bias by comparing networks trained on disjoint datasets, demonstrate its presence on real images, and use the exact scores available on tree-based data to characterize its onset. The mechanism is again sequential: coarse structure is learned early and independently of the specific data, while finer features are resolved later in a way that increasingly depends on individual training samples. As a consequence, early stopping at the test loss minimum may be insufficient for privacy-critical applications.

e178d237c13550d8.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
e178d237c13550d8.speaker: Marc Burger
e178d237c13550d8.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

e28a3c9bc79c944f.abstract:
Combinatorics and Arithmetic for Physics
The meeting’s focus is about questions of discrete mathematics and number theory with an emphasis on computability. Problems are drawn mainly from theoretical physics : renormalisation, combinatorial physics, geometry, evolution equations (commutative and noncommutative) or related to their models. Computations, based on combinatorial structures (graphs,trees, words, automata, semirings, bases) or classical structures (operators, Hopf algebras, evolution equations, special functions, categories) are good candidates for computer-based implementation and experimentation.

e62e71dd0d24aaaf.title: On the Wilson-Fisher Fixed Point in the Limit of Integer Spacetime Dimensions
e62e71dd0d24aaaf.speaker: Bernardo Zan
e62e71dd0d24aaaf.abstract:
The Wilson–Fisher (WF) fixed point, a scalar field theory with a quartic interaction in $d = 4 - \epsilon$ dimensions, is the textbook example of a weakly coupled CFT. The epsilon expansion accurately reproduces the critical exponents of the $d = 3$ and the $d = 2$ Ising model. This has led to the common view that WF defines a continuous family of CFTs in non-integer dimensions, interpolating between the free theory at $d=4$ and the Ising model at $d = 3$ and $d = 2$. In this talk I will look at what happens to the WF CFT when the number of dimensions approaches an integer value. Identifying the $d\to 2$ limit of WF as the $2d$ Ising CFT raises some issues, related to the fact that the $d=2$ CFT has infinitely many conserved currents that the $d>2$ theory does not have. I will propose a scenario, inspired by some exactly solved two-dimensional models, where the $d\to 2$ limit of WF contains the $d=2$ Ising CFT as a subsector, but contains more operators which do not completely decouple from the Ising subsector. I will explain why this makes the task of obtaining a $d= 2 + \epsilon$ expansion for the Ising model harder.

e7d50b8c5e8d381a.title: Homogenized Transformers
e7d50b8c5e8d381a.speaker: Hugo Koubbi
e7d50b8c5e8d381a.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: We study a random model of deep multi-head self-attention in which the weights are resampled independently across layers and heads, as at initialization of training. Viewing depth as a time variable, the residual stream defines a discrete-time interacting particle system on the unit sphere. We prove that, under suitable joint scalings of the depth, the residual step size, and the number of heads, this dynamics admits a nontrivial homogenized limit.Depending on the scaling, the limit is either deterministic or stochastic with common noise; in the mean-field regime, the latter leads to a stochastic nonlinear Fokker–Planck equation for the conditional law of a representative token. In the Gaussian setting, the limiting drift vanishes, making the homogenized dynamics explicit enough to study representation collapse. This yields quantitative trade-offs between dimension, context length, and temperature, and identifies regimes in which clustering can be mitigated.

e7dd149d1fe44b9a.title: The Stratified Shape
e7dd149d1fe44b9a.speaker: Marco Volpe
e7dd149d1fe44b9a.abstract:
In this talk, I will try to address the question of how to do algebraic topology with stratified spaces and schemes in a meaningful way. I will begin by recalling and motivating some of the main historical attempts to approach this question, both in topology and in algebraic geometry, passing through the work of Nash, Quinn, Siebenmann, Edwards–Hastings, Deligne, and, more recently, Lurie and Barwick–Glasman–Haine. I will then propose my own answer, based on a construction I call the stratified shape.
Time permitting, I will discuss some applications of the stratified shape to proper homotopy theory (joint with Georg Lehner), homology manifolds (joint with Markus Land), and a generalization of Lurie's exodromy equivalence (joint with Peter Haine and Guglielmo Nocera).

e93d9ae563910eea.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
e93d9ae563910eea.speaker: Emma Weschler
e93d9ae563910eea.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

eab425cd42dc1e8f.title: AI for Math: From Group Theory to Discrete Holography
eab425cd42dc1e8f.speaker: Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk
eab425cd42dc1e8f.abstract: I will describe how one can use modern machine learning methods to attack open problems in group theory. I will show how ideas from AI, pure math, integrability, string theory and quantum information meet here in a highly productive way. I will focus on much-studied Cayley graphs of permutation groups, which are often very hard to explore due to their enormous size. I will describe how a modern ML approach overcomes this challenge and provides efficient pathfinding on these huge graphs. The outcome is a large set of new results and conjectures that in particular sharpen famous bounds on the diameters of these graphs. These results also hint at the existence of a novel, discrete string-like duality for this setting. It provides a realisation of the paradigm "complexity = volume" from AdS/CFT holography, and may potentially be applicable to a wider range of AI tasks. Lastly I will outline some new results for combinatorics of quantum periods and how this could help in improving these ML approaches. Based on arXiv:2509.19162, 2603.22195 and work to appear. Our code is publicly available as the CayleyPy library.

ead7e14f1ce2d23b.title: How to Encode World Knowledge?
ead7e14f1ce2d23b.speaker: Guy Gilboa
ead7e14f1ce2d23b.abstract:
Foundation models are a key platform which implicitly encodes world knowledge. In this talk we first focus on vision-language models, such as CLIP, and investigate their geometric behavior and logic behind the high-dimensional feature encoding. For instance, we find that as image or text become more rare and distinct they are encoded further from the center of the embedding. We explain why InfoNCE loss leads to that behavior. We also find out empirically that each modality can be well modeled statistically as admitting a multivariate Gaussian distribution. This finding is then proved formally, where we show InfoNCE asymptotically induces Gaussian statistics. Finally, we connect two major image foundation models – encoders and generators, through a universal normal embedding hypothesis. A surprising consequence of this hypothesis is demonstrated, where generative diffusion « noise » contains semantic data which can be accessed by linear probing for either classification or editing. This talk is based on 6 recent papers in the group published at ICML 2025, ICLR 2026 and CVPR 2026.

ed8633e232e3c95b.title: Good complexifications of nonnegatively curved manifolds
ed8633e232e3c95b.speaker: Ethan Peng
ed8633e232e3c95b.abstract: A closed manifold M admits a good complexification if it is diffeomorphic to the set of real points of a real affine variety X such that the embedding X(R) -> X(C) is a homotopy equivalence. We will give examples of such closed manifolds, including classical ones (spheres, RP2, homogeneous spaces, Cheeger manifolds), as well as a class of closed Riemannian manifolds with non-negative sectional curvature constructed by B. Totaro using plumbing techniques. We will also discuss topological constraints on closed manifolds admitting a good complexification, such as the classical non-negativity of its Euler characteristic, and vanishing of some Betti numbers and Pontryagin numbers as proved by Totaro. An effort will be made to explain how the curvature constraints interplay with the algebro-geometric aspects. If time permits, we will also discuss how good complexifications pass to quotients by nice group actions, giving ways to "algebraicize" various familiar manifolds.

eef32bcaae0bd0d8.title: "Quantum'' rational numbers, q-deformed Coxeter friezes, and the cross-ratio
eef32bcaae0bd0d8.speaker: Valentin OVSIENKO
eef32bcaae0bd0d8.abstract:
The classical cross-ratio ``crosses'' both classical and modern mathematics, linking geometry with combinatorics, dynamics, and mathematical physics. It provides natural coordinates on many moduli spaces. In this talk, I will introduce a new q-deformed, or ``quantum'' cross-ratio: a PSL(2,Z)-invariant of ordered quadruples of distinct points on the rational projective line. The construction is based on the theory of q-deformed rational numbers developed jointly with Sophie Morier-Genoud. I will discuss several properties of this new invariant, with its close connection to q-deformed Coxeter frieze patterns taking centre stage.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.
eef32bcaae0bd0d8.organizer: J. Alev, D. Hernandez, B. Keller, Th. Levasseur, et S. Morier-Genoud.

eef507ba4813d3bf.title: Murphy’s law in non-abelian Hodge theory
eef507ba4813d3bf.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
eef507ba4813d3bf.abstract: We discuss explicit examples of non-integral variations of Q-Hodge structures. Our approach leverages Fenchel–Nielsen-type parameterizations, due to Kabaya and Maskit, of the Teichmüller component of relative character varieties. Additionally, we discuss various Diophantine results concerning the OK,S -integral points of such character varieties, and give a new proof of Beauville’s classical theorem on families of elliptic curves. If time permits, pathological behaviors of the Hodge locus of non-integral QVHS will also be presented.

ef67103dfc4fc979.title: Ondes internes et viscosité
ef67103dfc4fc979.speaker: Malo Jézéquel
ef67103dfc4fc979.abstract: Je discuterai dans cet exposé du phénomène de concentration géométrique des ondes internes en présence de viscosité. Après avoir présenté un peu de contexte, j'expliquerai comment on peut étudier le régime de basse viscosité en remplaçant le domaine sur lequel le problème est originellement posé (un domaine borné de R2) par une autre surface dans C2. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Jian Wang.

f034597a0e4253b5.title: Weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field
f034597a0e4253b5.speaker: Michael Maex
f034597a0e4253b5.abstract:
The theory of weight functions by Mustaţă-Nicaise on Berkovich spaces hints at an intrinsic approach to studying skeleta without the limitations of the usual tools from algebraic geometry, i.e., semistable reduction or resolution of singularities. In this talk we discuss how Mustaţă-Nicaise's construction can be generalised to define weight functions intrinsically on any quasi-smooth Berkovich space as a sort of normalised log-discrepancy of a canonical form.
Next, we turn our attention to computing weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field K. This question reduces to the entirely value-theoretic problem of describing the integral log differentials $\Omega^{\log}_{L^\circ / K^\circ}$ for a simple extension of real valued fields $L / K$ , which we describe using the data in MacLane-Vaquié chains.
We find that on the affine line, weight functions are completely determined by the integral piecewise linear (Z-PL) structure the affine line and vice versa, yielding new insight into the Z-PL structure.
Finally, we discuss how this can be used to define and compute the essential skeleton of certain Berkovich spaces.

f1541130f606c978.title: Exact curve counting on the once-punctured torus
f1541130f606c978.speaker: Mingkun Liu
f1541130f606c978.abstract: Two closed curves on a surface are said to have the same topological type if they lie in the same mapping class group orbit. Mirzakhani first showed that, on a hyperbolic surface, the number of closed geodesics of a given topological type of length at most L is asymptotically proportional to L^{6g-6}. In this talk, we will focus on the case of the once-punctured torus. Rather than using hyperbolic length, we will count curves according to their word length. In this setting, it turns out that exact counting formulas can be obtained. This is joint work with Filippo Baroni and David Fisac.

f4e64a7a842867c4.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
f4e64a7a842867c4.speaker: Maxime Marivain
f4e64a7a842867c4.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

f50fc35646665436.title: On the undefinability of C*-tensor norms
f50fc35646665436.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
f50fc35646665436.abstract:
Both the minimal and maximal tensor product norms on a pair of C*-algebras are defined in an "extrinsic" way in terms of representations of the C*-algebras involved. One might wonder if there could be an intrinsic definition of these norm. For example, one might wonder if either the minimal or maximal tensor norm on a sum of simple tensors could be calculated by some sort of formula using norms of *-polynomials of the elements appearing in the simple tensors. In this talk, I explain how to use model theory to formulate a precise version of this latter question. We then discuss two variants of the question: the global version (where such a formula should hold for all C*-algebras, perhaps relative to some elementary class) and, time permitting, the local version (where such a formula should hold only for the pair of C*-algebras involved). I will explain that the answer to the global questions for both the maximal and minimal tensor product norms is negative in general, while in the local case, we give some examples where the answer is negative. The latter examples use the quantum complexity results MIP*=RE and MIP^co=coRE. The work presented in this talk is joint with Thomas Sinclair.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

f564968cf9d1737e.title: Positivité et sommes de carrés
f564968cf9d1737e.abstract: En 1927, Artin résout le 17ème problème de Hilbert en montrant que tout polynôme réel qui ne prend que des valeurs positives est une somme de carrés de fractions rationnelles. Mais combien de carrés sont nécessaires ? Cette question quantitative sera le fil conducteur de l’exposé. Je l’aborderai dans le cadre classique des polynômes réels, ainsi que dans des variantes arithmétiques et analytiques, en présentant quelques problèmes ouverts et des développements récents.

f72c8d5c1e41a7b4.title: Depicting instabilities in linear, dispersive PDEs: a dynamical systems approach
f72c8d5c1e41a7b4.speaker: Maria Teresa Rotolo
f72c8d5c1e41a7b4.abstract:
We consider linear, time-dependent perturbations of periodic transport equations on tori of arbitrary dimension. We identify a class of perturbations that admit a large set of unstable solutions: to detect such behavior, we prove that their positive Sobolev norms grow exponentially fast in time. Moreover, we prove that this class of perturbations is generic in dimension two.
The proof relies on a normal form procedure combined with the study of dynamical properties of Morse-Smale transport systems.
In this talk, after a general introduction to the topic, we describe the result and ideas of the proof, focusing on the interplay between pseudodifferential theory and hyperbolic dynamics. This is a joint work with Gabriel Rivière.

f995fffb74480dc2.title: Kneser Graphs: Variations on a Theme
f995fffb74480dc2.speaker: Matej Stehlik
f995fffb74480dc2.abstract:
Kneser graphs are a classical family of graphs that play a central role in graph colouring. In 1978, Lovasz determined their chromatic number using topological methods. Schrijver later strengthened this result by identifying vertex-critical induced subgraphs of Kneser graphs, now known as Schrijver graphs.
The talk will survey several recent developments involving these graph families, including constructions of edge-critical subgraphs of Schrijver graphs, a common generalisation of Kneser and Schrijver graphs, and a new family of vertex-critical graphs for which the standard topological lower bounds on the chromatic number are not tight.
The talk is based on joint work with Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, and Tomas Kaiser.

f9a8885d047de507.title: Algebraic Hodge-Generic Points and the Period Conjecture
f9a8885d047de507.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
f9a8885d047de507.abstract: Let f:X\to S be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over Qbar. We prove that the points of S(Qbar) that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to f are analytically dense in S. More generally, motivated by the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large-monodromy assumption, we establish the density of algebraic points at which the periods of the fibre satisfy no unexpected relations of degree at most delta. The main technical input is a new result on relations among solutions of G-operators, based on height estimates of Bombieri and André. This is a joint work with Gal Binyamini and David Urbanik.

rec.title: Defects in skein theory
rec.speaker: Juan Ramón Gómez García
rec.abstract:
Skein theory forms a once-extended categorified TQFT that assigns skein algebras to surfaces and skein modules to 3-manifolds.
These algebras and modules are defined in terms of generators of topological flavor, namely a certain class of graphs embedded in the 3-manifold,
modulo the relations induced by evaluating (locally) these graphs in an underlying ribbon category. In this talk I will explain how this picture
can be extended to stratified manifolds with strata of codimension 1 and 2 (called defects). Using the appropriate algebraic structures,
we can define evaluation functors around defects, yielding notions of stratified skein modules and algebras. Examples of these structures
are provided by the formalism of parabolic restriction. As an application, we use an interpolating version of parabolic defects to construct
a categorification of the Turaev coproduct in the HOMFLY skein algebra.
rec.series_name: Séminaire de Géométrie et Dynamique de Cergy-Pontoise

rec.title: 2-catégories de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes et invariants quantiques homotopiques
rec.speaker: Matthew Cellot
rec.abstract:
À la fin du XXe siècle, les travaux remarquables de Jones, Drinfeld,
Witten et Kontsevich ont permis la construction de nouveaux invariants de
variétés, appelés invariants quantiques, obtenus notamment à partir de certains
groupes quantiques. L’un des premiers succès dans cette direction est l’invariant
de Turaev-Viro-Barrett-Westbury des 3-variétés, défini comme une somme d’états
à partir de la donnée d’une catégorie de fusion. Plus récemment, Douglas et
Reutter ont construit des invariants de 4-variétés par somme d’états, en utilisant
des 2-catégories de fusion.
Cet exposé porte sur les invariants quantiques homotopiques, c’est-à-dire les
invariants quantiques de variétés munies d’une structure supplémentaire codée
par une application vers un espace topologique. Plus précisément, nous
généralisons la construction de Douglas-Reutter pour obtenir des invariants des
3-fibrés plats sur les 4-variétés ou, de manière équivalente, des 4-variétés
munies d’une classe d’homotopie d’applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie.
Les structures algébriques utiles pour cette construction sont les 2-catégories
de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes, où le 3-groupe modélise le 3-type
d’homotopie. Dans ce cadre, les applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie sont
codées par des triangulations coloriées. En démontrant une généralisation
coloriée du théorème de Pachner, nous obtenons que ces invariants sont
indépendants de la triangulation choisie.
rec.series_name: Séminaire de Géométrie et Dynamique de Cergy-Pontoise

rec.title: Formes normales et structures géométriques sur les variétés de Hopf
rec.speaker: Paul Boureau
rec.abstract:
Nous montrerons comment la dynamique holomorphe contractante définissant
une variété de Hopf permet de construire naturellement une géométrie localement homogène.
La théorie de Poincaré–Dulac et les polynômes sous-résonnants conduisent à l’existence
d’une (G,Cn)(G,\mathbb C^n)-structure sur toute variété de Hopf de dimension au moins deux.
Nous étudierons également la rigidité, la non-unicité et la classification de ces structures.
rec.series_name: Séminaire de Géométrie et Dynamique de Cergy-Pontoise

rec.title: Mass in almost Kähler geometry
rec.speaker: Partha Ghosh
rec.abstract:
In this talk, I present an explicit formula for the ADM mass of asymptotically
locally Euclidean (ALE) almost Kähler manifolds. The formula expresses the mass in terms of
the total Hermitian scalar curvature and topological data associated with the underlying almost
complex structure, extending a result of Hein and LeBrun in the Kähler ALE case. The proof is
based on a spin-c adaptation of Witten’s proof of the positive mass conjecture in the spin case
and is therefore distinct from previous complex-geometric methods. In dimension 4, I show that
one can prove a positive mass theorem and a Penrose-type inequality for asymptotically Euclidean
(AE) almost Kähler manifolds using this formula.

rec.title: Diffuse Interface Models and their Sharp Interface Limits
rec.speaker: Helmut Abels
rec.abstract:
CANCELED – For personal reasons, Helmut Abels has unfortunately been forced to cancel his seminar. – CANCELED
Speaker: Helmut Abels (Universität Regensburg)
Interfaces separating two or more species or components of a material are omnipresent in applications in the sciences. Nowadays there are two main classes of models to describe interfaces, both from a theoretical and practical point of view: In classical so-called « sharp interface models » the species or components under consideration fill disjoint domains that are separated by lower dimensional surfaces of a certain regularity. On the other hand in « diffuse interface models » a partial mixing of the species or components on a small length scale is taken into account, which leads to an interfacial layer of small but positive thickness. This has the advantage that the interfaces do not need to be resolved explicitly and singularities in the interfaces can be described consistently.
In the first part of the talk we will give an overview of some basic diffuse interface models with applications to material sciences. Moreover, we will discuss some analytic results on the relation between diffuse and sharp interface models, when the interfacial thickness of the diffuse interface tends to zero. The analysis is based on formally matched asymptotic expansions (in a rigorous manner) together with uniform estimates for the linearized operator. In this part we will focus on the Allen-Cahn equation as basic model.
In the second part we will discuss a Navier-Stokes/Allen-Cahn system, which describes the flow of two macroscopically immiscible viscous incompressible fluid, separated by a diffuse interface. We will present some recent results on novel higher-order estimates for the sharp interface limit of this system. With the aid of a suitable weight taking the distance to the interface and the interfacial thickness into account we obtain optimal regularity estimates, which are uniformy in the interfacial thickness. This enables to improve previous convergence results in two space dimensions significantly and extend results to three space dimensions. This is a joint-work with Mingwen Fei, Yadong Liu, and Maximilian Moser.
Helmut Abels

rec.title: The Liquid Drop Model: From Minimizers to Non-Spherical Equilibria
rec.speaker: Monica Musso
rec.abstract:
Speaker: Monica Musso, University of Bath
Abstract for the mini course: Introduction to the Liquid Drop Model: Minimizers, Stability and Nonexistence
The liquid drop model, introduced by Gamow to describe atomic nuclei, is a classical problem in the calculus of variations involving the competition between surface tension, which favours compact shapes, and Coulomb repulsion, which favours spreading and fragmentation.
In this introductory lecture, I will present the mathematical formulation of the model and review some fundamental results concerning the existence and geometry of energy minimizers. Particular attention will be given to the role of balls, their minimality and stability properties, and the nonexistence of minimizers for sufficiently large masses. I will discuss the main mathematical ideas behind these results, as well as some open questions.
Abstract for the talk: Beyond Minimizers: Constructing Non-Spherical Equilibria
While balls are stationary configurations for the liquid drop energy at every volume, the existence of other critical points is a much more delicate question.
In this talk, I will discuss recent results on the existence and construction of smooth, compact, non-spherical equilibria of the liquid drop model, in both the small- and large-mass regimes. For small masses, I will describe the construction of configurations consisting of two nearly spherical regions connected by a very thin catenoidal neck. For large masses, I will present equilibria resembling necklaces of pearls, whose geometry is related to Delaunay unduloids. I will also discuss bifurcation phenomena from spherical equilibria, which give rise to further families of non-spherical stationary configurations.
The emphasis will be on the geometric ideas and analytical techniques behind these results, particularly singular perturbation methods and Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction. Together, these constructions reveal the richness of the critical point structure of the liquid drop energy, far beyond the theory of minimizers.
This work is in collaboration with M. del Pino, F. De Regibus, R. Frank, M. Grossi and A. Zuñiga.
Monica Musso (University of Bath)

rec.title: Dynamique des tourbillons visqueux dans un demi-plan
rec.speaker: Thierry Gallay
rec.abstract:
ANNULÉ – En raison de la fermeture du campus Pierre-et-Marie Curie le séminaire est ANNULÉ.
Speaker: Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)
Le but de cet exposé est de définir un cadre mathématique permettant de décrire les interactions entre tourbillons et parois pour des écoulements plans à grand nombre de Reynolds. Les phénomènes typiques que l’on souhaite étudier à terme sont le mouvement auto-induit (pour un tourbillon isolé) et l’effet de rebond (pour une paire de tourbillons).
Dans la première partie, à caractère tout à fait élémentaire, on explique comment résoudre les équations de Navier-Stokes incompressibles dans un demi-plan en exploitant l’équation d’évolution pour le tourbillon du fluide. Si l’on suppose que la vitesse s’annule sur la paroi, le tourbillon vérifie une condition au bord non linéaire et non locale qui est difficilement utilisable en pratique. On peut toutefois la remplacer par une condition intégrale permettant une formulation élégante du système, lequel se résout alors par un simple argument de point fixe dans un cadre fonctionnel approprié.
Dans la seconde partie, en cohérence avec l’objectif affiché, on suppose que la donnée initiale est une collection finie de tourbillons ponctuels, dont les circulations peuvent être arbitrairement grandes. Ce cas ne peut pas être traité comme précédemment par un simple argument de point fixe, mais on peut tout de même montrer l’existence et l’unicité de la solution en utilisant une décomposition appropriée, qui permet de traiter la partie la plus singulière de la solution dans le plan tout entier où l’on dispose d’outils plus affûtés. En fonction du temps disponible, on présentera également quelques résultats concernant le comportement asymptotique en temps de la solution, ses propriétés de localisation, ou la question difficile de la limite non visqueuse.
Cet exposé repose entièrement sur un travail en collaboration avec Anne-Laure Dalibard.
Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)

rec.title: Deux applications des marches aléatoires branchantes avec sélection
rec.speaker: Yueyun Hu
rec.abstract:
Les marches aléatoires branchantes avec sélection modélisent des populations de particules qui se déplacent et se reproduisent, mais dont la croissance est limitée par un mécanisme de sélection. Dans cet exposé, je présenterai deux applications de ce modèle : la première concerne la percolation par la moyenne sur le graphe complet, la seconde le problème du couplage planté dans les graphes. Travaux en commun avec Elie Aïdékon et Dana Yang.

rec.title: Un degré de différentiabilité peut tout changer
rec.speaker: Hélène Eynard-Bontemps
rec.abstract:
Par lisse, certains entendent de classe $C^1$, d’autres $C^\infty$, alors que pour l’analyse élémentaire, la mécanique Newtonienne ou les questions de courbure, $C^2$ semble plus naturel… Les mathématiques regorgent d’exemples de problèmes ou de techniques qui sont extrêmement sensibles à la régularité dans laquelle on travaille, souvent pour des raisons profondes et intéressantes. J’illustrerai cette affirmation à l’aide d’exemples tirés de la dynamique unidimensionnelle (qui s’intéresse aux difféomorphismes de l’intervalle et du cercle) mais aux origines bien géométriques : le célèbre théorème de Denjoy et le bijou moins connu qu’est le lemme de Nancy Kopell.

rec.title: David Bessis – La chute de l’économie du théorème
rec.speaker: REPORTÉ
rec.abstract:
Si les machines démontrent les théorèmes, que reste-t-il aux humains ? En quelques mois, les progrès des modèles d’IA ont fait entrer la recherche mathématique mondiale dans une crise sans précédent, remettant à la fois en cause ses critères de valeur, son organisation pratique et son image publique. En dépit de sa nouveauté radicale, la crise actuelle nous confronte à des questions anciennes, jamais résolues, dont les mathématicien(ne)s ont longtemps cru qu’elles étaient purement théoriques : que sont les mathématiques ? Comment créent-elles de la valeur ? Quel rôle jouent-elles dans la cognition humaine ?

rec.title: How to Encode World Knowledge?
rec.speaker: Guy Gilboa
rec.abstract:
Foundation models are a key platform which implicitly encodes world knowledge. In this talk we first focus on vision-language models, such as CLIP, and investigate their geometric behavior and logic behind the high-dimensional feature encoding. For instance, we find that as image or text become more rare and distinct they are encoded further from the center of the embedding. We explain why InfoNCE loss leads to that behavior. We also find out empirically that each modality can be well modeled statistically as admitting a multivariate Gaussian distribution. This finding is then proved formally, where we show InfoNCE asymptotically induces Gaussian statistics. Finally, we connect two major image foundation models – encoders and generators, through a universal normal embedding hypothesis. A surprising consequence of this hypothesis is demonstrated, where generative diffusion « noise » contains semantic data which can be accessed by linear probing for either classification or editing. This talk is based on 6 recent papers in the group published at ICML 2025, ICLR 2026 and CVPR 2026.

rec.title: Automath! À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? Maths + IA Controversy Workshop
rec.abstract:
À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? En deux ans à peine, les mathématiques semblent être passées du statut de frontière de l’IA à celui de territoire de l’IA, du statut d’idéal cognitif servant à tester les capacités de raisonnement des modèles d’IA, à celui d’infrastructure de connaissance, productive et mobilisable de façon en partie automatisée. C’est en tous cas le message envoyé par OpenAI (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture d’Erdős), Anthropic (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture jacobienne), Google DeepMind (e.g. AlphaProof) ou encore la DARPA avec le programme ExpMath. Si le moment se veut historique, la suite n’est pas écrite pour autant. La communauté mathématique se prépare et s’interroge : À quel endroit faut-il résister ? Et à quel autre faudrait-il plutôt s’adapter ? À quelles conditions ? Comment souhaitons-nous voir se dessiner les trajectoires de l’IA et de la recherche mathématiques ? L’équipe Inria SIRA, le LFPC et le collectif Automath invitent la communauté mathématique élargie à se saisir collectivement de ces enjeux lors d’une journée de workshop (ai4sciencecontroversy.com)
Comme en témoigne la Déclaration de Leiden [1.] ou le formule Terence Tao dans une publication récente [2.] : « How should the mathematical community respond to the advent of modern AI technologies, and their real and/or claimed capabilities to perform mathematical tasks? (…) It is a metamathematical question. »

rec.title: Autour de la localisation des racines d’un polynôme après dérivation
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé nous étudierons plusieurs questions autour du problème de la localisation des racines d’un polynôme dérivé par rapport aux racines de ce polynôme.
Tout d’abord nous rappellerons quelques résultats déterministes classiques autour de ce problème. Puis nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle probabiliste en nous demandant où se situent les racines du polynôme dérivé lorsque les racines du polynôme initial ont été tirées de manière indépendante et identiquement distribuée dans le plan complexe. Pour finir, nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle d’analyse en expliquant comment ce dernier peut mener à l’étude d’une équation aux dérivées partielles non linéaire et non locale obtenue après passage à une limite champ moyen
