rec.title: Monodromy in Radial Persistence Vineyards and visualizing with Bouquet2D
rec.speaker: Rohit Roy
rec.abstract:
Given a manifold M without boundary, the Radial Persistence Transform (RPT) assigns to each point x in R^2 the persistence diagram of the squared Euclidean distance function d_E^2(., x) restricted to M. As x moves along a closed loop gamma, these diagrams form a periodic vineyard. The RPT is a variant of the persistent homology transform (PHT) introduced by Turner and collaborators, and is more sensitive, see Onus et al. Both the RPT and PHT can exhibit monodromy; after a full traversal of gamma, points of the persistence diagram return permuted. Monodromy obstructs feature tracking and complicates downstream analysis in TDA pipelines, and understanding when and why it occurs is an open problem. Arya et al. gave an example with monodromy for the PHT and the geometric conditions that exclude monodromy, both in 2 dimensions.
Chambers et al. showed that monodromy and knotting of arbitrary complexity can occur for the RPT. We are exploring the relation between the monodromy in a vineyard and the topology of the vineyard for the RPT on one hand and the symmetry and focal set (the bifurcation set for distances) on the other. Classical results of Bruce, Giblin and Gibson, and of Porteous, show that the Morse decomposition of the distance function changes only when x crosses the symmetry set or the focal set of M. We prove that for curves in R^2, the vineyard of a sufficiently small loop gamma cannot exhibit monodromy unless gamma encloses a specific singularity of the symmetry set. This yields a local classification of the causes of monodromy in 2 dimensions, which we are currently expanding to a global classification. This opens the door to algorithmic criteria for detecting and then exploiting or avoiding it.
Our investigation has been informed and corroborated by experimentation with Bouquet2D, an interactive web-based tool for exploring this phenomenon. The tool allows the user to define M as a spline curve and draw a loop gamma, and the tool displays the symmetry and focal sets of M together with the vineyard as x moves along gamma. Deforming M updates all of these in real time, so one can directly observe how bifurcations of the symmetry and focal sets appear as events in the vineyard, and where monodromy arises. Bouquet2D is available for everyone to experiment with vineyard topology at: https://bouquet2d.rohitroy.me/.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, online

rec.title: Canopies for Generalized Persistence
rec.speaker: Barbara Giunti
rec.abstract: In this talk, we provide a new construction for studying parameterized persistence, called a canopy. We do this by making a simple but major modification in the persistence bundle representation information: namely, rather than tracking a point in the persistence diagram, we instead track some choice of pairs of simplices that created said point. This viewpoint is a combinatorial version of tracking the chain complex information rather than just the output of persistence. We show how to construct the canopies from any filtered filtration function, proving, using the algebraic structure of filtered chain complexes, that different choices of pairs result in homeomorphic structures. Finally, we showcase the power of our approach by using canopies to define vines even in the presence of points with multiplicity; to discuss monodromy; and to obtain some immediate results linking non-trivial monodromy in the persistent homology transform with the existence of non-Hausdorff points in the canopy.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, online

rec.title: Colloquium : "Nielsen meets Weil"
rec.speaker: Maxim Kontsevich
rec.abstract: A hundred years ago Jacob Nielsen proposed a lower bound on the number of fixed points of a self-map, utilizing the action on the fundamental group. The natural bookkeeping device is the Reidemeister trace, a linear combination of twisted conjugacy classes. I will review the classical theory and propose an analogue for varieties over finite fields, in the spirit of the rationality part of the Weil conjectures, where the self-map is replaced by the Frobenius automorphism. The resulting conjecture can be checked in non-trivial examples.

rec.title: Conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland et applications
rec.speaker: Vanja ZULIANI
rec.abstract:
Les conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland nous permettent d’étudier les espaces de modules d’objets dans une catégorie dérivée et de décomposer chaque objet en facteurs plus “simples". Cette thèse examine deux applications de la théorie des conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland. Dans la première partie, on étudie la géométrie d’une variété de Fano de dimension 8 et d’indice 3, définie comme une sousvariété lagrangienne d’une variété hyperkählérienne ; on étudie une dégénérescence semistable et on en déduit ses nombres de Hodge. En particulier, on observe que la structure de Hodge est de type K3 et que le rang de Picard est égal à un.
La deuxième application de la théorie des conditions de stabilité concerne l’étude du programme des modèles minimaux non commutatifs. On montre que les décompositions semiorthogonales standard sur les grassmanniennes, les quadriques et les hypersurfaces cubiques de dimension 3 et 4 sont induites par des chemins quasi-convergents dans la variété de stabilité, dont la charge centrale est donnée par la cohomologie quantique. Une partie du dernier chapitre est basée sur un travail en collaboration avec Tomohiro Karube et Antonios-Alexandros Robotis.

rec.title: Une inégalité isopérimétrique quantitative dans l'espace
rec.speaker: Gisella Croce
rec.abstract:
Dans ce séminaire nous allons étudier un problème de stabilité pour l'inégalité isopérimétrique dans $\mathbb{R}^3$, faisant intervenir une asymétrie de type Hausdorff. Pour un corps convexe $F \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ de volume $4\pi/3$ (c'est-à-dire le volume de la boule unité dans l'espace), nous considérons la fonctionnelle \[ Q^*(F) := \frac{\delta(F)\log\bigl(\delta(F)+\delta(F)^{-1}\bigr)P(F)^3} {\lambda^*(F)^2}, \] o\`u $\delta(F)$ d\'esigne le déficit isop\'erim\'etrique, c'est-à-dire la différence entre le périmétre $P(F)$ et le périmètre de la boule unité, et $\displaystyle \lambda^*(F):=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^3} d_H(F,B+x)$
la distance de Hausdorff à la famille des boules unit\'es. Le facteur logarithmique reflète l'échelle capacitaire optimale au voisinage de la boule en dimension trois, tandis que le facteur $P(F)^3$ assure la coercivité. Notre résultat principal est l'existence du minimum de $Q^*$ dans la classe des corps convexes de volume $4\pi/3$.
Ce travail est en collaboration avec S. Bove et G. Pisante.

rec.title: A Reider Theorem for Hilbert Schemes of Points on a Surface
rec.speaker: Aaron Bertram
rec.abstract: Reider's Theorem on very ampleness of divisors of the form \(K_S + D\) on a non-singular surface has a natural generalization to ampleness of divisors of the form \((K_S + D)_d - \Delta\) on the Hilbert schemes of d points on \(S\). The boundary case, where we can prove the divisor is nef but not ample, is a very natural generalization of the pull-back of \(2\Theta\) under the Abel-Jacobi map for curves. In light of Mumford's theorem for surfaces with \(p_g\) different from zero, these nef divisors surprised us. In this talk I will explain some interesting geometry for particular surfaces and also sketch the proof, which relies on results of Bayer-Macrì and Toda on Bridgeland stability conditions on surfaces.

rec.title: On the Wasserstein Geodesic Principal Component Analysis of probability measures
rec.speaker: Alice Le Brigant
rec.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: In this talk we discuss how to perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of a dataset whose elements are probability distributions, compared using the Wasserstein distance. The goal is to identify geodesic curves in the space of probability measures that best capture the modes of variation of the underlying dataset. To achieve this, we leverage the Riemannian interpretation of the Wasserstein metric. We first address the case of a collection of centered Gaussian distributions, and show how to lift the computations in the space of invertible linear maps using Bures-Wasserstein geometry. For the more general setting of absolutely continuous probability measures, we use Otto-Wasserstein geometry and neural networks to parameterize geodesics in Wasserstein space. Finally, we compare to classical tangent PCA through various examples and provide illustrations on real-world datasets.

rec.title: Algèbres de von Neumann de réseaux arithmétiques et ensembles de Kakeya
rec.speaker: Mikael de la Salle
rec.abstract:
Une forme de la conjecture de rigidité de Connes prédit que les algèbres de von Neumann de $\mathrm{PSL_n}(Z)$ sont toutes distinctes. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est toujours ouverte. Des anciens travaux avec Vincent Lafforgue et Tim de Laat (ainsi que d'autres travaux de Uffe Haagerup et Tim de Laat) suggèrent une approche possible à cette conjecture, en terme de propriétés d'approximation.
J'expliquerai pourquoi cette approche est difficile: elle implique aussi une forme de la conjecture de Kakeya en toute dimension.
La conjecture de Kakeya en dimension d affirme que toute partie de l'espace euclidien de dimension d, qui contient un segment dans toute direction, est de dimension de Hausdorff égale à d. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est prouvée uniquement en dimension 2 (Davies, Cordoba) et 3 (Wang et Zahl).

rec.title: Depicting instabilities in linear, dispersive PDEs: a dynamical systems approach
rec.speaker: Maria Teresa Rotolo
rec.abstract:
We consider linear, time-dependent perturbations of periodic transport equations on tori of arbitrary dimension. We identify a class of perturbations that admit a large set of unstable solutions: to detect such behavior, we prove that their positive Sobolev norms grow exponentially fast in time. Moreover, we prove that this class of perturbations is generic in dimension two.
The proof relies on a normal form procedure combined with the study of dynamical properties of Morse-Smale transport systems.
In this talk, after a general introduction to the topic, we describe the result and ideas of the proof, focusing on the interplay between pseudodifferential theory and hyperbolic dynamics. This is a joint work with Gabriel Rivière.

rec.title: Hidden symmetries of modular geodesics
rec.speaker: Alain Valette
rec.abstract:
The dihedral group of order 4 acts on the conjugation classes of hyperbolic elements of $PSL_2(\mathbf{Z})$: by passage to the inverse, by conjugation by an element of $GL_2(\mathbf{Z})$ of determinant -1, and by the product of the 2. Via the dictionary (which will be recalled) between closed hyperbolic and geodesic conjugation classes of the modular surface, the same group acts on modular geodesics, which can therefore acquire non-trivial symmetries by being fixed under one of the 3 involutions above. We will characterize these invariant geodesics and we will see that there is a strong link with Gauss' reciprocal, ambiguous and inert quadratic forms. It is a joint work with C.-L. Simon (Rennes)
Cultural coffee by Ramanujan Santharoubane at 13:05.

rec.title: Homogenized Transformers
rec.speaker: Hugo Koubbi
rec.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: We study a random model of deep multi-head self-attention in which the weights are resampled independently across layers and heads, as at initialization of training. Viewing depth as a time variable, the residual stream defines a discrete-time interacting particle system on the unit sphere. We prove that, under suitable joint scalings of the depth, the residual step size, and the number of heads, this dynamics admits a nontrivial homogenized limit.Depending on the scaling, the limit is either deterministic or stochastic with common noise; in the mean-field regime, the latter leads to a stochastic nonlinear Fokker–Planck equation for the conditional law of a representative token. In the Gaussian setting, the limiting drift vanishes, making the homogenized dynamics explicit enough to study representation collapse. This yields quantitative trade-offs between dimension, context length, and temperature, and identifies regimes in which clustering can be mitigated.

rec.title: Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres ~~ Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture
rec.speaker: Quentin Gazda, Felipe Gambardella
rec.abstract:
Felipe Gambardella (Orsay), 2-3pm
Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture.
Seeking a Diophantine characterisation of cohomological dimension of fields, Kato and Kuzumaki introduced the C_i^q property for every pair of non-negative integers i and q. These properties are inspired by Lang’s notion of a C_i field and Bloch-Kato’s conjecture relating Milnor K-theory with Galois cohomology. An interesting property of C_i fields is that they satisfy a transfer principle with respect to equicharacteristic complete discrete valuations – i.e. if a field k is C_i, then the field of Laurent series k((t)) is C_{i+1}. However, for the C_i^q property, no such transfer result is known to hold and the situation is more subtle than the one of C_i fields. For instance, the optimistic statement “k((t)) satisfies C_{i+1}^q whenever k satisfies C_i^q ” is false. This talk reports on joint work with Konstantinos Kartas. I will present a transfer principle for C_i fields with respect to non-discrete valuations. This principle has as a corollary a transfer principle for a variant of the Kato-Kuzumaki properties. Moreover, this is enough to establish the Kato-Kuzumaki conjecture for several fields of arithmetic interest such as the perfection of Fp((t_1)) . . . ((t_n)) or C(x_1, . . . , x_n)((t_1)) . . . ((t_m)) and to establish a strengthening of the C_1^1 property for Q_p introduced by Wittenberg.
Quentin Gazda (IMJ-PRG), 3.30-4.30pm
Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons un travail en commun avec Tess Bouis où nous construisons une version q-déformée du régulateur de Dirichlet p-adique des corps de nombres. De manière surprenante, notre construction ne nécessite ni la complétion en p, ni que p soit premier. Nous interpréterons ce régulateur à travers la notion de q-Gauges, objets globaux ayant vocation à interpoler les structures de Hodge p-adiques en chaque p.

rec.abstract:
Le séminaire des doctorants se propose de fournir aux doctorants une occasion de s'ouvrir aux autres domaines des mathématiques que le leur. A chaque séance, un intervenant réalise un exposé sur un fait standard de leur domaine d'étude, de niveau adapté à l'ensemble des doctorants.
Introduction aux empilements de cercles
Le théorème des empilements de cercles (circle-packings) est un théorème très amusant et dont la preuve est élémentaire. Il permet d'associer un empilement de cercles à toute triangulation simple et planaire. Ce théorème a été découvert indépendamment à trois reprises, à chaque fois pour des motifs différents. Ce n'est qu'après une conférence donnée par Thurston en 1985 que la communauté mathématique se saisit des empilements de cercles. L'objectif de l'exposé est de présenter une preuve du théorème et quelques-unes de ses multiples applications.
----
The PhD students seminar aims to provide PhD students with an opportunity to explore other areas of mathematics beyond their own. At each session, a speaker gives a presentation on a standard topic in their field of study, at a level suitable for all phd students.
The circle-packing theorem is a very fun theorem whose proof is elementary. It associates a circle-packing to any simple planar triangulation. This theorem was independently discovered three times, each time with different motives. In 1985, Thurston gave a talk on the subject which is responsible for the growth of interest for circle-packings in the mathematical community. The goal of the talk is to give a proof of the theorem together with a few of its numerous applications.

rec.title: Plongements conformes de surfaces de Riemann
rec.speaker: Alaa Mohamed BOUKHOLKHAL
rec.abstract: Étant donnée une surface riemannienne, il n’est pas toujours possible de la plonger isométriquement dans une variété riemannienne donnée M, notamment en raison de contraintes telles que la courbure. Cependant, la situation devient beaucoup plus flexible si l’on cherche un plongement conforme. Dans cet exposé, on montre l’existence de plongements conformes dans le cas où M est une variété pseudo-riemannienne. De plus, on montre que l’inclusion de l’espace des immersions lisses et conformes dans l’espace des immersions induit une bijection entre les composantes connexes par arcs de ces deux espaces.

rec.title: Géométries de Wasserstein slicées et hiérarchiques : flots de gradient et analyse variationnelle
rec.speaker: Christophe Vauthier
rec.abstract: Dans cette thèse, nous analysons la géométrie induite par deux variantes de la distance de Wasserstein en transport optimal: la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et la distance Wasserstein sur Wasserstein. Dans la première partie de cette thèse, nous nous focalisons sur la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et nous examinons les propriétés de convergence et les points critiques de sa forme semi-discrète. Puis, nous définissons un cadre général pour l'étude de points critiques de fonctionnelles définies sur des espaces de mesures de probabilités, que nous utilisons pour démontrer que les points critiques en contexte semi-discret sont un cas particulier d'un type spécifique de mesures critiques que nous appelons points critiques lagrangiens. Nous étudions ensuite les propriétes des points critiques lagrangiens de la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, notamment leur existence et leur stabilité. Enfin, nous étudions la quantification de la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et nous dérivons de nouvelles bornes sur son erreur de quantification uniforme. Dans la deuxième partie de cette thèse, nous nous concentrons sur le cas particulier du transport optimal où l'espace sous-jacent est lui-même un espace de probabilités. Nous construisons en particulier une structure de type riemannien sur l'espace de mesures de probabilités sur des mesures de probabilités $\cPP{\R^d}$, muni de la distance Wasserstein sur Wasserstein, nous permettant de considérer des flots de gradient Wasserstein sur cet espace. Nous montrons ensuite comment ce cadre théorique peut être appliqué à divers problèmes de machine learning, par le biais de flots de jeux de données représentés par des éléments de $\cPP{\R^d}$. Enfin, dans la troisième et dernière partie, nous étendons cette théorie à toute la suite d'espaces $\cPn{n}{\cM} = \cP_2(\ldots\cP_2(\cM)\ldots)$ obtenue en itérant l'opération $\cP_2$ sur une variété riemannienne $\cM$. Nous montrons que ces espaces peuvent à nouveau être munis d'une structure de type riemannien d'une façon systématique, nous permettant d'analyser leur géométrie, de caractériser leurs géodésiques et de définir le gradient de fonctionnelles.

rec.title: Rigorous identification of dynamics from data
rec.speaker: Konstantin Mischaikow
rec.abstract:
It is well established that there is no algorithm that given countable data can identify up to conjugacy the global dynamics of nonlinear system. Thus, if we wish to systematically and rigorously understand data driven dynamics we need a courser characterization of dynamics that still capable capturing essential features, e.g., fixed points, periodic orbits, chaotic dynamics, bifurcations, etc.
With this in mind I will focus on two topics.
1. I will describe a combinatorial/algebraic topological approach to dynamics based on ideas of Conley and show that at this level dynamics can be learned given enough data and enough computing power. In addition, I will show that for low dimensional examples this approach is computationally tractable and requires relatively little data.
2. I will show how using encoders and latent dynamics this approach can give rigorous results about high dimensional systems. I will present examples that show that experimental results are much more promising than theory suggests.

rec.title: Points critiques stationnaires pour un modèle champ de phase en mécanique de la rupture
rec.speaker: Martin Rakovsky
rec.abstract: Cette thèse est consacrée à la fonctionnelle de Mumford-Shah, utilisée pour modéliser les fissures fragiles dans un matériau élastique, et plus particulièrement à son approximation par la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous nous intéressons notamment à l'analyse asymptotique des points critiques de la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli, afin d'étendre aux points critiques la convergence des minimiseurs globaux obtenue par $Gamma$-convergence. Nous commençons par présenter les fonctionnelles de Mumford--Shah et d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli et le principe de l'approximation champ de phase. Ensuite, en dimension $1$, nous établissons la convergence des points critiques dans le cas où l'on rajoute à la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli une condition d'obstacle. En dimension quelconque, la convergence des points critiques est connue sous l'hypothèse supplémentaire que l'énergie d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli converge. En dimension $2$, nous montrons ce résultat en ne supposant qu'une partie de la convergence de l'énergie. Enfin, nous étudions le système parabolique associé aux équations vérifiées par les points critiques d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous établissons l'existence, les conditions d'unicité et la régularité des solutions de ce système, et obtenons en particulier leur régularité maximale en toute dimension.

rec.abstract: Cette soutenance présentera certaines de mes contributions à la théorie des tests multiples. Je présenterai notamment de nouvelles méthodologies pour contrôler les fausses découvertes grâce à des bornes de confiance et des procédures de contrôle du False Discovery Rate (FDR). Ces procédures assurent un recouvrement post hoc, ce qui signifie qu'elles préservent les garanties statistiques même après l'intervention du praticien --- comme le p-hacking ou le HARKing --- et offrent une plus grande flexibilité en lui permettant de sélectionner l'ensemble de rejets de manière adaptative. De plus, ces méthodes exploitent également la structure des données ; elles vont au-delà de l'hypothèse i.i.d. traditionnelle en prenant en compte l'hétérogénéité des données afin d'améliorer la puissance statistique.

rec.title: Scattering and smoothing for the two-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
rec.speaker: Muyuan Lyu
rec.abstract:
Scattering theory describes the large-time behavior of nonlinear evolution equations through comparison with a linear flow. This raises a further question: can the nonlinear correction to the asymptotic state be smoother than the initial data?
I will begin with an introduction to scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, highlighting several developments that motivate this question. I will then present a deterministic smoothing result for the two-dimensional cubic equation. Assuming that a solution scatters in the harmonic Sobolev space (\mathcal H^s), with (s>0), the difference between its scattering state and its initial datum belongs to (\mathcal H^{s+\sigma}) for every (0<\sigma<\min{2s,1}). The proof combines the lens transform, which turns the large-time problem into a finite-time endpoint problem, with bilinear Strichartz estimates and harmonic spectral analysis. The emphasis will be on the mechanism behind the regularity gain. The talk is intended for graduate students in analysis, with no prior familiarity with nonlinear scattering required.

rec.title: Training deep Transformers: mean-field models and convergence analysis
rec.speaker: Raphael Barboni
rec.abstract:
Transformers have become the dominant architecture in modern machine learning, yet the theoretical understanding of their training dynamics remains limited, especially for deep architectures with many layers and Attention heads. I will present a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing gradient-based training of Transformers in the overparameterized regime, where depth, width and context length tend to infinity. This mean-field model features two types of measure representations: token distributions evolving through layers (measures over the token space), and Attention parameters at each layer (measures over the parameter space). Our contributions are twofold: (i) We prove the well-posedness of gradient flow curves in a conditional Wasserstein metric space, establishing a rigorous foundation for gradient-based Transformer training. (ii) We prove convergence of gradient flow towards global minima when the initial training risk is sufficiently low. A key technical contribution is providing necessary and sufficient conditions for injectivity of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) for Attention mechanisms: we show that NTK injectivity is equivalent to linear independence of log-sum-exp functions modulo affine functions, a condition satisfied by diverse token distributions, including discrete distributions, uniform distributions, and Gaussian mixtures.
These results builds on joint works with M. de Hoop, T. Furuya, G. Peyré and F.-X. Vialard.

rec.abstract:
Thematic 3-weeks programme at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris, May 18th to June 4th, 2027.
Beware: It was reported to us that scammers are sending to participants fraudulent e-mails about accommodation/fees. Please be particularly cautious about e-mails not coming from the organisers nor from an @ihp.fr address.
REGISTRATION IS FREE, HOWEVER MANDATORY.
Presentation of the programme
In recent years, there have been major advances using techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to show, in a rigorous way, that many classical problems in Dynamical Systems are impossible to solve. In this context, a problem that can be set in a Polish space is said to be impossible to solve if it cannot be settled using inherently countable techniques. These groundbreaking results mostly lie in Ergodic Theory, with further significant advances in Topological and Smooth Dynamical Systems.
One main goal of this program is to further enhance interactions between Descriptive Set Theory and Dynamical Systems. It brings together researchers from different fields to settle some of the most famous problems in dynamics dating to the mid-20th century.
A second main goal is to expand applications of the techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to other areas of mathematics.
Week 1
The program begins with lectures introducing the basic impossibility techniques and lectures explaining fundamental concepts in areas of potential applications.
We plan to have tutorials on:
Impossibility Results
Ergodic Theory
Symbolic Dynamics
Smooth Dynamical Systems
Additionally, there will be Research Talks and Expository Lectures (primarily in Ergodic Theory and Descriptive Set Theory).
Week 2
Research talks in Descriptive Set Theory, Ergodic Theory, Smooth and Symbolic Dynamics, as well as Expository Lectures, including on:
Impossibility Results in Ergodic theory
Complexity Theory
Flexibility and Rigidity
Moreover, we will have Problem and Discussion Sessions.

rec.abstract:
Thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops
September 14th to December 4th, 2026 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris

Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. Deadline for financial support request is March 15, 2026
Operator algebras are self-adjoint subalgebras of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space and divide into two main classes: C∗-algebras and von Neumann algebras, according to whether one demands that they are closed in the norm topology or the weak operator topology. When one first meets these algebras, they might look quite similar, but they have different natures as exemplified by the commutative case: via the Gelfand transform, abelian C∗-algebras are algebras of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on a locally compact Hausdorff space, while abelian von Neumann algebras are essentially bounded measurable functions on a measure space. These flavours persist in general. Topological concepts such as dimension and invariants such as K-theory pervade the study of C∗-algebras, while measure-theoretic style methods are often used to study von Neumann algebras.
The long thematic program OA will focus on operator algebras and its still evolving interactions with ergodic theory, topological dynamics, discrete subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, analytic, ergodic and geometric group theory, quantum information theory and random matrices.

This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators.

Deadline for financial support request has been extended to: June 30th, 2026.
Summary
The program centers on the development of a unified understanding of kinetic theory in systems with long‑range interactions, with a particular emphasis on the quantum regime. Long‑range interacting quantum systems—realized experimentally in cold atoms, trapped ions, and polar molecules—exhibit rich dynamical behavior such as metastability, collisionless dynamics, anomalous transport, critical scaling, and turbulence‑like phenomena. These effects are often linked to the Vlasov equation, the collisionless kinetic equation that emerges in the thermodynamic limit. While Vlasov theory is conceptually well established in classical plasma physics, its systematic extension to quantum many‑body systems remains incomplete.
A key scientific motivation of the program is that different communities—mathematical physics, quantum many‑body theory, and AMO physics—address similar non‑equilibrium long‑range phenomena using different methods, preventing the emergence of a unified framework. The program aims to bridge these approaches and clarify conceptual connections between classical and quantum kinetic theories.
The scientific agenda spans several interconnected themes. One major theme is the analysis of classical transport, Vlasov dynamics, and their differences from Boltzmann kinetic theory, including how turbulence, chaos, and long‑range correlations emerge in classical systems. Another theme concerns the quantum generalizations of Vlasov theory, focusing on rigorous derivations and effective equations for quantum gases, including mean‑field and Gross–Pitaevskii limits, and the treatment of finite‑size effects in quantum simulators.
The program will explore non‑equilibrium many‑body dynamics in quantum systems, including quantum turbulence, cascade processes, ergodicity breaking, and anomalous scaling. A related line of inquiry concerns the dynamics of quantum correlations and entanglement, the onset of quantum chaos, and the characterization of universal quasi‑static dynamics in isolated systems. Another scientific direction is the study of effective theories in quantum matter, connecting renormalisation‑group methods with kinetic descriptions and identifying the regimes where classical scaling concepts can illuminate quantum behavior.
On the mathematical side, the program emphasizes rigorous derivations of macroscopic equations from microscopic many‑body dynamics, particularly in long‑range systems, and the formulation of effective transport equations, scaling limits, and mean‑field theories. Renormalisation‑group tools are highlighted both in their rigorous and approximate forms, with the aim of connecting microscopic models to emergent large‑scale behavior in many‑body systems.
Finally, the proposal identifies a scientific need to synthesize current insights into a coherent and predictive quantum kinetic theory for long‑range interactions, and to outline a roadmap of open problems invol

Recent trends at the interface between information theory, probability, statistics and high-dimensional geometry raise new questions on the role and importance of entropy in the understanding of both asymptotic and finite range phenomena, in particular towards discrete structures and applications to areas such as quantum information, percolation and random matrices. Recent fruitful developments warrant imminent blossom of new ideas and results in this area in the near future.
Another central theme at the interface of High-Dimensional Probability and Convexity is the study of isoperimetric properties of log-concave measures (including isoperimetric-type questions related to convex bodies). This is not a mere curiosity: convexity and isoperimetry play an important role in the study of concentration of measure phenomena which is crucial for harnessing various high-dimensional effects in Probability as well as several applied fields.
The scope of the semester includes developing further connections between Information Theory and Convexity, in all of the different directions described above. The semester will aim to strengthen these powerful interdisciplinary methods, aiming towards challenging issues and applications, including the isoperimetry questions for log-concave measures, and super-concentration properties of models from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
The semester’s objective is to foster cross-fertilization between probability, analysis, information theory and convex geometry (continuous and discrete). By organizing two thematic pre-schools, we will ensure active participation by junior researchers, which should have a lasting effect on their careers, as well as influence the routes along which these research areas will be developed in the future. Our two workshops will further provide opportunities for many re- searchers from across the globe to interact and collaborate. We believe that close interactions between these disciplines are a necessary condition to address many mathematical challenges raised in the last decades, and that the timing is optimal to bring together all these powerful ideas which have been recently developed in several communities. Therefore, our proposed semester program will have a strong and lasting impact on High-Dimensional Probability, Convexity and Analysis as a whole.

This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on mathematical developments in Advances in Quantum Cryptography (QCRYPTO).

Presentation of the programme
Quantum cryptography lies at the intersection of cryptography, quantum information, and computational complexity. Quantum technologies offer new cryptographic possibilities, while also changing our understanding of which security guarantees and computational tasks are achievable. Recent developments have revealed deep connections between these areas, but many fundamental questions remain open.
This programme will bring together researchers from theoretical computer science, mathematics, cryptography, and quantum information. It will explore three closely connected directions: information-theoretic foundations, including quantum communication, nonlocality, randomness, and device-independent security; complexity-theoretic foundations, including quantum proofs, verification, reductions, and computational assumptions; and computational and interactive primitives, including commitments, zero knowledge, secure computation, and protocols involving quantum devices.
Through an introductory school, seminars, focused workshops, informal discussions, and extended research visits, the programme aims to develop a common language across neighboring communities. It will provide opportunities for sustained collaboration between senior and junior researchers, encourage new research partnerships, and help identify important directions for the next stage of quantum cryptography.

rec.title: Séminaire 09/10/2026 - Gabriel Peyré and Vianney Perchet
rec.abstract:
14h15-15h15 Gabriel Peyré (ENS)
The Expressive Power of Large Language Models
Abstract: Large language models process vast sequences of input tokens by alternating between classical multi-layer perceptron layers and self-attention mechanisms. While the approximation capabilities of perceptrons are relatively well understood, those of attention mechanisms remain less explored. In this talk, I will compare the proof techniques and approximation results associated with these two types of layers, emphasizing key open questions that connect large language models with approximation theory in infinite-dimensional spaces representing input token distributions.
15h30-16h30 Vianney Perchet (Criteo et ENSAE)
AI-powered AI. Robustness, Consistency and Smoothness of Algorithms.
Abstract: AI systems no longer operate as isolated algorithms, machines, or agents; instead, they
interact with each other. An algorithm designed for a specific task might use the output or
prediction of another as its input. This has serious consequences: blindly relying on another
algorithm can be extremely helpful if it is accurate, but devastating if it is not, as a single error -
even the tiniest one - could break down the whole system. New algorithms will need to incorporate
these predictions to improve their consistency, while remaining robust against errors. We will use
simple toy examples to show how the generic framework of learning-augmented algorithms (LAA) is
perfectly suited for this challenge, highlighting the complexity of designing practical and potentially
vastly more efficient algorithms.

rec.title: Amal Omrani - Explicit Computation of Super-Hedging Prices and Strategies under Transaction Costs
rec.abstract: In markets with transaction costs, can super-hedging prices and strategies be explicitly characterized and computed directly from real market data, without relying on dual formulations? This talk presents a constructive approach based on conditional supports and dynamic programming, leading to explicit recursive formulas for super-hedging prices and strategies. The approach is illustrated using real market data.
rec.location_text: Salle Olga Ladyjenskaïa, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Ruben Haalebos - Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
rec.abstract: We study dynamic portfolio decarbonization under incomplete information about firms' carbon intensities and the underlying transition state. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth net of a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. Asset returns and carbon intensities depend on a stochastic transition factor, while the investor may need to infer the current transition state, its long-run mean and firms' carbon intensities from market observations and periodic noisy disclosures. The optimal strategy combines a Merton-type component with climate-dependent expected-return adjustments, a direct carbon intensity penalty and intertemporal hedging demands associated with stochastic carbon intensities and learning. In a numerical application, incomplete information has limited effects on welfare and target satisfaction when prior beliefs are well specified. By contrast, biased beliefs generate welfare losses in either direction but asymmetric environmental consequences: optimistic and pessimistic beliefs induce opposite portfolio tilts and therefore affect the probability of exceeding the cumulative emissions target differently.
rec.location_text: Salle Olga Ladyjenskaïa, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Élise Devey - A Frank–Wolfe-Type Algorithm for High-Dimensional Stochastic Control Problems with Non-Exchangeable Agents
rec.abstract: Abstract : This paper presents a Frank--Wolfe type algorithm for computing approximately optimal distributed stochastic controls in a large population of $N$ agents cooperating to minimize a convex cost functional. The cost includes a heterogeneous pairwise interaction term between the agents' controls, which rules out a direct treatment by the classical Mean Field Control framework. Working directly at finite $N$ rather than through a mean-field limit, we prove that the distributed controls returned by our algorithm are $N^{-1/2}$-optimal for the original problem, with an explicit rate in the number of iterations $K$ and in a measure of interaction heterogeneity, $\Delta_{\mathrm{spread}}$, that we introduce. The algorithm avoids the curse of dimensionality: at each iteration, the coupled $N$-agent problem is linearized and decomposed into $N$ independent, low-dimensional subproblems. We illustrate the approach on a linear-quadratic benchmark, for which we derive a closed-form Riccati-type characterization of the optimal control, and validate the predicted convergence rate numerically. Interaction structures of this heterogeneous, pairwise-penalized type arise naturally in applications such as electricity grid flexibility management, where local storage units are coupled through shared transmission-line capacity constraints.

rec.title: Marco Plazzogna - Endogenous Dynamic Networks for Heteroscedastic Outcomes
rec.abstract:
Many economic and financial systems are naturally represented as networks: the outcome of one unit may depend on those of other units through relationships that evolve over time. A central difficulty is that these relationships need not be exogenous. The network itself may react to the same shocks that affect the variables of interest, creating an endogeneity problem that cannot be addressed by treating network weights as fixed or predetermined.
We study a dynamic spatial model in which the interaction network is time-varying and generated by an auxiliary formation process. Dependence between innovations driving network formation and the structural outcome shock is explicitly incorporated through a control-function approach.
The framework is further extended to allow for conditional heteroskedasticity. In particular, we distinguish between two potentially different dynamic networks: one governing the transmission of outcomes in the conditional mean, and another governing the propagation of past shocks in the conditional variance. This makes it possible to separate network effects on the level of the process from network effects on its risk and volatility.
The resulting model provides a framework for studying systems in which both interactions and uncertainty evolve endogenously over time.

rec.title: Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables
rec.abstract:
La Cinquième rencontre de probabilités intégrables aura lieu le vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à l'Institut Henri Poincaré.
Titles and Abstracts
Mini-course (2x1h) by Cédric Boutillier
Title:
Abstract:
Seminar talk (1h) by Elia Bisi (Università degli Studi di Firenze)
Title: Matrix Whittaker processes
Abstract: The log-gamma polymer is a prominent integrable model in the KPZ class: the law of its partition function is a marginal of a Whittaker measure, a positive-temperature analogue of the Schur measure. I will present a non-commutative generalisation, in which the “particles” are positive definite matrices. These evolve as interacting multiplicative random walks with inverse Wishart increments, arranged in a triangular array with push-and-block interactions. Using intertwining relations, we show that, for suitable random initial configurations, the bottom edge of the array evolves as an autonomous Markov process, with a kernel built from Whittaker functions of matrix arguments. For a singular initial state, its fixed-time law is a matrix Whittaker measure. Consequently, the matrix log-gamma polymer partition function is distributed as the first marginal of this measure.
Joint work with Jonas Arista and Neil O’Connell.

rec.title: Le problème de Littlewood inverse pour les fonctions multiplicatives
rec.speaker: Péa Bazin
rec.abstract: Nous montrons que si $f$ est une fonction complètement multiplicative vérifiant $$\int_0^1 \left| \sum_{n\le x} f(n)e(\alpha n) \right|\,d\alpha \ll \log x$$ pour tout $x$, alors $f$ est exactement de la forme $\chi(n) n^{it}.$ Travail coécrit avec Oleksiy Klurman.

rec.title: Sur la probabilité qu’un entier possède un diviseur de la forme $p-1$ dans un intervalle donné
rec.speaker: Rebecca Abi Abdallah
rec.abstract: Dans cet exposé, nous étudierons la fonction qui compte les entiers naturels inférieurs ou égaux à $x$ possédant, dans un intervalle $(y,z]$, un diviseur de la forme $p-1$, où $p$ est premier. En analysant le comportement asymptotique de cette quantité dans les différents régimes de $z=z(y)$, nous mettrons en évidence une transition de phase qui révèle les dépendances entre ces événements de divisibilité en fonction de la longueur logarithmique de l’intervalle $(y,z]$. Notre résultat généralise un théorème de Ford correspondant au cas $z=x$. Ceci est un travail en collaboration avec V. Kovaleva, J. Schlitt et N. Tardy.

rec.abstract: Nous expliquerons comment la preuve d’un théorème central limite pour les fonctions multiplicatives aléatoires étendues nécessite des résultats sur les équations diophantiennes. Cela aboutit à des problèmes de comptage intéressants. C’est un travail en collaboration avec Max Xu et Victor Wang.

rec.title: Irreducibility of random reciprocal polynomials
rec.speaker: David Hokken
rec.abstract: Let $P = a_m T^m + \sum_{j=0}^{m} a_j (T^{m-j} + T^{m+j})$ be a monic reciprocal polynomial of even degree n, with the $a_j$ drawn independently and uniformly at random from $\{1, 2, \ldots, H\}$ for some fixed integer $H \geq 35$. In joint work with Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, building on prior work of Bary-Soroker—Koukoulopoulos—Kozma, we show that $P$ is irreducible over the rationals, and has large Galois group, with probability tending to 1 as $n$ tends to infinity. This is in line with the long-held belief going back in various forms to Hilbert, Van der Waerden, Odlyzko—Poonen and Konyagin that a typical polynomial is irreducible and has Galois group as large as possible. I will discuss some recent, related developments in the field of probabilistic Galois theory before discussing aspects of the proof, which draws from classical polynomial theory, Fourier analysis, probability theory and group theory.

rec.title: Palindromes and Kloostermania
rec.speaker: Daniel Johnston
rec.abstract: Recently, there has been a surge in new results on the digital properties of numbers. In this talk, we discuss some recent results on palindromes, numbers which are the same backwards and forwards (e.g. 12321 or 7887) in a fixed base. Despite being elementary objects of study, in order to prove deep results about their multiplicative properties we need to turn to powerful estimates on exponential sums. For this talk, we focus particularly on a recent result of Bryce Kerr and myself, establishing the infinitude of square-free palindromes.

rec.title: Low Lying Zeros of Hecke $L$-Functions
rec.speaker: Ezra Waxman
rec.speaker_affiliation: Academic College of Engineering in Tel Aviv, Israël
rec.abstract: The one-level density measures the statistical distribution of zeros across a family of $L$-functions near the central point. In this talk, I will present several results concerning the one-level density for families of $L$-functions associated to CM elliptic curves of the form $y^2=x^3-dx$. The talk will moreover discuss applications to bounding the average rank of such curves (joint work with Chantal David, Lucile Devin, and Alessandro Fazzari).

rec.abstract:
Le séminaire Bourbaki a été fondé en 1948. Au rythme de quatre séances par an, il tente d'offrir un panorama des développements mathématiques actuels.

rec.title: An affirmative solution to the generalized Busemann-Petty problem with subspaces dimensions 2 and 3
rec.speaker: Cheng Lin
rec.abstract: The generalized Busemann--Petty problem asks whether two origin-symmetric convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ having larger volume of all $m$-dimensional sections necessarily have larger volume. When $m\geq 4$, this is known to be false, but the cases $m=2, 3$ for $n\geq 5$ have remained open since the 1990s. In this work, we resolve these cases. Together with the known results, the generalized Busemann--Petty problem is completely solved: the answer is affirmative for $m=1, 2, 3$, and negative for $m\geq 4$. This talk is based on the joint work with Yu-de LIU and Ge XIONG.

rec.title: Exact curve counting on the once-punctured torus
rec.speaker: Mingkun Liu
rec.abstract: Two closed curves on a surface are said to have the same topological type if they lie in the same mapping class group orbit. Mirzakhani first showed that, on a hyperbolic surface, the number of closed geodesics of a given topological type of length at most L is asymptotically proportional to L^{6g-6}. In this talk, we will focus on the case of the once-punctured torus. Rather than using hyperbolic length, we will count curves according to their word length. In this setting, it turns out that exact counting formulas can be obtained. This is joint work with Filippo Baroni and David Fisac.

rec.title: An Introduction to D-Modules
rec.speaker: Raoul Hallopeau
rec.abstract: The theory of D-modules had initially been developed for complex (algebraic and analytic) varieties in the 1970's, and allows for an algebraic approach of partial differential equations. There are lots of applications; for instance, in the 1980's Masaki Kashiwara and Zoghman Mebkhout have used it to generalize the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. D-modules are also an invaluable tool in less expected areas, such as Representation Theory. In more recent years, D-modules have also found applications to the world of arithmetic varieties.

rec.title: The p-adic Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence

rec.abstract: In this talk, I will introduce differential equations on p-adic analytic varieties. We will see how the ultrametric p-adic topology is an obstruction to a Cauchy-Lipschitz-type result. I will then show, following Scholze, how the pro-étale topology and the introduction of new numbers called "periods" provide a workaround to this issue.

rec.title: De la modélisation aux problèmes inverses : une méthodologie pour les systèmes dynamiques en biomédecine.
rec.speaker: Pierre Monmarché
rec.abstract:
Oratrice : Annabelle Collin (Université de Nantes)
Résumé : Les systèmes dynamiques constituent un cadre naturel pour décrire l'évolution temporelle et spatiale de nombreux phénomènes rencontrés en biologie, et en médecine. Qu'ils soient formulés sous la forme d'équations différentielles ordinaires (EDO) ou d'équations aux dérivées partielles (EDP), ces modèles permettent de formaliser des mécanismes biologiques, physiologiques ou épidémiologiques et d'étudier leur dynamique.
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons les principales étapes d'une démarche de modélisation mathématique appliquée à des problématiques biomédicales : construction et formalisation du modèle, étude de ses propriétés théoriques, approximation numérique, puis confrontation du modèle aux données à travers la résolution de problèmes inverses. Une attention particulière sera portée à l'estimation de paramètres et d'états non directement observables, ainsi qu'aux difficultés associées à l'identifiabilité, aux incertitudes et au caractère potentiellement bruité ou incomplet des observations.
Nous nous intéresserons plus particulièrement aux approches séquentielles, qui permettent de mettre à jour progressivement l'estimation de l'état du système et de ses paramètres au fur et à mesure de l'acquisition de nouvelles données.
Cette démarche sera illustrée sur un exemple volontairement simple, permettant de mettre en évidence les principales étapes méthodologiques tout en montrant comment des modèles relativement parcimonieux peuvent déjà conduire à des résultats quantitatifs pertinents et exploitables dans un contexte de santé publique.

rec.title: Limit of archimedean heights and Ceresa cycles
rec.speaker: Souvik Goswami
rec.speaker_affiliation: IISER - Indian Institute of Science Education and Research
rec.abstract: For a smooth, projective and complex variety $X$, and a pair of algebraic cycles $Z$ and $W$ that are homologous to zero and are in complementary codimensions, the archimedean height pairing is a real number that can be interpreted as a secondary intersection pairing that measures how far a certain cohomology group of the pair $(X\setminus |Z|, |W|)$ is from being real split. This interpretation makes it suitable for variational study: Let $\Delta := \{t\in \mathbb{C};\,|t|<1\}$, and $\Delta^{\ast}=\Delta\setminus \{0\}$. Given a family $\{X_t\}_{t\in \Delta}$ of projective and complex varieties that are smooth for $t\in \Delta^{\ast}$, while $X_0$ is a simple normal crossing divisor, and a family $\{Z_t, W_t\}_{t\in \Delta^{\ast}}$ of algebraic cycles in complementary codimensions that are homologous to zero, the function $h := \Delta^{\ast}\to\mathbb{R}$, with $h(t)$ being the archimedean height pairing of the pair $(Z_t, W_t)$, is smooth. But $h$ does not extend to $t=0$. R.~Hain, G.~Pearlstein, P.~Brosnan et al. have shown that the asymptotic function $\widetilde h(t)= h(t)+\mu \log|t|$ extends continuously to $t=0$, where $\mu\in\mathbb{Q}$ depends on the monodromy of the variation of mixed Hodge structures associated with these pairings. Fixing a parameter $t$, one can ask if $\widetilde h(0)$ is given by the archimedean height pairing of algebraic cycles associated with the central fiber $X_{0}$. In a joint work with Dr. Irene Spelta, I have shown that this question has an affirmative answer in case of height pairings of Ceresa cycles (arxiv.org/abs/2604.01842). The purpose of this talk will be to explore this result and some interesting questions that still remains unanswered.

rec.title: Exposés de Marco Di Marco et Jean-François Babadjian
rec.abstract:
Marco Di Marco :
Title: Quantization of measures in Carnot groups
Abstract: The aim of the talk is to present a sub-Riemannian analogue of the celebrated Zador theorem, a cornerstone of the theory of quantization of measures. After a brief introduction to sub-Riemannian geometry and Carnot groups, I will outline the key ideas behind the proof of the Euclidean Zador theorem and its sub-Riemannian version. Talk based on a joint work with Mikaela Iacobelli.
Jean-François Babadjian :
Titre : Energies de surfaces anisotropes, courbure et approximation champ de phase
Résumé : Dans cet exposé, je présenterai des résultats obtenus en collaboration avec Blanche Buet (LMO, Orsay) et Michaël Goldman (LAMA, Créteil) concernant les effets régularisants de termes de type courbure moyenne pour les modèles avec interface en présence d'anisotropie. Lorsque la tension superficielle est une fonction convexe de la normale, l'anisotropie est dite faible. Ceci assure généralement la semi-continuité inférieure de l'énergie associée. En revanche, si la tension superficielle dépend de la normale de manière non convexe, cette forte anisotropie peut engendrer des instabilités liées à l'absence de semi-continuité inférieure de la fonctionnelle. Nous étudions les effets régularisants de l'ajout d'un terme d'ordre supérieur de type Willmore à l'énergie. Nous considérons deux types de problèmes : une généralisation anisotrope non convexe du périmètre et une fonctionnelle aux discontinuités libres de Mumford-Shah, anisotrope non convexe. Dans les deux cas, nous établissons les propriétés de semi-continuité inférieure des énergies, ainsi qu'une approximation par Gamma-convergence par des modèles de champ de phase. L'un des aspects originaux de notre travail dans le cadre des problèmes à discontinuités libres est le traitement des énergies de points qui repose sur un résultat de type Gauss-Bonnet pour les varifolds.

rec.title: An equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma
rec.speaker: Filippo Belfiori
rec.abstract: Gabber’s preparation lemma is a fundamental result in algebraic geometry, originally established by Gabber in 1994 in his work on the exactness of certain Gersten complexes. Following the work of Morel, Gabber’s lemma has become a cornerstone of motivic homotopy theory over fields, the homotopy theory of algebraic varieties. When algebraic varieties are equipped with an action of an algebraic group G, one can similarly define an equivariant motivic homotopy category, providing a framework for studying the homotopy theory of varieties with G-action. In this talk, I will first recall Gabber’s preparation lemma and discuss some of its main consequences. I will then propose and study an equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma for a finite constant abelian group G, based on the C2-equivariant version introduced by Bachmann. If time permits, I will also discuss some applications of this equivariant version of Gabber’s lemma.
rec.location_text: Salle Pierre Grisvard, IHP - Bâtiment Borel

rec.title: Good complexifications of nonnegatively curved manifolds
rec.speaker: Ethan Peng
rec.abstract: A closed manifold M admits a good complexification if it is diffeomorphic to the set of real points of a real affine variety X such that the embedding X(R) -> X(C) is a homotopy equivalence. We will give examples of such closed manifolds, including classical ones (spheres, RP2, homogeneous spaces, Cheeger manifolds), as well as a class of closed Riemannian manifolds with non-negative sectional curvature constructed by B. Totaro using plumbing techniques. We will also discuss topological constraints on closed manifolds admitting a good complexification, such as the classical non-negativity of its Euler characteristic, and vanishing of some Betti numbers and Pontryagin numbers as proved by Totaro. An effort will be made to explain how the curvature constraints interplay with the algebro-geometric aspects. If time permits, we will also discuss how good complexifications pass to quotients by nice group actions, giving ways to "algebraicize" various familiar manifolds.

rec.title: Zeta values as moments: A random matrix theory
rec.speaker: Hartmut Monien
rec.abstract: Values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be obtained as moments of a certain probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in representation theory of the symmetric group.

rec.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
rec.speaker: Sergei Nechaev
rec.abstract: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual tread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, they observed a logarithmic increase in the transverse span, D, of a thread with its length, N. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is an intermediate one, and sufficiently long threads exhibit topological localization, where span D approaches a finite limit at N >> 1. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints, giving rise to topological microphase separation. We study braids within a locally free approximation and confirm the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group LF_n which approximates the braid group B_{n+1}. We conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, n ~ 3 -- 5, the span, D, grows algebraically with N (N>>1), as D ~ N^{1/4}. By contrast, for large n, each thread in a long braid asymptotically localizes, approaching D ~ const.

rec.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette, « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
rec.abstract:
« Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle
Cette conférence hybride sera suivie d'un moment convivial.

rec.title: Origami Tori
rec.speaker: Richard Schwartz
rec.abstract:
An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R3. It is surprising that these things exist, but thanks to the work of Burago and Zalgaller in 1960 they do. 30 years later, B&Z proved that every flat torus is realized as an origami torus. In 2023, Lazarus and Tallerie proved that you can realize all flat tori using a single underlying triangulation with about 2500 vertices.
The question remained: how many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In this talk I will prove that the minimum number of vertices needed is 8. I will also discuss joint work, with Peter Doyle, proving that almost every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. Finally, I will explain work-in-progress with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel, which shows that in fact every flat torus is represented by an 8-vertex origami torus. If I have time, I will also discuss hyperbolic versions of this business.

rec.title: Families of Discrete Representations from Incidence Theorems
rec.speaker: Jean-Philippe Burelle
rec.abstract: Motivated by a family of examples constructed by R. Schwartz based on Pappus's theorem, we explore constructions of representations of discrete groups arising from incidence theorems in projective spaces. Schwartz recently proved that his construction parametrizes the boundary of a connected component of Anosov representations in a certain moduli space of representations of PSL(2,Z) into Isom(SL(3,R)/SO(3)). We use a generalized version of Pappus's theorem to define a higher dimensional analogue of this family, and we prove that in RP3 these representations are "extended geometrically finite", a notion of relative Anosov representation introduced by T. Weisman. This is joint work in progress with W. Dimoune.

rec.title: Nonrelativistic Conformal Collider Physics of Multiparticle Point Production
rec.speaker: Dam Thanh Son
rec.abstract:
Motivated by nuclear experiments where a few neutrons are produced by a local source, we develop a formalism of "nonrelativistic conformal collider physics." We define detector operators in the nonrelativistic conformal field theory describing fermions at unitarity. We reduce the problem of computing the momentum distribution and correlation between final particles produced by a local source ("point-produced") to the computation of correlation functions involving the detector operators. The general formalism is applied to the point production of three unitary fermions, where we find the momentum and angular distribution of final particles, and point production of a large number of fermions. We discuss a nonrelativistic version of celestial holography, which maps the asymptotic out-state to a quantum wave function in the so-called "oscillator frame." Based on arXiv:2608.18202 with Cyuan-Han Chang, Subham Dutta Chowdhury, and Ian Moult.

rec.title: On the Wilson-Fisher Fixed Point in the Limit of Integer Spacetime Dimensions
rec.speaker: Bernardo Zan
rec.abstract:
The Wilson–Fisher (WF) fixed point, a scalar field theory with a quartic interaction in $d = 4 - \epsilon$ dimensions, is the textbook example of a weakly coupled CFT. The epsilon expansion accurately reproduces the critical exponents of the $d = 3$ and the $d = 2$ Ising model. This has led to the common view that WF defines a continuous family of CFTs in non-integer dimensions, interpolating between the free theory at $d=4$ and the Ising model at $d = 3$ and $d = 2$. In this talk I will look at what happens to the WF CFT when the number of dimensions approaches an integer value. Identifying the $d\to 2$ limit of WF as the $2d$ Ising CFT raises some issues, related to the fact that the $d=2$ CFT has infinitely many conserved currents that the $d>2$ theory does not have. I will propose a scenario, inspired by some exactly solved two-dimensional models, where the $d\to 2$ limit of WF contains the $d=2$ Ising CFT as a subsector, but contains more operators which do not completely decouple from the Ising subsector. I will explain why this makes the task of obtaining a $d= 2 + \epsilon$ expansion for the Ising model harder.

rec.title: The Messy Story of Crossing Dispersion Relations
rec.speaker: Andrea Guerrieri
rec.abstract:
In this talk I will discuss an attempt of unifying under a simple geometric picture, the plethora of crossing symmetric dispersion relations existing in literature.
Each dispersion is valid on a different finite window in energy, but none of them could be extended to infinity.
I will explain how they can all be understood from a simple choice of a foliation of the kinematics space.
This geometric viewpoint also suggests the existence of a particular (but not so nice) foliation that naturally covers all energies. Unfortunately, this example turns out to be impractical for phenomenological and bootstrap applications. I will comment why, and what teaches us about the dual bootstrap.

rec.title: Proliferation Transitions for Non-Abelian Anyons
rec.speaker: Andrea Antinucci
rec.abstract:
Phases of matter and the transitions between them are famously characterized within the Landau paradigm and Landau–Ginzburg theory: phases are labeled by broken or unbroken symmetries, while phase transitions are described in terms of scalar order parameters. There are, however, phases beyond the standard Landau paradigm that are distinguished not by the realization of ordinary symmetries, but by that of generalized global symmetries. Among these, topologically ordered phases in (2+1)d possess non-invertible 1-form symmetries described by anyon lines. In this talk, I will present a framework for describing transitions between topologically ordered phases related by anyon proliferation, which can be viewed as a non-invertible generalization of the choice of the unbroken symmetry. The resulting theories involve scalar fields coupled to gauge fields. A crucial ingredient in this construction is the (3+1)d Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which allows to separate symmetry from dynamics and will be employed in a rather unconventional way.

rec.title: AI for Math: From Group Theory to Discrete Holography
rec.speaker: Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk
rec.abstract: I will describe how one can use modern machine learning methods to attack open problems in group theory. I will show how ideas from AI, pure math, integrability, string theory and quantum information meet here in a highly productive way. I will focus on much-studied Cayley graphs of permutation groups, which are often very hard to explore due to their enormous size. I will describe how a modern ML approach overcomes this challenge and provides efficient pathfinding on these huge graphs. The outcome is a large set of new results and conjectures that in particular sharpen famous bounds on the diameters of these graphs. These results also hint at the existence of a novel, discrete string-like duality for this setting. It provides a realisation of the paradigm "complexity = volume" from AdS/CFT holography, and may potentially be applicable to a wider range of AI tasks. Lastly I will outline some new results for combinatorics of quantum periods and how this could help in improving these ML approaches. Based on arXiv:2509.19162, 2603.22195 and work to appear. Our code is publicly available as the CayleyPy library.

rec.title: On “Siegel Domains” in p-adic Period Spaces
rec.speaker: Yoichi Mieda
rec.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
A Siegel domain is a finite-volume subset of a symmetric space whose translates under the action of the relevant arithmetic group cover the entire space. In this talk, we consider an analogue for the p-adic period spaces introduced by Rapoport and Zink. We give a partial criterion for the existence of a Siegel domain and discuss its expected applications.

rec.title: The Pentagram Map and Ramifications
rec.abstract:
October 12-15, 2026
at IHES - Marilyn and James Simons Conference Center
How to get to IHES
This workshop explores the mathematics connected to the pentagram map and its generalizations.
With 3 talks per day, spread out over 4 days, leaving time for individualized interactions, it will not be confined to the special topic of the pentagram map, but rather an exploration of the kind of mathematics that it relates to: integrable systems, algebraic dynamics, projective geometry and cluster algebras.
The pentagram map is a geometrically flavored dynamical system defined on polygons by a simple and projectively natural straight-line construction.
Starting with a polygon, one intersects the shortest diagonals in cyclic order to produce a new polygon with the same number of vertices.
Though quite elementary to define, the pentagram map turns out to have a deep structure connected to completely integrable systems, symplectic geometry, cluster algebras, dimers, algebraic dynamics, and moduli spaces.
The same goes for the many generalizations of the pentagram map, some of which are still quite mysterious.

rec.title: Dynamical Tidal Response of Neutron Stars from Scattering Amplitudes
rec.speaker: Muddu Venkata Sai Saketh
rec.speaker_affiliation: International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS-TIFR), Bengaluru, India
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In this talk I will describe an amplitude-based framework for extracting the frequency-dependent tidal response of neutron stars while preserving the tidal resonances associated with their normal modes. The response is obtained by matching the amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a neutron star, equivalently gravitational Compton scattering, computed using relativistic stellar perturbation theory, to the corresponding amplitude in worldline effective field theory. The tidal contribution is isolated through the difference between the neutron-star and black-hole scattering phases. Unlike conventional treatments, the construction allows for a post-Newtonian expansion without Taylor expanding the response in frequency or assuming a harmonic-oscillator model for the internal dynamics.
I will present the tidal response through relative third post-Newtonian (3PN) order and use currently available numerical results to illustrate its frequency dependence. The results reproduce the known static Love numbers in the low-frequency limit, exhibit resonances at the expected stellar mode frequencies, and capture their damping through gravitational-wave emission. I will also discuss the renormalisation of the tidal response required through 3PN order. Time permitting, I will outline how the resulting response can be incorporated into binary dynamics and ultimately into gravitational waveforms.

rec.title: Zeta Values as Moments: A Random Matrix Theory
rec.speaker: Hartmut Monien
rec.abstract: The values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be viewed as moments of a probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in the representation theory of the symmetric group.

rec.title: Finiteness and Density Problems for (Positive) Integral Points on Mordell–Schinzel Surfaces
rec.speaker: Robin Zhang
rec.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
In 1952, Mordell erroneously claimed that the surface xyz = G(x,y) has infinitely many integral points for any G ∈ ℤ[x,y]. I will discuss a classification for finiteness and Zariski density of (positive) integral points on these log K3 surfaces when the coefficients of G are non-negative. This combines a dynamical argument proposed by Mordell, the theory of generalized cluster algebras, and the Killing–Cartan classification of semisimple Lie algebras. This talk is partially based on joint work with Antoine de Saint Germain.

rec.title: Gravitational Sommerfeld Effects: Framework and Applications
rec.speaker: Chia-Hsien Shen
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
Sommerfeld effects describe long-distance corrections to radiation emitted by a short-distance source. They play an important role in atomic physics and dark matter phenomenology, but the same mechanism also arises in gravitational-wave radiation from compact binaries. In this talk, I will develop a systematic framework for gravitational Sommerfeld effects by combining worldline effective field theory with black hole perturbation theory. A key advantage of this framework is that it organizes high-order perturbative calculations without requiring any nontrivial loop integration, allowing us to compute the waveform to tenth order in the perturbative expansion and beyond. The formulation also reveals an exact connection between the radiation waveform and Compton scattering, as well as the underlying structures of the classical renormalization group of the multipoles and tidal Love numbers. I will conclude by discussing how these results can be incorporated into waveform resummation models for gravitational-wave signals. This talk is based on arXiv:2604.14112 with Chih-Hao Chang and Zihan Zhou, and work in progress.

rec.title: The Doubly Conformal Dispersion Relation
rec.speaker: Balt van Rees
rec.abstract:
We provide a simple derivation of the conformal dispersion relation of Carmi and Caron-Huot which reconstructs a CFT four-point function from its double discontinuity. We exhibit a hidden conformal symmetry which explains the appearance of the "magic variable" x as a simple cross-ratio, built from four physical cross-ratios. We also introduce a regulator in the double discontinuity operation and then prove that one subtraction suffices for all integrals to converge.

rec.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette : « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
rec.abstract:
Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle.

rec.title: Horizon flux-balance laws in the multiscale perturbation
rec.speaker: Ali M. Seraj
rec.speaker_affiliation: Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences (IPM), Tehran
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
I study the evolution of the event horizon in a “two-timescale” perturbative expansion around a stationary black hole. This leads to strong constraints on the “coarse-grained” horizon dynamics. At leading order, the horizon exhibits an “adiabatic rigidity”: the leading corrections to its angular velocity and inaffinity remain uniform on each horizon cut, while evolving on the slow timescale. We then provide a systematic procedure for transforming a perturbative bulk solution, given for example in Lorenz gauge, to an ingoing Newman--Unti gauge adapted to the horizon, allowing the perturbed horizon geometry to be extracted directly from the metric. Finally, we formulate “horizon conservation laws” associated with horizon symmetries, including energy, dynamical entropy, and angular momentum. We expand the charges through second order and their fluxes through third order in perturbation theory, providing a framework for future applications to horizon absorption and backreaction in extreme mass-ratio inspirals.

rec.title: Maximal functions, Nikodym sets and local smoothing estimates
rec.speaker: Chen Mingfeng
rec.abstract:
Séminaire d'Analyse
I will discuss some recent works related to maximal operators and Nikodym sets in the plane. Nikodym constructed a measure-zero Borel set in the plane that contains a line segment passing through each point in the unit square. Fenton and Falconer asked whether a similar construction is possible when “lines through a point” are replaced by ”circles with a prescribed center.” This was answered in the negative by Bourgain and Marstrand. We study a generalization of this question, in which “lines through a point” or “circles with prescribed center” are replaced by general analytic families of plane curves.
Using decouping, we prove new maximal function and local smoothing estimates for families of curves satisfying a multi-parameter analogue of Sogge's cinematic curvature condition. Combining with a recent nonlinear generalization of Falconer's prescribed projection theorem to construct Nikodym-type sets, we characterize when Nikodym-type sets exist for analytic families of plane curves.
