rec.title: Near-horizon Collisions at the Extreme: Naturalness and Observability of Critical Near-horizon Collisions around Near-extremal Black Holes
rec.speaker: Delilah Gates
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
In principle, rapidly rotating black holes could naturally act as particle colliders because geodesics particles that collide can exhibit center-of-mass (CM) energies that diverges in the limit that the black hole approaches extremality and the collision radius approaches the horizon, provided that one particle has a critically tuned angular momentum. In this talk, I present work to understand the naturalness and observability of these critical-particle collisions around near-extremal BHs. I will highlight 1) the landscape of conditions under which these critical-particle collisions occur, 2) the CM energy achievable for critical-particle collision where one particle falls from in from infinity and the other particle is part of an accretion disk, and 3) the observability as measure by the escape probability and expected energy of emission born of a critical-particle collision.

rec.title: The Stratified Shape
rec.speaker: Marco Volpe
rec.abstract:
In this talk, I will try to address the question of how to do algebraic topology with stratified spaces and schemes in a meaningful way. I will begin by recalling and motivating some of the main historical attempts to approach this question, both in topology and in algebraic geometry, passing through the work of Nash, Quinn, Siebenmann, Edwards–Hastings, Deligne, and, more recently, Lurie and Barwick–Glasman–Haine. I will then propose my own answer, based on a construction I call the stratified shape.
Time permitting, I will discuss some applications of the stratified shape to proper homotopy theory (joint with Georg Lehner), homology manifolds (joint with Markus Land), and a generalization of Lurie's exodromy equivalence (joint with Peter Haine and Guglielmo Nocera).

rec.title: Algebraic Theory of Indefinite Theta Functions
rec.speaker: Kenz Kallal
rec.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
Jacobi's theta function $\Theta(q) := 1 + 2q + 2q^4 + 2q^9 + \cdots $, and more generally the theta functions associated to positive-definite quadratic forms, have the property that they are modular forms of half-integral weight. The usual proof of this fact is completely analytic in nature, using the Poisson summation formula. However, $\Theta$ is also related to diffusion of heat on a uniform circle-shaped material: it is a restriction of the fundamental solution to the heat equation on a circle. By algebraically characterizing the heat equation as a specific flat connection on a certain bundle on a modular curve, we produce a completely algebraic technique for proving modularity of theta functions. More specifically, we produce a refinement of the algebraic theory of theta functions due to Moret-Bailly, Faltings--Chai, and Candelori. As a consequence of the algebraic nature of our theory and the fact that it applies to indefinite quadratic forms / non-ample line bundles (which the prior algebraic theory does not), we also generalize the Kudla--Millson analytic theory of theta functions for indefinite quadratic forms to the case of torsion coefficients. This is joint work with Akshay Venkatesh.

rec.title: Combinations of Non-Archimedean Discrete Groups
rec.speaker: Konstantinos Tsouvalas
rec.abstract: Chatterji and Venkataramana, motivated by Nori's problem, asked for a real algebraic semisimple Lie group G and a simple Lie subgroup H of G, whether a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup of G, intersecting H in a lattice, is itself a lattice in G. After discussing what is known related to this question and Nori's problem, we will address a similar version of this question for the k-points of semisimple groups defined over a non-Archimedean local field k, and provide examples for which a positive answer fails. This is based on a combination theorem for discrete subgroups of matrix groups over discretely valued fields. We will also discuss a construction of non-Fuchsian hyperbolic groups that quasi-isometrically embed as subgroups of matrix groups over a discretely valued field.

Le 14e séminaire Itzykson est organisé par Jean-René Chazottes (CPHT), Guillaume Dubach (CMLS), Ruben Minasian (IPhT) et Julio Parra-Martinez (IHES).
Depuis bientôt une quinzaine d’années l’axe math-physique de la FMJH organise un séminaire Itzykson tous les ans à l’IHES. Il s’agit d’une journée consacrée à un thème de physique mathématique, avec un cours et deux ou trois exposés spécialisés (en français ou en anglais selon le choix des orateurs).
Le prochain séminaire Itzykson portera sur la dualité markovienne, et ses liens avec les algèbres de Lie et les systèmes de particules en interaction. Ces sujets sont reliés par une même idée directrice : l'approche algébrique de la dualité, qui permet de construire et d'analyser des processus markoviens exactement solubles. Le séminaire donnera des perspectives algébriques, probabilistes et physiques sur des résultats récents, notamment au sujet des symétries des générateurs markoviens, des interprétations trajectorielles en génétique des populations, et des fluctuations macroscopiques hors d'équilibre.
Les cours et exposés de cette journée seront présentés par :
Cristian Giardinà (Università di Modena e Reggio Emilia)

rec.title: Scattering and Smoothing for the Two-Dimensional Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
rec.speaker: Muyuan Lyu
rec.abstract:
Séminaire d'Analyse
Scattering theory describes the large-time behavior of nonlinear evolution equations through comparison with a linear flow. This raises a further question: can the nonlinear correction to the asymptotic state be smoother than the initial data?
I will begin with an introduction to scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, highlighting several developments that motivate this question. I will then present a deterministic smoothing result for the two-dimensional cubic equation. Assuming that a solution scatters in the harmonic Sobolev space $(\mathcal H^s)$, with $(s>0)$, the difference between its scattering state and its initial datum belongs to $(\mathcal H^{s+\sigma})$ for every $(0<\sigma<\min{2s,1})$. The proof combines the lens transform, which turns the large-time problem into a finite-time endpoint problem, with bilinear Strichartz estimates and harmonic spectral analysis. The emphasis will be on the mechanism behind the regularity gain.

rec.title: A Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture in Dimension Three
rec.speaker: Thomas Mordant
rec.abstract:
Seed Seminar of Mathematics and Physics
AI and the Future of Mathematics and Physics
The Jacobian conjecture states that for any polynomial map from to itself, if it is everywhere a local diffeomorphism, then it admits a polynomial global inverse. In this talk, I will present the three-dimensional counterexample to this conjecture posted by L. Alpöge on and credited to Claude.
After stating the conjecture and the counterexample, I will explain the geometric interpretation of the counterexample which was posted by A. Jiang and credited to ChatGPT. Finally I will give some observations about the history of the conjecture and its significance.
We answer this problem coming from representation theory using topological tools. On the representation theory side we define extensions of Habiro type rings. On the topological side, we construct a universal Jones link invariant and a universal Alexander link invariant. Putting these together, our universal invariants of geometrical nature take values in the extended Habiro rings that we construct.

rec.title: Two Applications of the Arithmetic Margulis Lemma
rec.speaker: Marc Burger
rec.abstract:
This course has two parts. In the first we will define a general notion of integer point in a higher Teichmüller space and two invariants thereof, the arithmetic dimension and the arithmetic height. The aim is to show finiteness, modulo the mapping class group action, of the number of integer points for which both invariants are bounded.
In the second part we will give the main steps leading to the recent result of Frączyk, Hurtado and Raimbault, stating that the topological complexity of an arithmetic locally symmetric space is bounded by its volume.
Both parts rely on the arithmetic Margulis lemma proven by the same authors as a consequence of Breuillard's height gap theorem.

rec.title: Kneser Graphs: Variations on a Theme
rec.speaker: Matej Stehlik
rec.abstract:
Kneser graphs are a classical family of graphs that play a central role in graph colouring. In 1978, Lovasz determined their chromatic number using topological methods. Schrijver later strengthened this result by identifying vertex-critical induced subgraphs of Kneser graphs, now known as Schrijver graphs.
The talk will survey several recent developments involving these graph families, including constructions of edge-critical subgraphs of Schrijver graphs, a common generalisation of Kneser and Schrijver graphs, and a new family of vertex-critical graphs for which the standard topological lower bounds on the chromatic number are not tight.
The talk is based on joint work with Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, and Tomas Kaiser.

rec.title: Grid Minors in planar graphs
rec.speaker: Eileen Robinson
rec.abstract:
In 1984, Robertson and Seymour showed that the treewidth of a planar graph with no t × t grid as minor is bounded by a function g(t). Together with Thomas, they later proved that g(t) can be taken to be linear. The current best known bound, due to Gu and Tamaki (2012), is g(t) ≤ 9/2 t − 11/2. In this talk, I will show an improved bound of g(t) ≤ 4t + O(1), which is within a factor 2 of optimal.
This talk is based on joint work with Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Quentin Claus, Gwenaël Joret, Robin Petit and Jean-Florent Raymond.

rec.title: Combinatorial tools for posets topology and simplicial complexes
rec.speaker: Lucas Pouillart
rec.abstract: Topological theory of posets originates from a simple observation : the Möbius function of an interval of a poset P can be interpreted as the Euler characteristic of a simplicial complex. It turned out that in a lot of cases, these complexes hold a lot more information on P and that a lot of interesting examples satisfy the (homotopy) Cohen-Macaulay property, which gives both nice topological and algebraic properties. A lot of techniques were developed by combinatorialists to prove the Cohen-Macaulay property and give interpretations of algebraic and topological problems for posets as enumeration problems, and I will present some of them in this talk.

rec.title: Informative Trains: A Memory-Efficient Journey to a Self-Stabilizing Leader Election Algorithm in Anonymous Graphs
rec.speaker: Sylvain Gay
rec.abstract:
We study the self-stabilizing leader election problem in anonymous n-nodes networks. Achieving self-stabilization with low space memory complexity is particularly challenging, and designing space-optimal leader election algorithms remains an open problem for general graphs. In deterministic settings, it is known that Ω(log log n) bits of memory per node are necessary [Blin et al., Disc. Math. & Theor. Comput. Sci., 2023], while in probabilistic settings the same lower bound holds for some values of n, but only for an unfair scheduler [Beauquier et al., PODC 1999]. Several deterministic and probabilistic protocols have been proposed in models ranging from the state model to the population protocols. However, to the best of our knowledge, existing solutions either require Ω(log n) bits of memory per node for general worst-case graphs, or achieve low state complexity only under restricted network topologies such as rings, trees, or bounded-degree graphs.
In this paper, we present a probabilistic self-stabilizing leader election algorithm for arbitrary anonymous networks that uses O(log log n) bits of memory per node. Our algorithm operates in the state model under a synchronous scheduler and assumes knowledge of a global parameter N = Θ(log n). We show that, under our protocol, the system converges almost surely to a stable configuration with a unique leader and stabilizes within O(poly(n)) rounds with high probability.
Our algorithm is inspired by the uniform constant-state leader election protocol in [Vacus and Ziccardi, PODC 2025] for the beeping model (without self-stabilization). A novel component of our approach is the introduction of an information train mechanism that propagates O(log n)-bit information across the network while requiring only O(loglog n) local memory per node. We believe this mechanism may be of independent interest for the design of space-efficient self-stabilizing distributed algorithms.

rec.title: Introduction aux "enhanced categories"
rec.speaker: Sylvain Douteau
rec.abstract: Dans cette exposé, j'exposerai dans les grandes lignes la notion de "enhanced categories" introduite par Kaledin. Celle-ci est très inspirée de la théorie des dérivateurs, et vise à remplacer à la fois le formalisme 1-catégorique des catégories modèles et les raisonnements homotopiques des infinies catégories

rec.title: Les polygraphes réguliers et leur théorème de recollement homotopique
rec.speaker: Clémence Chanavat
rec.abstract:
Je commencerai par présenter deux (ou trois) manières de régulariser les polygraphes, que j'appellerai méthode-Hadzihasanovic, méthode-Steiner et, si le temps le permet, méthode-Henry.
J'expliquerai pourquoi la méthode-Hadzihasanovic ne produit pas toujours des polygraphes, à moins que l'on impose aux ∞-catégories strictes des lois d'échange supplémentaires, dictées par des égalités de topologie combinatoire.
Je terminerai par un théorème de recollement, issu de mes derniers travaux, qui assure que certains de ces polygraphes sont librement générés en un sens homotopique, ce qui signifie que ce sont aussi des polygraphes dans la théorie des (∞, n)-catégories.

rec.title: Combinatoire des mots, combinatoire énumérative et combinatoire algébrique autour de la forme normale alternante des tresses
rec.speaker: June Roupin
rec.abstract:
Les tresses sont des objets topologiques qui possèdent de très bonnes propriétés combinatoires, et peuvent en particulier être représentées et étudiées comme des classes d’équivalence de mots sur l'alphabet des transpositions. Un concept naturel dans ce contexte est la notion de forme normale : le choix d’un représentant unique pour chaque tresse. La forme normale alternante, dont l’étude a initialement été motivée par ses liens avec l’ordre standard des tresses, associe à chaque tresse sur n fils une séquence unique de tresses sur n-1 fils, appelés des blocs, permettant de définir récursivement un unique représentant.
Dans cet exposé, je vais présenter quelques propriétés combinatoires et algébriques importante de la forme normale alternante, notamment la régularité et l'automaticité du langage associé. Je vais ensuite aborder plusieurs applications de ces résultats couvrant divers domaines de combinatoires : énumération des tresses ; bon ordre totale sur le monoïde de tresse ; généralisations aux monoïdes d'Artin-Tits.

rec.title: Well-typed program generation, with prenex polymorphism
rec.speaker: Gabriel Scherer
rec.abstract:
Fuzzing” is a popular testing approach where we throw random inputs at a program and check that it respects some expected properties on all inputs. Fuzzing a metaprogram such as a compiler requires producing random input programs. To exercise interesting behaviors of the compiler, we want our input programs to be well-formed in a strong sense, in particular to be well-typed. Generating random well-typed program is difficult when the type-system is powerful, there is a whole scientific literature on the topic, see for example [Testing an Optimising Compiler by Generating Random Lambda Terms, Pałka, 2012].
Most existing generators integrate a large part of the implementation of a type-checker, “inverted” to assist in top-down random term generation by efficiently discarding choices that result in ill-typed programs. Scaling this approach to a full language would result in implementing two sophisticated type-checkers, once in the compiler and once in the program generator. This is one type-checker too many!
We present preliminary work on reusing the constraint-based type inference approach [The Essence of ML-based type inference, Pottier and Rémy, 2004] to write a single type-checker that can be used for both purposes: to check types of user-provided programs, and to efficiently guide a random program generator. This only requires a fairly simple modification to constraint generators: parametrizing them over a search monad. We have succesfully implemented a generator of simply-typed terms in this style, and are in the process (almost done) of scaling it to Hindley-Milner type inference.
(Relevant previous work is [Making Random Judgments: Automatically Generating Well-Typed Terms from the Definition of a Type-System, Fetscher, Claessen, Pałka, Hughes, Findler]. They start from Redex, a Racket DSL to implement simple type systems, and derive a random program generator. The limitation of this approach is that Redex only works with fairly simple type systems, in particular we do not expect it to scale to ML-style type inference with polymorphism, which is the part that hand-crafted generators also struggle on.)
Note: I gave a Formath talk on a preliminary version of this work in March 2024. At the time my prototype only supported the simply-typed lambda-calculus. The extension to Hindley-Milner is follow-up joint work with my 2025 intern Hugo Barreiro. I will also discuss optimizations to the search monad that are necessary to effectively generate terms of larger size.

rec.title: Remarques autour de la formule U^X = ∑_A:U X^A
rec.speaker: Mathieu Anel
rec.abstract: Cette formule classique de théorie des types est remarquable en ce qu’elle égalise des constructions contravariante et covariante en X. Pour l'étudier, je vais me placer dans la catégorie des algèbres sous la monade polynomiale associée à la famille universelle de types U’—>U. Cette catégorie est additive et monoïdale et on peut y relire la formule en terme de dualité et de formes quadratiques. Cela permet une caractérisation précise des paires (U,X) pour lesquelles la formule est vraie.

rec.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
rec.speaker: Carl Jontza
rec.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

rec.title: Verso Blueprint: Reimagining Blueprints for the AI Era
rec.speaker: Emilio Gallego Arias
rec.abstract:
Large-scale formalization projects have long needed tools to
coordinate contributions, track dependencies, and connect mathematical
exposition with formal proofs. A key example is Lean
Blueprint. Introduced in 2020 for the sphere eversion project, Lean
Blueprint extends plasTeX to provide a shared map of statements,
dependencies, Lean declarations, and progress. Lean Blueprint's model
has been quite influential and has helped shape how mathematicians and
formalizers work together on large-scale formalization projects.
This talk presents recent work on Verso Blueprint, a Lean-native
implementation of the Lean Blueprint concept built on Verso, Lean's
official markup language. Designed for close integration with Lean,
Verso Blueprint maintains a three-layer database linking source
material, informal statements, and their formalized counterparts. The
database is populated from Verso documents, analysis of Lean
declarations, and other user-provided data. Interactive HTML views
provide navigation and previews, connecting mathematical exposition
with the formal development. We have now largely reached our original
goal, with functionality comparable to Lean Blueprint or Lean
Architect.
But matching that functionality is no longer enough: this is an
extraordinary moment for formalisation. The practice is radically
chaining even as we build its tools.
When we began this project, our central use case was for humans to
write detailed statements and dependencies to guide
formalization. Today, coding agents are increasingly writing and
interacting with the blueprints themselves in an autonomous
fashion. Blueprints are taking on the reverse role: not just guiding
the construction of formal proofs, but making AI-generated proofs
intelligible to humans. At the same time, dependency tracking and
organizational information remain essential for coordinating
large-scale autoformalization. For example, Prove2Me, a theorem
database with dependency tracking, played a key coordination role in
the recent Fermat's Last Theorem auto-formalization milestone.
What comes next for blueprints in this extraordinary moment? We are
redesigning Verso Blueprint around the idea of "programmatic
blueprints": human-readable, machine-actionable objects synchronized
with formal developments. Our ambition is for blueprints to become a
*foundational harness for AI-assisted formalization*, maintaining the
shared state of a project and coordinating what happens next across
mathematicians, formalizers, code repository workflows, and agents.

rec.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
rec.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
rec.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

rec.title: Dynamics of singularity surfaces for the compressible viscous fluids.
rec.speaker: Marcel Zodji
rec.speaker_affiliation: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry
rec.abstract:
The motion of a compressible viscous fluid is described by the Navier-Stokes system.
It is a system of hyperbolic-parabolic mixed-type PDEs. In this talk, we will study
the so-called density patch problem: \emph{If we are given a density that is initially "regular"
on both sides of a hypersurface across which it is discontinuous, will this structure
be preserved over time?}
An important quantity in the mathematical analysis of this system is the so-called effective flux,
which was discovered by Hoff and Smoller (1985). More precisely, the mathematical properties
of this quantity play a crucial role in the study of the propagation of oscillations in
compressible fluids [Serre, 1991], in the construction of weak solutions [P-L Lions, 1996] or the
propagation of discontinuity surfaces [Hoff, 2002], to cite just a few examples.
In the case of density-dependent viscosities, the behavior of the effective flux degenerates,
which renders the analysis more subtle.

rec.title: Multi-scale modeling and analysis of signal processing in neurons
rec.speaker: Claire Guerrier
rec.abstract: In this talk, I will present models for signal propagation in neurons, ranging from the macro- to the micro-scale, with various applications to neuronal signalling. The first application concerns myelin plasticity, and the influence of neuronal myelin geometry on signal transmission. We investigate the evolution of the maximum of a signal in a damped heat equation on x>0, with a Dirichlet boundary condition representing the signal, which models signal transmission in a myelinated internode. We derive an expression of the solution, and derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator at x=0. We then investigate the max. At a more refined scale, to investigate signal summation in the neuronal dendritic tree, we consider the Poisson-Nernst Planck system of equations representing ionic electrodiffusion in an electrolyte. This system expresses a sharp boundary layer of the size of the Debye length at the boundary, where the extra-charges accumulates. In particular, we derive an asymptotic approximation of the solution at steady state, in the regime of small Debye length.

rec.title: Mosquito borne disease outbreak : Climate change impact to Physics Informed Neural Network use
rec.speaker: Aniket Banerjee
rec.abstract:
Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are expanding across new
territories as their vector, the tiger mosquito _Aedes albopictus_,
tracks a warming climate. Forecasting where and when outbreaks will
occur requires models that are both mechanistically faithful to mosquito
ecology and disciplined by real observational data — yet the
biological parameters that govern transmission, such as the biting rate,
the extrinsic incubation period and mosquito survival, are precisely the
ones we cannot measure directly in the field.
In this talk, I present a national -scale furcating framework that
couples a mechanistic _Aedes albopictus_ population model, in the spirit
of the Arbocarto approach, to a vector-to-human transmission layer, and
the use of Neural Network use to predict diffusion pattern in
epidemiological systems. I will explain the modelling choices behind the
population and transmission layers, the structure of the inverse
problem, and how PINNs let a mechanistic model "speak" to messy,
heterogeneous data.

rec.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
rec.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
rec.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

rec.title: Torseurs sur la droite affine sous des groupes lisses
rec.speaker: Alexis Bouthier
rec.abstract:
Si G est réductif sur un corps, un théorème de Raghunathan-Ramanathan énonce que
tout G-torseur sur la droite affine, trivial sur la clôture séparable, est trivial.
Le cas non-réductif avait été écarté d'emblée par les auteurs comme "rather complicated".
On montre qu'un tel énoncé vaut pour tout k-groupe lisse (et même pas lisse du tout).
On discutera également d'autres extensions et généralisations à l'étude des G-torseurs sur des espaces affines.
Travail en commun K. Cesnavicius et F. Scavia.

rec.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
rec.speaker: Martin Ortiz
rec.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

rec.speaker: Diego Izquierdo
rec.abstract: Dans cet exposé, je partirai de certaines conjectures de Kato et Kuzumaki reliant la dimension cohomologique des corps à l'existence de certains zéro-cycles sur des hypersurfaces de petit degré. On verra qu'en remplaçant les hypersurfaces de petit degré par des espaces homogènes il est possible d'obtenir des caractérisations de nature diophantienne de la dimension cohomologique. Il s'agit de travaux en commun avec Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche.

rec.title: A Dieudonné theory for analytic p-divisible groups
rec.speaker: Lucas Gerth
rec.abstract: We prove a classification of families of analytic p-divisible groups on adic spaces S over Qp in terms of Hodge–Tate triples on S, generalizing a theorem of Fargues. From this, for S a perfectoid space, we construct an analytic Dieudonné theory with values in mixed characteristic shtukas. As applications, we obtain moduli descriptions of local Shimura varieties of EL and PEL type. We also explain how to derive generalizations of the fundamental exact sequence of Colmez--Dospinescu--Nizio? on smooth Stein spaces.

rec.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
rec.speaker: Emma Weschler
rec.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

rec.title: Biased random walk on dynamical percolation
rec.speaker: Nina Gantert
rec.abstract:
As an example for a random walk in random environment, we
study biased random walk for dynamical percolation on the
d-dimensional lattice. We establish a law
of large numbers and an invariance principle for this random walk
using regeneration times.
Moreover, we verify that the Einstein relation holds, and we
investigate the speed of the walk
as a function of the bias. While for d = 1 the speed is
increasing, we show that in general this
fails in dimension d ? 2. As our main result, we establish two
regimes of parameters, separated
by a critical curve, such that the speed is either eventually
strictly increasing or eventually
strictly decreasing. This is in sharp contrast to the biased
random walk on a static supercritical
percolation cluster, where the speed is known to be eventually
zero.
Based on joint work with Sebastian Andres, Dominik Schmid and
Perla Sousi.
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
rec.speaker: Maxime Marivain
rec.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: À propos de la tessellation de Poisson-Delaunay : quelques techniques classiques et de nouveaux résultats de loi
rec.speaker: Cecilia d'Errico
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, nous présentons la tessellation de Delaunay issue d’un processus ponctuel de Poisson homogène sur Rd. Dans une première partie, nous parlerons de la cellule typique et montrerons comment obtenir sa loi à l’aide d’une technique 'combo'
classique : la formule de Mecke + changement de variable de Blaschke-Petkantschin. Dans la deuxième partie, nous étudions le volume de cette cellule : nous voyons comment obtenir ses moments, puis nous résolvons le problème des moments pour déterminer la loi
du volume de la cellule typique. Enfin, nous présenterons d’autres résultats de loi de fonctionnelles de la cellule typique que nous avons obtenus en étendant ces techniques.

rec.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
rec.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
rec.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?
rec.location_text: Salle B107
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 2)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.

rec.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
rec.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
rec.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: Minimal model for localization of topological Fukaya categories of surfaces
rec.speaker: Pierre BODIN
rec.abstract:
In the first half of this talk, I will present the construction of the topological Fukaya category of a graded marked surface, as introduced by Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich, and present some of its main properties.
In the second half, I will present a minimal model for the localization of this category at a spherical object corresponding to a simple closed curve on the surface. This new description will then be used to describe the indecomposable objects of the localization in terms of graded curves on the singular surface obtained by collapsing the simple closed curve to a point.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
rec.speaker: Serge Cantat
rec.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: Characterizing totally geodesic manifolds in negative curvature
rec.speaker: David Fisher
rec.abstract: The talk centers around the question of what invariant sets for Anosov flows and diffeomorphisms can look like. It is known that closed invariant sets can be arbitrarily bad and for example be fractals of arbitrary Hausdorff dimension. An old and interesting question, first raised by Hirsch in 1968 is what closed invariant submanifolds can look like. There are many surprising rigidity results in this direction, some quite old, and recently Rose Eliott Smith and I proved a new one, giving a dynamical characterization of totally geodesic submanifolds in negative curvature. I will explain the theorem and both the classical motivation and some more contemporary motivation. If time permits I will give some hints about the proof and particularly how it uses very old results from Smale and Mane.

Dans cette thèse, nous présenterons des asympotiques d'états cohérents propagés par une équation de Schrödinger associée à un Hamiltonien donné. Ces résultats étendent ceux obtenus par Combescure et Robert, dans lesquels un état cohérent propagé est approché dans la limite $h\to 0$ par des paquets gaussiens déformés dits états cohérents comprimés. Cette description reste valide pour des temps $t$ pouvant tendre vers l'infini quand $h\to 0$, dans le régime $|t|\leq |\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ où $\lambda_0$ est l'exposant de Lyapunov maximal de la dynamique classique. L'échec de cette approximation au temps $|\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ est relié à la flexion des paquets d'ondes évolués : une fois étalés à l'échelle $h^{1/3}$, les états comprimés ne founissent plus une description appropriée. Pour obtenir une représentation valide jusqu'à des temps $|t|\leq C|\log h|$ avec un plus grand $C$ (par exemple jusqu'au temps d'Ehrenfest $|\log h|/(2\lambda_0)$ où un étalement à des échelles macroscopiques est autorisé), on ajoute des hypothèses sur le flot $\Phi_t$ associé à la dynamique classique, imposant des contraintes sur les directions d'élongation. La description obtenue met en évidence que les états propagés ne doivent plus être considérés comme microlocalisés en un point mais plutôt le long d'une sous-variété isotrope (correspondant à des directions instables).
Ces résultats seront ensuite appliqués à l'étude de l'équation des ondes amorties sur une variété Anosov, on expliquera comment une telle asymptotique d'états cohérents propagés peut être utilisée pour obtenir des estimées de propagateurs, permettant d'obtenir un trou spectral et des estimées de résolvante pour l'opérateur associé, et ainsi de montrer la décroissance exponentielle de l'énergie des solutions.

imj-91.name: Séminaire Arithmetic Geometry Preprint Seminar
imj-91.department: Formes Automorphes; Théorie des Nombres; Topologie et Géométrie Algébriques
imj-91.organizers: Yves André, Javier Fresán, Wiesława Nizioł
imj-91.description: Souvent, il nous arrive de vouloir étudier en détail une prépublication qui nous intéresse particulièrement, peut-être décisive pour notre travail, mais d’autres tâches renvoient ce voeu aux calendes. Le but de ce séminaire est de nous inciter à réaliser ce voeu, en faisant aussi profiter tour à tour les collègues géomètres arithméticiens des efforts investis dans cette lecture. Il s’agira donc d’exposer, en deux heures, une prépublication significative d’autrui de son choix, devant un public varié de géomètres arithméticiens.

imj-95.description:
[K-OS] KNOT ONLINE SEMINAR
[K-OS] is an online research seminar which focuses on knot theory and low-dimensional topology. Talks will be delivered by authors of recent arXiv articles that made a breakthrough in our field. It happens the 3rd Thursday of months Thursdays from 16:00 to 17:00 (CET/CEST Berlin, Brussels, Madrid, Paris, Rome, Vienna, Warsaw, Zurich) on Zoom.
It is organized by Alexandra Kjuchukova, Lukas Lewark, Louis-Hadrien Robert and Emmanuel Wagner. It benefits from logistical support from the CNRS, the university of Paris and the university of Regensburg.

imj-96.name: Groupe de travail Preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau
imj-96.description:
Voici le calendrier du groupe de travail sur la preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau :
0) 24/01 Introduction générale : Conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel et morphismes de Lattès, stratégie de la preuve
1) 31/01 Analytification de Berkovich sur un corps valué complet et sur un anneau de Banach
2) 07/02 Théorie du (pluri)potentiel global sur les espaces de Berkovich : métriques FS, CPSH (continue psh), métrique d'équilibre d'un système dynamique polarisé (thèse de Pille-Schneider); sur un corps: mesures de MA de métriques CPSH, estimée de Chern-Levine-Nirenberg (Boucksom-Eriksson?)
3) 07/03 Continuité des mesures canoniques (Haar ou Dirac au point de Gauss) sur P^1 [I, Thm 6.8] et des mesures d'équilibre (via Chern-Levine-Nirenberg)
4) 21/03 Hauteurs, énergie mutuelle des mesures et continuité [II et Favre--Riviera-Letelier]
5) 04/04 Cas des Lattès : minoration centrale (énergie mutuelle d'intervalles en valuation triviale) et globale [II, section 6]
6) 18/04 Minoration globale de l'énergie mutuelle et fin de la preuve [II, sections 7-8]
Les séances auront lieu de 10h à 12h en salle 15.25.502 à Jussieu sauf pour le 24/1 qui aura lieu en salle 15.16.413.

m2fonda-gt-combi.name: GT M2 — Combinatoire et entropie
m2fonda-gt-combi.description: Entropy methods in additive combinatorics (Green–Manners–Tao, Hochman), Jan.–Feb. 2026.

m2fonda-gt-dag.name: GT M2 — Géométrie dérivée (DAG Jussieu working group)
m2fonda-gt-dag.description: Goal: postnikov towers of connective E∞-rings are square-zero extensions (Lurie, Higher Algebra 7.4.1.28). Weekly programme started 2 Oct 2025 (∞-categories, stable ∞-categories, E∞-rings, cotangent complex).

m2fonda-gt-dgt.name: GT M2 — Géométrie différentielle non lisse et applications
m2fonda-gt-dgt.description: Optimal transport, metric measure spaces, CD/RCD conditions and stability under lower Ricci bounds (Jan. 2026).

m2fonda-gt-groups.name: GT M2 — Groupes et courbure
m2fonda-gt-groups.description: Curvature and fundamental groups (Bonnet, Cartan–Hadamard, Preissmann, Milnor), then hyperbolic groups (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-hyper.name: GT M2 — Géométrie hyperkählérienne
m2fonda-gt-hyper.description: Holonomy and Berger's classification, Calabi–Yau, variations of Hodge structure, period map and global Torelli (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-k.name: GT M2 — K-théorie (groupe de lecture)
m2fonda-gt-k.description: Algebraic K-theory following Srinivas: K0, K1, K2, then higher K-groups via the plus and Q constructions (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-langlands.name: GT M2 — Langlands p-adique en dimension deux
m2fonda-gt-langlands.recurrence: Tuesdays 16:40–18:40, Jussieu 15-16-101 (as stated in the PDF of 4 Nov. 2025)
m2fonda-gt-langlands.description: p-adic Langlands for GL2(Qp): (φ,Γ)-modules, Fontaine rings, following Astérisque 319/330/331.

m2fonda-gt-mmp.name: GT M2 — Programme minimal
m2fonda-gt-mmp.description: Minimal model program; call for speakers (2025–26).

m2fonda-gt-rh.name: GT M2 — Correspondance de Riemann-Hilbert
m2fonda-gt-rh.description: Flat connections, local systems and representations of π1; Gauss–Manin connection; then regular singularities or D-modules (Nov. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-shen.name: Sujet proposé — Faisceaux cohérents et super-connexions
m2fonda-gt-shen.description: Topic proposed by Shu Shen (not yet organised): coherent sheaves, derived categories, antiholomorphic superconnections and Block's equivalence (Bismut–Shen–Wei).

m2fonda-gt-vss.name: GT M2 — Sexual and gender-based violence and discrimination working group
m2fonda-gt-vss.description: Student working group of the M2, 2025–2026 (presentation PDF updated 2025-12-16). Sessions are arranged among the participants and not published with dates.

paris-apres-midi-topologie.description: Afternoons of several topology talks announced in the LAGA topology seminar listing, e.g. « Après-midi parisienne de topologie » (8 Jan 2026, LAGA) and « Après-midi topologie algébrique » (26 Mar 2026, Sophie Germain). arxiv:2409.06064.title: Approximability of deep computations
arxiv:2409.06064.summary: This is the first of a series of papers in which we study deep computations (ultracomputations) and deep iterates, formalizing the ideas of "asymptotic limit" of computations and compositional iterates, respectively. In this first paper of the series, we characterize deep computations that are bona fide computable, and prove the existence of deep equilibria, which hitherto have been found only empirically in deep learning. A subsequent paper will study the complexity of ultracomputations.
arxiv:2409.06064.authors: Samson Alva, Eduardo Due\~nez, Jose Iovino, Claire Walton

arxiv:2610.22000.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
arxiv:2610.22000.summary: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which leads to new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is 1-Frobenius.
arxiv:2610.22000.authors: Jingcheng Dong, Sebastien Palcoux, Arnaud Plessis

arxiv:2610.27198.title: DeGroot Dynamics on Multiplex Networks with Directed and Acyclic Interlayer Connectivities
arxiv:2610.27198.summary: In models of opinion dynamics, researchers typically examine how an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced by the opinions of their neighbors in a network. However, people's opinions on a topic are also influenced by their opinions and their neighbors' opinions on related topics. In an election, for example, the opinions of a voter on a variety of issues inform their opinions of electoral candidates.
arxiv:2610.27198.authors: Mia Zender, Kye Shi, Abigail Hickok, Weiqi Chu, Mason A. Porter

arxiv:2610.28446.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
arxiv:2610.28446.summary: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class.

arxiv:2610.28635.title: Model-based computational study of reactive fluid systems using transfer operator methods
arxiv:2610.28635.summary: In many industrial applications one aims for the design of efficient chemical reactions. This is often done using experimental analysis of the reactors in combination with numerical twins. However, the simultaneous modeling of flow, mixing and chemical reaction remains a complicated task because the computational costs are still significant and oftentimes prohibitive.
arxiv:2610.28635.authors: Anja G\"obel, Anna Kl\"unker, Alexandra von Kameke, Kathrin Padberg-Gehle

arxiv:2610.28657.title: Ideal balanced pairs in n-exangulated categories
arxiv:2610.28657.summary: This paper is devoted to ideal approximation theory in $n$-exangulated categories. We define ideal balanced pairs and explore their properties and equivalent characterizations. We prove that any complete ideal cotorsion triple $(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{K},\mathcal{J})$ satisfying suitable assumptions yields an ideal balanced pair $(\mathcal{I}, \mathcal{J})$, and the converse holds under additional hypotheses.
arxiv:2610.28657.authors: Peiyu Zhang, Zhuolin Zheng, Li Wang, Dajun Liu

arxiv:2610.28672.title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of the Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
arxiv:2610.28672.summary: We study the analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.

arxiv:2610.28691.title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
arxiv:2610.28691.summary: We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both constructed from the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. The first consists of affine moments of ordinary powers. For fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<\beta<1$, we prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity in the polynomial variable by a continuant comparison criterion.

arxiv:2610.28715.title: Low-Dimensional Reduction of Mean-Field Coupled Dynamical Systems with Units Described by Two Real Variables: Classification and Applications
arxiv:2610.28715.summary: Low-dimensional reduction is crucial for understanding network systems with many units. In a recent advance, Martens and Dharmavaram developed a theory of exact low-dimensional reduction for a general class of mean-field coupled dynamical systems characterized by a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure. In this paper, we classify mean-field coupled dynamical systems with a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, where each unit is described by two real variables.

arxiv:2610.28780.title: Low-degree filtrations in ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology
arxiv:2610.28780.summary: We prove the Hilbert-series formulas conjectured by Reiner--Tudose and by the Polymath Jr. Grassmannian group for the subalgebras of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology generated in bounded degree. We determine the finite coefficient images underlying the proofs, together with the kernels of the coefficient and cancellation maps.

arxiv:2610.28792.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
arxiv:2610.28792.summary: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.

arxiv:2610.28809.title: The moduli space of maps from hypersurfaces and its Goodwillie tower
arxiv:2610.28809.summary: We define a moduli space of continuous maps from smooth hypersurfaces varying in an ample linear system. To study its topology, we construct a scanning map to an appropriate section space and investigate its effect on homology. Our main innovation is a general argument based on Goodwillie calculus and applicable to various moduli spaces of maps.

arxiv:2610.28813.title: Embeddings of Relative Dimension Groups for Zero-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
arxiv:2610.28813.summary: Let $\pi:(X,T)\rightarrow(Y,S)$ be a factor map between zero-dimensional dynamical systems, and let $X_0$ and $Y_0$ be quasi-sections with $\pi(X_0)=Y_0$. We study the homomorphism $\pi^*:K^0(Y|Y_0,S)\rightarrow K^0(X|X_0,T)$, $[f]\mapsto[f\circ\pi]$, between the corresponding relative dimension groups, and identify it with the homomorphism induced by the premorphism between Bratteli--Vershik realizations associated with $\pi$. Generalizing a result of Glasner and Weiss for minimal Cantor systems, we show that if $Y_0$ is quasi-simple, then $\pi^*$ is an injective unital order-preserving homomorphism, and that if $X_0=\pi^{-1}(Y_0)$, then $\pi^*$ is a unital order embedding; the latter…

arxiv:2610.28820.title: A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
arxiv:2610.28820.summary: We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual.
arxiv:2610.28820.authors: Daniella Bar-Lev, Hiram H. L\'opez, Gretchen L. Matthews, Flavio Salizzoni

arxiv:2610.28828.title: A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
arxiv:2610.28828.summary: It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.

arxiv:2610.28839.title: On a conjecture of Velani
arxiv:2610.28839.summary: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg.

arxiv:2610.28861.title: From Wheel to Jahangir graphs: spectra and energy under structured edge deletion
arxiv:2610.28861.summary: The energy of a graph, introduced by Gutman, is defined as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. In this work we study how the energy of the Wheel graph $W_n$ changes when a specific set of spokes is removed. The resulting graphs are precisely the Jahangir graphs $J_{m,n}$, where m divides n, and which may also be viewed as the Cycle graph $C_n$ together with an additional vertex adjacent to certain vertices of $C_n$ in a cyclic pattern.
arxiv:2610.28861.authors: Diego Bravo, Florencia Cubr\'ia, Annabella Zapattini

arxiv:2610.28865.title: Tree-independence number VIII. 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number
arxiv:2610.28865.summary: A three-path-configuration is a graph consisting of three pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths, the union of every two of which is an induced cycle of length at least four. A graph is 3PC-free if no induced subgraph of it is a three-path-configuration. We show that 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number, which is asymptotically best possible.
arxiv:2610.28865.authors: Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Ajaykrishnan E S, Daniel Lokshtanov, Ilya Maier

arxiv:2610.28874.title: A sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines
arxiv:2610.28874.summary: We construct a sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines in the real projective plane. It is obtained from the icosahedral arrangement $\mathcal{A}(21,2)$ by adjoining the $30$ images of the line $y+\sqrt{\varphi}\,z=0$ under the rotation group of the icosahedron, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Its intersection multiplicities are $t_2=120$, $t_3=190$, $t_5=36$, and $t_6=15$, with all other $t_r$ zero.

arxiv:2610.28936.title: The domination number of the $k$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$
arxiv:2610.28936.summary: This paper is about token graphs and domination number. Let $G=(X,E)$ denote an undirected graph that is connected, with no loops or multiple edges, vertex set $X$, and edge set $E$. Pick a positive integer $k\leq \vert X\vert$.
arxiv:2610.28936.authors: Nathaniel Chinman, Antonio Cortijo, Beatrice Pedroni, Ian Seong, Lucy Stenger

arxiv:2610.28959.title: Polynomial Invariants of Pseudo-Anosov Maps (Addendum)
arxiv:2610.28959.summary: We show that homology, puncture, and symplectic polynomials of a pseudo-Anosov map arXiv:1001.5094 are invariants of the mapping class, as well as of the conjugacy class.

arxiv:2610.28960.title: Same Gaps, Different Sets: A Survey on Complimentary sets and their Dimensions
arxiv:2610.28960.summary: Let a=\{a_n\} be a non-increasing sequence of positive real numbers adding up to $1$. Cutting out of the unit interval disjoint open gaps of lengths $a_1,a_2,\dots$, one for each term, leaves a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero, and since the gaps can be placed in infinitely many ways, there are infinitely many such sets. We call them the \emph{complementary sets} of $a$ and write $\mathfrak{C}_a$ for the family of all of them.
arxiv:2610.28960.authors: Nicol\'as Angelini, Carlos Cabrelli, Ursula Molter

arxiv:2610.28963.title: Asymptotics of Masur-Veech volume of strata of quadratic differentials with many simple poles
arxiv:2610.28963.summary: We provide large $n$ asymptotics of the Masur-Veech volumes for strata of quadratic differentials of the form $\mathcal{Q}_g(n,d_1,\dots,d_k,-1^{n+D-4g+4})$, where all positive integers $d_i$ are fixed and $D=d_1+\dots+d_k$. Our formulae are particularly explicit in genus $1$. For the two series of non-varying strata $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,-1^n)$ and $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,1,-1^{n+1})$ we give simple closed formulae for the volumes for any $n$.

arxiv:2610.28986.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
arxiv:2610.28986.summary: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi (k-1)}{k}}\}$.

arxiv:2610.29011.title: Affine $G$-multibiquandle modules for colored links I: representability of coloring functors and color-profile polynomials
arxiv:2610.29011.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $G$ be an abelian group, and fix $u\in R[G]^\times$. For each component-labeled oriented link diagram $(D,\sigma)$, we construct a finitely presented $R[G]$-module $M_u(D,\sigma;R[G])$ with a universal affine coloring $U_{D,\sigma}$. Every affine coloring with values in an $R[G]$-module factors uniquely through $U_{D,\sigma}$ by a module homomorphism.

arxiv:2610.29015.title: On the Number of Iterations in a Kruskal-Type Process
arxiv:2610.29015.summary: Motivated by the Kruskal counting procedure, this paper investigates a combinatorial elimination process defined on a deck consisting of $m$ copies of each value $1,2,\ldots,n$. Starting from an arbitrary arrangement of the $mn$ cards, the process repeatedly removes a number of consecutive cards equal to the value of the first remaining card. This generates a sequence of elimination steps whose length determines $T$, representing the total number of iterations required to exhaust the deck.

arxiv:2610.29039.title: Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning the Flow of Autonomous Systems by Conjugation to Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows
arxiv:2610.29039.summary: We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE $\dot x=f(x)$ as a conjugate $\Phi_t=F_\theta^{-1}\circ\Psi_t\circ F_\theta$ of an explicitly integrable reference flow $\Psi_t$ by an invertible neural network $F_\theta$, the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A $C^1$ conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of $\Psi$.

arxiv:2610.29043.title: Every tournament of dichromatic number $10 k^2$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood has dichromatic number more than $k$
arxiv:2610.29043.summary: The dichromatic number of a tournament is the minimum number of colors needed to color the vertices so that no directed cycle is monochromatic. Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour (2025) asked whether every tournament with dichromatic number $2k$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number at least $k$. We answer their question negatively by finding an example with dichromatic number $\Omega(k^2)$.

arxiv:2610.29044.title: Non-trivial intersecting families for direct products
arxiv:2610.29044.summary: A family of sets is intersecting if any two of its sets intersect, and non-trivial intersecting if there is not any element which appears in every set of the family. The study of intersection problems (or Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado problems) on families of sets is one of the most important topics in extremal combinatorics. A natural extension of the Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado problem in direct products setting was introduced by Frankl, and developed by Alon and Katona et al.
arxiv:2610.29044.authors: Jian Wang, Biao Wu, Huajun Zhang

arxiv:2610.29048.title: Proofs of Li, Wang and Guo's conjectures on (signless) Laplacian spectral radius
arxiv:2610.29048.summary: Let $\mu(G)$ and $q(G)$ be the Laplacian and signless Laplacian spectral radii of a graph $G$. Li, Wang and Guo (2026) conjectured that, if $H$ with $|V(H)|\geq 1$ is an induced subgraph of a graph $G$, then $\mu(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}\mu(H_v^t)$ and $q(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}q(H_v^t)$, where $t=e(G)-e(H)$ and $H_v^t$ is the graph obtained from $H$ by adding $t$ pendant edges to $v\in V(H)$. We prove this conjecture by establishing a spectral comparison theorem for a broader family of positive semidefinite graph matrices which includes the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices.
arxiv:2610.29048.authors: Hongzhang Chen, Jianxi Li, Xiaoyun Lv

arxiv:2610.29056.title: General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into $\omega$-Chains
arxiv:2610.29056.summary: Given a poset $P$ with no maximal element the question naturally arises of when $P$ can be partitioned into $\omega$-chains. In this paper we give general criterion for when this can be done. We show that in the case when a poset with no maximal element is countable or a well-founded forest, then it can always be partitioned into $\omega$-chains.

arxiv:2610.29065.title: Pontryagin-Thom, $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors
arxiv:2610.29065.summary: Segal computed $\pi_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(\Gamma_k)$ of finite \'etale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(\Gamma_k)\to\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation.

arxiv:2610.29080.title: Pappus configurations in the Hall plane
arxiv:2610.29080.summary: In this paper, we investigate Pappus configurations in the finite affine Hall plane. In particular, we show that for any two lines $\ell_1,\ell_2$ and for any triple of points on $\ell_1$ there is a triple of points on $\ell_2$ that are contained in a Pappus configuration, thus improving on the results of [F. Lazebnik and L.
arxiv:2610.29080.authors: Stefano Lia, John Sheekey, Geertrui Van de Voorde

arxiv:2610.29115.title: On a conjecture concerning two-stack sortable permutations
arxiv:2610.29115.summary: The two-stack sortable permutations of length $n$ are known to be equinumerous with permutations of length $n$ avoiding the dashed patterns $3\text{-}1\text{-}4\text{-}2$ and $2\text{-}41\text{-}3$. In this paper, we confirm an intriguing conjecture posed by Claesson, Kitaev, and Steingr\'imsson, which asserts that the quadruple $(\comp,\asc,\ldr,\rmax)$ is equidistributed on these two permutation classes. Here $\comp$ and $\asc$ count the number of components and ascents, respectively, $\ldr$ denotes the length of the initial decreasing run, and $\rmax$ denotes the number of right-to-left maxima.
arxiv:2610.29115.authors: Yongzhou Wen, Sherry H. F. Yan

arxiv:2610.29125.title: Integer Flows on Cyclic Covers of Graphs
arxiv:2610.29125.summary: Graph covers preserve the local structure of a graph while allowing its global structure to change substantially. In this paper, we study how such changes in cyclic covers affect nowhere-zero flow properties. For a fixed integer $\ell \ge 2$, we show that for every bridgeless graph $G$, there exists an $\ell$-fold cyclic cover of $G$ that admits a nowhere-zero $3$-flow if $\ell$ is even and a nowhere-zero $4$-flow if $\ell$ is odd.
arxiv:2610.29125.authors: Rong Luo, Yuying Ma, D. Christopher Stephens, Dong Ye

arxiv:2610.29130.title: $G$-crossed braided tensor categories of twisted modules
arxiv:2610.29130.summary: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. We prove Huang's conjecture that the categories of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, for $g\in G$, form a $G$-crossed braided fusion category. This category is faithfully $G$-graded, with tensor products representing the complete twisted intertwining operators of Du-Huang, the canonical pullback $G$-action, and crossed braiding.

arxiv:2610.29131.title: Small covers and the Four Color Theorem
arxiv:2610.29131.summary: We give a combinatorial proof that every simple convex $3$-polytope admits a small cover without using the Four Color Theorem. We also prove that the assertion that every simple plane triangulation admits a mod~$2$ characteristic function with at most five values is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem.

arxiv:2610.29197.title: The Local Dyadic Conjecture
arxiv:2610.29197.summary: A rational with denominator a power of two is said to be dyadic. A long standing conjecture of Paul Seymour predicts that for an ideal clutter, the dual of the set covering problem always admits an optimal solution where all variables take dyadic values. We present a local version of this conjecture, and motivate it by proving an important special case.
arxiv:2610.29197.authors: Mahtab Alghasi, Bertrand Guenin, Levent Tun\c{c}el

arxiv:2610.29204.title: The Logarithmic A-Discriminant
arxiv:2610.29204.summary: We extend the GKZ theory of discriminants to the setting of Euler integrals where both coefficients and exponents are variables. The integrand is the likelihood function of a toric model in algebraic statistics, whose number of critical points is the volume of the Newton polytope. Our logarithmic A-discriminant vanishes when two critical points come together.
arxiv:2610.29204.authors: Madeleine Goertz, Bernd Sturmfels, Simon Telen

arxiv:2610.29211.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
arxiv:2610.29211.summary: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field.
arxiv:2610.29211.authors: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

arxiv:2610.29215.title: Third and Fourth Moment Phenomena for Monochromatic Edges and Applications to Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
arxiv:2610.29215.summary: Given a graph sequence $\{G_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, denote by $T_n$ the number of monochromatic edges when the vertices of $G_n$ are independently colored red or blue with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, respectively. We characterize the asymptotic normality of $T_n$, after centering and scaling to unit variance, in terms of subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments. One of the highlights of our results is a {\it third moment phenomenon}: for every fixed $p\in(0,1)\backslash\{\frac12\}$, asymptotic normality holds if and only if the standardized third moment converges to zero.
arxiv:2610.29215.authors: Siva Athreya, Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya, Yogesh Dahiya, Karambir Das, Spandan Ghoshal, Sourish Maniyar, Elizabeth Sara Roy

arxiv:2610.29233.title: Bistable Dynamics and Complete Classifications of A Seasonal Competition Model Between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
arxiv:2610.29233.summary: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable.
arxiv:2610.29233.authors: Lei Niu, Yi Wang, Xizhuang Xie, Bo Zheng

arxiv:2610.29239.title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
arxiv:2610.29239.summary: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $\pi_n\star\pi_m\cong\pi_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups.

arxiv:2610.29263.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
arxiv:2610.29263.summary: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty.
arxiv:2610.29263.authors: Indranil Biswas, Satyajit Guin, Pradip Kumar

arxiv:2610.29274.title: Nielsen coincidence theory for $(n,m)$-valued pairs
arxiv:2610.29274.summary: We define a Nielsen coincidence number for pairs of maps $(f,g)$ where $f$ is $n$-valued and $g$ is $m$-valued. The classical definition of the Nielsen number does not work in this setting, but we propose a theory where coincidence classes are allowed to overlap. We invoke a notion of multiplicity of a coincidence point, which indicates to how many classes it can belong, and we show that our Nielsen number is a homotopy-invariant lower bound for the number of coincidence points with multiplicity.

arxiv:2610.29275.title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
arxiv:2610.29275.summary: Let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$ with $p$ prime, and write $e=\nu_p(d)$. Ward conjectured that $C$ is $p^{\max\{0,e-f+1\}}$-divisible. In this paper, we prove this conjecture.

arxiv:2610.29291.title: Counting and constructing Latin tableaux
arxiv:2610.29291.summary: Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares to Young diagrams and have interesting connections to linear algebra and Rota's basis conjecture. Conjecturally, a partition admits Latin tableaux if and only if it belongs to a special class called wide partitions. We prove that various classes of wide partitions admit Latin tableaux.
arxiv:2610.29291.authors: Spencer Daugherty, Michaela Fahnesock, Shawn Huxtable, Michael Larson, Nourah Al Munayes, Storey Peacock

arxiv:2610.29307.title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
arxiv:2610.29307.summary: We prove effective stability and matching logarithmic upper bounds for small solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs on the one-dimensional torus. An analytic coefficient-majorant calculus and an explicit normal-form iteration yield stability times with logarithms of order $L^{1+1/p}/(\log L)^{1/p}$ for Gevrey weights and $L^{1+(q-1)/(pq+1)}$ for logarithmic ultra-differentiable weights, where $L=\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $p\geq1$ measures the order dependence of the small divisors. Even frequencies are organized into the exact blocks $\{n,-n\}$; elementary frequency gaps and constant weights on these blocks close the energy estimate.

arxiv:2610.29360.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
arxiv:2610.29360.summary: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections.

arxiv:2610.29469.title: An entropy proof of the commonality of apices of trees
arxiv:2610.29469.summary: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-colouring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random colouring with an equal proportion of each colour. Grzesik, Lee, Lidick\'y and Volec conjectured that every $k$-apex of any connected Sidorenko graph is common. Recently, Kr{\'a}l', Krnc and Lamaison proved that the $k$-apex of any tree is common for $k\leq 5$.

arxiv:2610.29485.title: Frequency Structure of AMM Liquidity Pools: A Multiresolution Analysis of Regime Transitions
arxiv:2610.29485.summary: This study examines the temporal structure of liquidity pools in constant-product automated market makers.
