arxiv:2610.31109.summary: Let a finite simple graph be given. We study symmetric matrices with this graph pattern that admit a null vector with prescribed exact support. Such a vector exists precisely when its support is a fort, meaning that no vertex outside the support has exactly one neighbor inside it.

arxiv:2610.31128.title: Open dynamics with a moving hole: inhomogeneous IFS and exponential separation condition
arxiv:2610.31128.summary: Let $\mathcal F=\{f_i(x)=r_i x+t_i\}_{i=0}^{b-1}$ be a self-similar iterated function system (IFS) on $\mathbb R$ with $b\ge 3$, and let $K_{\mathcal F}$ be the associated self-similar set. Given $m\in\mathbb N$, for any sequence $\omega=\omega^0\omega^1\ldots$ with each $\omega^i\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^m$ a block of length $m$, let \[ K_{\mathcal F}^\omega:=\pi_{\mathcal F}\left(\{(d_i)\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}: d_{k+1}d_{k+2}\ldots d_{k+m}\ne\omega^k\quad\forall k\ge 0\}\right), \] where $\pi_{\mathcal F}$ is the natural coding map from $\{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}$ to $K_{\mathcal F}$. The set $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ is called the survivor set of an open dynamical system with…
arxiv:2610.31128.authors: Derong Kong, Kun Li, Cai-Yun Ma, K\'{a}roly Simon

arxiv:2610.31138.title: Zero Forcing on Maximal Outerplanar Graphs: Capacities and Phase Repair
arxiv:2610.31138.summary: We determine the zero-forcing number of maximal biconnected outerplanar graphs. When the weak dual is a path, the zero-forcing number and the induced path-covering number are both two. Otherwise, the branching faces determine a canonical core and a family of terminal strips.

arxiv:2610.31150.title: Gamma conjectures for Milnor hypersurfaces
arxiv:2610.31150.summary: We prove Gamma conjectures I and II of Galkin, Golyshev and Iritani for Milnor hypersurfaces, the smooth hypersurfaces of bidegree $(1,1)$ in the product of two projective spaces. We provide a criterion for Gamma conjecture II for general Fano manifolds, generalizing the criterion by Hu and Ke. Using the mirror symmetry technique of Galkin and Iritani, we establish global Gamma-I for Milnor hypersurfaces, thereby proving Gamma conjecture I as a special case.
arxiv:2610.31150.authors: Jianxun Hu, Hua-Zhong Ke, Changzheng Li, Jiayu Song

arxiv:2610.31174.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
arxiv:2610.31174.summary: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

arxiv:2610.31212.title: An algebraic proof of 1-extension
arxiv:2610.31212.summary: We give a new proof that 1-extension preserves generic local rigidity of bar-joint frameworks in all dimensions. The proof does not use a special position argument, which makes the approach potentially useful for X-replacement in 3-space. Instead, the balancing conditions recently introduced by the first author use directed paths in the line graph, and by modifying the end of these paths, we transfer a self-stress on the 1-extended graph back to the original.

arxiv:2610.31233.title: Positivity of supercritical LYZ pairs
arxiv:2610.31233.summary: We introduce the roots of supercritical Leung--Yau--Zaslow pairs and prove pointwise strong positivity of the associated Schur forms. The resulting LYZ cones contain the pliant cone on smooth projective threefolds, with strict inclusion on a Fujino--Sato threefold. We also establish Hard Lefschetz and Hodge--Riemann relations for the associated Chern classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds in bidegrees $1\le p+q\le\dim X$ with $\min\{p,q\}\le1$.
arxiv:2610.31233.authors: Bowen Liu, Mao Sheng, Shing-Tung Yau

arxiv:2610.31241.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
arxiv:2610.31241.summary: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.

arxiv:2610.31250.title: Three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds
arxiv:2610.31250.summary: We give a construction of the previously announced family of three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds of Euler degree $72$. We prove that their defining $\mathbb{Z}$-algebras are Koszul and Artin--Schelter regular, and compute the Hilbert series of their section algebras.

arxiv:2610.31265.title: Log blow-ups and global resolutions in rigid geometry
arxiv:2610.31265.summary: In this article, we study log blow-ups in the setting of log adic spaces. As in the theory of log schemes, we prove the existence of global resolutions of toric singularities for fs log adic spaces log smooth over a $p$-adic field, and the acyclicity of certain sheaves under log blow-ups. One new feature of (log) rigid analytic varieties is their integral structure sheaf: we prove that it is also almost acyclic under log blow-ups in the Kummer \'etale topology.

arxiv:2610.31289.title: Cohomology of integral structure sheaves for open varieties
arxiv:2610.31289.summary: We study the cohomology of integral structure sheaves for two types of open rigid analytic varieties: complements of divisors in quasi-compact varieties, and partially proper spaces. As applications, we prove a strengthened form of the Hebbarkeitssatz (Riemann's extension theorem), involving the almost vanishing of $R^1\lim$, and study pro-\'etale $G$-torsors on open varieties.

arxiv:2610.31295.title: Model Predictive Control of Wind Turbines: A Model-Oriented Review of Prediction Models, Control Objectives, and Nonlinear Aerodynamic Formulations
arxiv:2610.31295.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to wind-turbine regulation with markedly different internal prediction models, ranging from linearized low-order turbine models to nonlinear, aeroelastic, floating, and data-driven predictors. This review organizes the literature primarily by the model propagated by the controller and treats model order, predictor representation, MPC formulation, control objective, and validation plant as separate descriptors. Primary studies show that low-order linear or piecewise-affine predictors are attractive for constrained power and speed regulation, whereas flexible drivetrain, structural, and floating models are needed when drivetrain twist, tower…
arxiv:2610.31295.authors: Roya Khalili-Amirabadi, Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani, Mahdi Ghane

arxiv:2610.31301.title: Mathematical AI Predicts 40% and 57% Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against H1N1 and H3N2, Respectively, for the 2026--2027 U.S. Season
arxiv:2610.31301.summary: Background: Clinical influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) has often been low over the past two decades, highlighting the need for preseason VE forecasting. Timely forecasts could help health authorities plan prevention strategies and allocate healthcare resources. However, preseason forecasting of clinical influenza VE remains relatively uncommon.

arxiv:2610.31327.title: Typical periodic optimization and freezing phase transition: Dini potentials and beyond
arxiv:2610.31327.summary: We investigate the Typical Periodic Optimization (TPO) Conjecture and freezing phase transitions for Dini potentials and beyond. We show that the TPO conjecture fails already at Dini regularity. We identify a sharp regularity threshold for freezing phase transitions, which we call weak log-log Dini.
arxiv:2610.31327.authors: Yunping Jiang, Zhiqiang Li, Yiqing Sun

arxiv:2610.31358.title: Sum-rank analogues of Reed--Muller codes over Abelian Galois extensions
arxiv:2610.31358.summary: Let $\mathbb L/\mathbb K$ be a finite Abelian Galois extension with a fixed decomposition $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb L/\mathbb K)=\langle\sigma_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langle\sigma_m\rangle$. We show that the quotient of the multivariate skew polynomial ring $\mathbb L[x_1,\ldots,x_m;\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m]$ by suitable central polynomials $H_1(x_1),\ldots,H_m(x_m)$ is isomorphic to a product of $t$ copies of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb K}(\mathbb L)$, so that one skew polynomial represents all blocks of a sum-rank metric space. The sum-rank weight of an element equals the rank of an associated Dickson matrix and of a generalized Moore matrix.

arxiv:2610.31362.title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: $S(6)\ge 537$
arxiv:2610.31362.summary: We give an explicit partition of $\{1,\ldots,537\}$ into six sum-free sets, establishing $S(6)\ge 537$. This improves the lower bound 536 of Fredricksen and Sweet (2000). Known recursive constructions then give the improved lower bounds $S(8)\ge 5\,372$, $S(11)\ge 204\,208$, $S(13)\ge 2\,042\,082$, and $R_6(3)\ge 539$.
arxiv:2610.31362.authors: Zhiyang Chen, Ligeng Zhu, Fan Long

arxiv:2610.31379.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
arxiv:2610.31379.summary: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$.

arxiv:2610.31391.title: Bridging persistence of discrete and continuous 1D maps: Total variation, permutation equivalence, and diagonal affine transformations
arxiv:2610.31391.summary: Fundamental to the field of topological signal processing (TSP) is the \textit{persistence diagram} (PD), or barcode, of a signal, which gives noise-resistant measures of topologically significant features as distinct from noise. Existing literature proves that the total persistence computed from these diagrams is equal to the total variation, for certain continuous signals on compact domains. We provide a closed formula for this shared quantity, and generalize to all continuous and discrete functions on bounded domains, and to certain functions on non-compact 1D manifolds.

arxiv:2610.31398.title: Control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems
arxiv:2610.31398.summary: This monograph presents a selection of the author's recent works on the control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. After a detailed introduction to topics related to time-delay systems covered in the monograph, its main contents are presented in a series of mostly independent chapters.

arxiv:2610.31399.title: An asymptotic $\Gamma$-BMT inequality
arxiv:2610.31399.summary: We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $\Gamma$-Bayer-Macr\`i-Toda ($\Gamma$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization.

arxiv:2610.31410.title: The symmetric skew monoidal structure of Gray-categories
arxiv:2610.31410.summary: In a previous paper, we constructed a closed skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories and Gray-functors whose internal hom Psd(A, B) captures pseudomaps and pseudo-transformations. In the present paper we give a symmetric description of the Gray-category Psd(A,B) and use this to prove that the skew monoidal structure is symmetric skew monoidal.

arxiv:2610.31411.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
arxiv:2610.31411.summary: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.

arxiv:2610.31440.title: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets
arxiv:2610.31440.summary: Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution.
arxiv:2610.31440.authors: Derong Kong, Cai-Yun Ma, K\'{a}roly Simon

arxiv:2610.31442.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
arxiv:2610.31442.summary: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.

arxiv:2610.31448.title: Semi-strict 4-categories as enriched categories
arxiv:2610.31448.summary: We introduce several flavours of semi-strict 4-category as enriched categories. We give the axioms for semi-strict 4-categories in elementary terms and describe a wide range of examples. In particular, we answer the question of what exactly Gray-categories and the higher transformations between them form: namely, a left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$.

arxiv:2610.31460.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
arxiv:2610.31460.summary: Let $u$ be a received word for the full-length Reed--Solomon code $\operatorname{RS}_q(k)$, with interpolation polynomial $f_u$ of degree $k+m$. For each $m\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, we classify all such deep holes over every finite field, without a field-size hypothesis. None occur for odd $m$ in this range.

arxiv:2610.31475.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
arxiv:2610.31475.summary: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.

arxiv:2610.31485.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions I: Algebra, geometry, and a spin model
arxiv:2610.31485.summary: We introduce a family of five-dimensional non-flexible quadratic real algebras $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ with canonical basis $1,i,j,k,\ell$, in which $\gamma$ changes the multiplication but not their norm, and study how this change affects geometry and dynamics. The algebras are pairwise non-isomorphic, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra, and $\mathcal A_1$ is the Pentarnion algebra. The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_\gamma v,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_\gamma\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle…

arxiv:2610.31497.title: A semiampleness result for hyperk\"ahler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
arxiv:2610.31497.summary: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperk\"ahler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.
arxiv:2610.31497.authors: Andreas H\"oring, Vladimir Lazi\'c, Christian Lehn

arxiv:2610.31499.title: Water Transport on 3-Spiders: Unbounded Lengths of Shortest Optimal Strategies
arxiv:2610.31499.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. An averaging operation selects a nonempty connected vertex set and replaces the weights of its vertices by their arithmetic mean. For a nonnegative initial weight function $\omega:V(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ and a target vertex $x$, let $t(G,x,\omega)$ denote the minimum number of averaging operations needed to attain the maximum reachable weight at $x$.
arxiv:2610.31499.authors: Guanheng Chen, Ran Tao, Tianyi Tao

arxiv:2610.31513.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
arxiv:2610.31513.summary: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods.
arxiv:2610.31513.authors: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

arxiv:2610.31516.title: Functions determining $(q+3)/2$ directions over the finite field with $q$ elements
arxiv:2610.31516.summary: Let $q=p^n$, where $p>2$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-set $U\subseteq\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ determining exactly $(q+3)/2$ directions is affinely equivalent to the graph of $x^{(q+1)/2}$. For $n\ge2$, we also prove that a $q$-set determining at most $(q+p)/2$ directions is either an affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear set or affinely equivalent to this graph.

arxiv:2610.31530.title: Polytopal substitutions and conformal dimension
arxiv:2610.31530.summary: We introduce polytopal substitutions, a recursive procedure for constructing polyhedral approximations of self-similar topological spaces. For a class of substitutions called sub-hyperbolic, we show that the limit of these approximations is naturally homeomorphic to the limit space of the associated iterated monodromy group. We establish a relationship between the $\ell^p$-contraction coefficients of sub-hyperbolic substitutions and the conformal dimension of their limit spaces.

arxiv:2610.31533.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
arxiv:2610.31533.summary: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the…

arxiv:2610.31556.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
arxiv:2610.31556.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor\frac{d-1}{2}\rfloor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel.

arxiv:2610.31557.title: The domination number of the 2-token graph of the complete bipartite graph
arxiv:2610.31557.summary: For a graph $G$, the $2$-token graph $F_2(G)$ has as vertices all $2$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two such subsets adjacent whenever their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper, we determine the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, for all integers $2\le m\le n$. We show that it equals $\lceil m/2\rceil+n-1$, except when $m=3$, or when $m\ge5$ is odd and $n=m+1$; in these two exceptional situations it is one less.
arxiv:2610.31557.authors: E. Acosta Troncoso, I. Caldera Caldera, L. M. Rivera

arxiv:2610.31589.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
arxiv:2610.31589.summary: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges.

arxiv:2610.31590.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
arxiv:2610.31590.summary: For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{\Delta/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $\Delta \geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In contrast, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to…

arxiv:2610.31599.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
arxiv:2610.31599.summary: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.

arxiv:2610.31600.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
arxiv:2610.31600.summary: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous.
arxiv:2610.31600.authors: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

arxiv:2610.31602.title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
arxiv:2610.31602.summary: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval.

arxiv:2610.31607.title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
arxiv:2610.31607.summary: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $\lambda_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function.
arxiv:2610.31607.authors: Vassily Gorbounov, Christian Korff, Leonardo C. Mihalcea

arxiv:2610.31618.title: The Asymptotic Number of Anticodes in Hamming Spaces
arxiv:2610.31618.summary: In the Hamming space $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, a $d$-anticode is a subset in which every pair of points has Hamming distance at most $d$, or equivalently, a set of diameter at most $d$. Let $m_q(n,d)$ denote the maximum size of a $d$-anticode and let $\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)$ be the family of all $d$-anticodes. We show that for fixed $q$, as $n\to\infty$, the total number of $d$-anticodes satisfies \[ |\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)|=2^{(1+o(1))m_q(n,d)} \] for $4\le d\le n-1$, except when $q=2$ and $d=n-1$.

arxiv:2610.31619.title: Leafrians, Poisson structures, and Frobenius splittings on moduli spaces
arxiv:2610.31619.summary: The Poisson $T$-Pfaffians of Bott--Samelson varieties, $G/U$, and $G/B$ produce Frobenius splittings, but only by a local, coordinate-bound argument. We isolate the local mechanism: a weighted trace pairing on the deformation space of a fat point, whose top coefficient factors over the blocks. At the members of a presentation, polyvector fields on the base $X$ transfer to the moduli space $M$.

arxiv:2610.31628.title: Almost simple subgroups of the space Cremona group
arxiv:2610.31628.summary: We prove that every finite almost simple subgroup that is not simple of the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space is isomorphic to one of the following: $\mathfrak{S}_5$, $\mathfrak{S}_6$, $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$. We also prove that the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space contains unique (up to conjugation) subgroups isomorphic to $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$.

arxiv:2610.31638.title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
arxiv:2610.31638.summary: Does computing a composition of total Boolean functions require the product of the randomized query complexities of its factors? We give a negative answer. There are families of total functions $f,g$ such that $R(f\circ g) =\Theta\!\left(\frac1{\log R(g)}\right)R(f)R(g)$ This result requires first separating linearized query complexity $\LR$, as well as noisy randomized query complexity $noisyR$, from standard randomized query complexity $R$.

arxiv:2610.31654.title: On the Concordance Invariants of Cable Links
arxiv:2610.31654.summary: We study the Beliakova--Wehrli link $s$-invariant and Cavallo's link $\tau$-invariant of coherently oriented cables. For knots satisfying extremal four-ball genus and maximal self-linking hypotheses, we establish bounds for the $s$-invariant of $(p,q)$-cables, where $p$ and $q$ are not necessarily coprime, and show that these bounds are sharp under certain conditions. For the $\tau$-invariant, we prove analogous bounds for arbitrary companion knots and exact formulas whenever $\tau(K)=\pm g_4(K)\ne 0$.

arxiv:2610.31655.title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
arxiv:2610.31655.summary: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions.
arxiv:2610.31655.authors: Jian-Rong Li, Michael Oren Perlstein, Ran J. Tessler

arxiv:2610.31674.title: M5-brane source charges, Chern--Connes pairings and noncommutative compactifications
arxiv:2610.31674.summary: We formulate a source-adapted Chern--Connes description of M5-brane magnetic charge in physically motivated noncommutative and quotient linking sectors. The starting point is the local codimension-five geometry of an M5-brane source: the magnetic charge is measured on a four-dimensional link. In the smooth local model the link is the ordinary four-sphere, and the pairing reduces to the standard flux integral of the M-theory four-form field strength.

arxiv:2610.31696.title: Links of minimum degree and exact covering numbers
arxiv:2610.31696.summary: The covering number $C(v,k,t)$ is the least number of $k$-subsets, called blocks, of a $v$-set such that every $t$-subset lies in one of them. We reduce the question whether a covering with $L$ blocks exists to the classification of links. If every point of such a covering lies in at least $r$ blocks and $(r+1)v>kL$, some point lies in exactly $r$ blocks, and its link, the blocks through it with the point removed, is a $(v-1,k-1,t-1)$-covering with $r$ blocks.

arxiv:2610.31740.title: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
arxiv:2610.31740.summary: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension $2n$ with $n+1$ a prime number, and all powers of these varieties. For any variety $X$ of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4, we show that the Lefschetz standard conjecture for $X$ implies the Hodge conjecture for $X$ and all its powers.

arxiv:2610.31771.title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods
arxiv:2610.31771.summary: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones.
arxiv:2610.31771.authors: Tsao-Hsien Chen, Sanath K. Devalapurkar, Mark Macerato, David Nadler

arxiv:2610.31781.title: Ozone groups and centers of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras
arxiv:2610.31781.summary: Let $p,q$ be roots of unity with $pq\neq1$, and put $\ell=|\langle p,q\rangle|$ and $t=\ord(pq)$. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is $\mu_\ell\times\mu_{\ell/t}$, generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order $t$.
arxiv:2610.31781.authors: James G\'omez, H\'ector Su\'arez, Helbert Venegas

arxiv:2610.31785.title: Principal specializations of the $t$-chromatic symmetric function
arxiv:2610.31785.summary: We introduce the $t$-chromatic symmetric function $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, a variant of Stanley's chromatic symmetric function in which the variable $t$ records the number of distinct colors used in a proper coloring. Although $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$ is equivalent to the chromatic symmetric function as a graph invariant, its principal specializations retain substantially more information than those of the chromatic symmetric function. This construction is motivated by the work of Bajo--Beck--Vindas-Mel\'endez on the $q$-chromatic polynomial and the conjecture of Loehr--Warrington that the $n$th principal specialization of the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees on at most $n$ vertices,…
arxiv:2610.31785.authors: Aram Bingham, Kyle Celano, Patricia Commins, Rosa Orellana, Jianping Pan, Mary Claire Simone

arxiv:2610.31795.title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
arxiv:2610.31795.summary: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements.
arxiv:2610.31795.authors: Sara Billey, Herman Chau, Kevin Liu

arxiv:2610.31798.title: Sphere decomposition for finite subgroups of 3-manifold mapping class groups
arxiv:2610.31798.summary: For a closed, oriented 3-manifold $M$, we show that any finite subgroup of its mapping class group preserves an isotopy class of filling sphere system on $M$. This is an isotopy version of the "equivariant sphere theorem" of Meeks-Yau. As part of our analysis, we establish a bijection between simplices of the Guirardel--Levitt outer space for $\pi_1(M)$ and filling sphere systems in $M$, generalizing an argument of Hatcher.

arxiv:2610.31806.title: Tate Frobenius and chromatic blueshift of finite spectra
arxiv:2610.31806.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $n\geq 1$. We prove that the Tate-Frobenius of the $\operatorname{K}(n)$-local sphere induces an equivalence between $L_{n-1}L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y$ and $(L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y)^{t\Sigma_p} \cong (L_nY)^{t\Sigma_p}$ for any finite $p$-local type $n-1$ spectrum $Y$ with trivial $\Sigma_p$-action.

arxiv:2610.31807.title: Additive energy and Fourier complexity of graphs
arxiv:2610.31807.summary: We study the additive energy and the Fourier approximation of graph adjacency matrices labeled by a cyclic group. For a graph with $N$ vertices, $s$ edges and adjacency matrix $M$, the additive energy of its directed edge set is at most $\min\{(2s)^3,N^2\operatorname{tr}(M^4)\}$, and equality in the spectral bound holds exactly when the labeling attains the graph-energy lower bound for the Fourier ratio. Such a labeling also minimizes every best $k$-term Fourier approximation error, whose square equals the tail of the squared adjacency singular values.
arxiv:2610.31807.authors: Vishal Gupta, Sam Ferguson, Alex Iosevich, Joshua Iosevich, Haoyuan Tian, Ben Song

arxiv:2610.31823.title: Higher-order asymptotic formulae for periodic orbits of 3-dimensional volume-preserving Anosov flows and the Foulon conjecture
arxiv:2610.31823.summary: Let $X^t$ be a volume-preserving Anosov flow of class $C^7$ on a closed $3$-manifold. We consider a sequence of periodic orbits which shadow a homoclinic loop of a fixed periodic orbit $\gamma$, and derive higher-order asymptotic expansions for their periods $T_n$ and for the logarithms of their unstable multipliers $\log\lambda_n$. We give geometric interpretations of the coefficients in these expansions, in particular in terms of the Anosov cocycle (\`a la Hurder-Katok) and the longitudinal Anosov cocycle (\`a la Foulon-Hasselblatt), evaluated on $\gamma$.

arxiv:2610.31826.title: Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of symmetric powers and applications
arxiv:2610.31826.summary: The Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class $c_{SM}(X)$ is defined in the Chow group $A_*(X)$ of a scheme $X$, and generalizes $c(T_X)\cap [X]$ if $X$ is smooth. In this paper we independently compute $c_{SM}(S^nX)\in A_*(S^nX)$ modulo $n!$ torsion; we use this result to compute the pushforward to $S^nX$ of $c_{SM}(Quot^n_X(E))$ (and in particular $c_{SM}(Hilb^n X)$) when $X$ is smooth and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$. Finally, when $X$ is smooth and complete of dimension $3$ we propose a refined version of the the MNOP conjecture that computes the image of the pushforward of $[Hilb^n X]^{vir}$ to $A_0(S^nX)$ and prove it modulo $n!$ torsion when $X$ is Calabi-Yau.

arxiv:2610.31837.title: Presheaf structures governed by oriented matroids and pseudohyperplane arrangements
arxiv:2610.31837.summary: We study higher complements of pseudohyperplane arrangements and the specialization maps between them, induced by degenerations. We develop a presheaf formalism on oriented matroids and weak maps, which model degenerations. Our main constructions are the posets of weighted and weightwise topes, which provide functorial combinatorial models for higher complements and their specialization morphisms.

arxiv:2610.31853.title: The $d$-invariant of surgeries on $2$-component L-space links
arxiv:2610.31853.summary: Gorsky, B. Liu and Moore provided a formula for the $d$-invariants of integral surgeries on $2$-component $L$-space links with linking number $0$. This paper generalizes these results to the nonzero linking number case.

arxiv:2610.31865.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
arxiv:2610.31865.summary: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$.
arxiv:2610.31865.authors: Hac\`{e}ne Belbachir, Jos\'{e} Ricardo G. Mendon\c{c}a

arxiv:2610.31872.title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
arxiv:2610.31872.summary: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$.

arxiv:2610.31879.title: Comparison of Logarithmic Hochschild Homologies
arxiv:2610.31879.summary: We construct a comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}$ between Rognes' logarithmic Hochschild homology and Olsson's logarithmic Hochschild homology which generalizes the comparison between Gabber's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Gab}}$ and Olsson's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In particular, Olsson's comparison is recovered as the first associated graded piece of our comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In the development of this comparison, we also prove a descent result for the cotangent complex generalizing a result of Bhatt, and construct a notion of…

arxiv:2610.31921.title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems for Banach Space Cocycles
arxiv:2610.31921.summary: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of $q$-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles.

arxiv:2610.31939.title: Flexibility of topological entropy and factor persistence in the $C^0$-Gromov Hausdorff topology
arxiv:2610.31939.summary: We prove that every surjective topological dynamical system on a compact metric space can be approximated in the $C^0$-Gromov--Hausdorff topology by homeomorphisms with any prescribed topological entropy in $[0,+\infty]$, even when simultaneous approximation of its sets of invariant and ergodic measures is required. We also establish a rigidity result under uniform geometric bounds in a fixed dimension: for a homeomorphism of a closed, connected Riemannian manifold, topological stability in the sense of Gromov--Hausdorff guarantees its persistence as a factor of sufficiently close perturbations within the same geometric class. This persistence prevents topological entropy from decreasing…

arxiv:2610.31940.title: The space of equators has infinite Hofer's diameter
arxiv:2610.31940.summary: We settle several questions about Hofer's geometry of the two-sphere. We prove that the space of equators has infinite Hofer diameter, construct simple commutators of arbitrarily large Hofer norm, and exhibit a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism whose iterates escape to infinity in Hofer distance from the set of autonomous diffeomorphisms. Finally, we construct a bi-Lipschitz group monomorphism from the free group of rank two, equipped with its conjugation-invariant generator norm, into the Hamiltonian group equipped with Hofer's metric.

arxiv:2610.31961.title: Spectrum of the basilica group and the associated real and complex 2D dynamics
arxiv:2610.31961.summary: In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar.
arxiv:2610.31961.authors: Eric Bedford, Rostislav Grigorchuk, Nguyen-Bac Dang, Mikhail Lyubich

arxiv:2610.31964.title: On perfectoid ideals
arxiv:2610.31964.summary: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals.

arxiv:2610.31967.title: Swapping Compatible Words
arxiv:2610.31967.summary: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality iff $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. In 2024 Carrigan et. al. asked if there is a "natural" bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question.

arxiv:2610.31980.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
arxiv:2610.31980.summary: For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial.
arxiv:2610.31980.authors: Muchen Ju, Junjie Ni, Kaixin Wang, Yihan Xiao

arxiv:2610.32000.title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
arxiv:2610.32000.summary: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours.

arxiv:2610.32003.title: Kashiwara's Lemma for Potent D-modules
arxiv:2610.32003.summary: On stacks there is a richer version of $\mathcal{D}$-modules---called $\textit{potent }\mathcal{D}\textit{-modules}$---which decompletes at equivariant parameters, in the same sense that genuine equivariant $K$-theory decompletes equivariant cohomology. In this paper, we prove a ``genuine'' version of Kashiwara's lemma for $\mathcal{D}$-modules. Namely, we show that for a broad class of geometric stacks $X$, if $Z \subset X$ is a closed substack, the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $Z$ is equivalent under pushforward to the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}} _Z(X)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $X$ with support contained in $Z$.

arxiv:2610.32016.title: Tropical cohomology for band schemes over the tropical hyperfield
arxiv:2610.32016.summary: We define tropical band varieties as $\mathbf{T}$-reductions of separated finitely presented $\mathbf{T}$-band schemes. We construct a faithful functor from the category of tropical band varieties to the category of extended polyhedral spaces in the sense of Gross--Shokrieh. As a byproduct, we show that tropical cohomology can be defined functorially on tropical band varieties.

arxiv:2610.32035.title: Equifacetted polytopes whose facets are products of simplices: The simplicial prism case
arxiv:2610.32035.summary: We study \emph{prismatical} polytopes, those all of whose facets are combinatorially isomorphic to the simplicial prism $\Delta^{d-2}\times\Delta^1$. In dimension three these are exactly the cubical polytopes, so the class sits naturally between simplicial and cubical polytopes. In dimension four, $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$ is the simplest prismatical polytope and we can construct infinitely many by using connected sums.
arxiv:2610.32035.authors: Federico Castillo, Guillermo Pi\~neda-Villavicencio, Jos\'e Alejandro Samper

arxiv:2610.32036.title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
arxiv:2610.32036.summary: Let $(X, \Omega)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $\Omega$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, \Omega)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau.

arxiv:2610.32038.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
arxiv:2610.32038.summary: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations.

arxiv:2610.32040.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
arxiv:2610.32040.summary: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

arxiv:2610.32050.title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
arxiv:2610.32050.summary: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive.
arxiv:2610.32050.authors: Jiaxuan Chen, Chance Crigler, Shengtao Ding, Dana Paquin, Julian Schennach

arxiv:2610.32056.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
arxiv:2610.32056.summary: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two.
arxiv:2610.32056.authors: Nardo Gim\'enez, Juan Francisco Gottig, Miguel Palacios, Mariana P\'erez, Melina Privitelli

arxiv:2610.32064.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
arxiv:2610.32064.summary: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere.

arxiv:2610.32074.title: Contributions to the Stable Derived Categories of Gorenstein Rings
arxiv:2610.32074.summary: The stable derived category $D_{sg}(R)$ of a Gorenstein ring $R$ is the Verdier quotient of the bounded derived category $D^b(\mathsf{mod}\, R)$ by the thick subcategory of perfect complexes, and was introduced by Buchweitz as a homological measure of the singularities of $R$. This thesis contributes to its study, centered around representation-theoretic and Koszul duality aspects. In Part I, we complete (over $\mathbb{C}$) the classification of homogeneous complete intersection isolated singularities $R$ for which $D^{\mathbb{Z}}_{sg}(R)$ (respectively, $D^b(\mathsf{coh}\, X)$ for $X = \mathsf{proj}\, R$) contains a tilting object.

arxiv:2610.32086.title: The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers
arxiv:2610.32086.summary: Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colon\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^\alpha$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[ \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{\alpha+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}.
arxiv:2610.32086.authors: Matija Blagojevi\'c, Pavle V. M. Blagojevi\'c

arxiv:2610.32147.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons
arxiv:2610.32147.summary: We propose a neural exploratory framework for variational problems over graphons, i.e., symmetric measurable functions $[0,1]^2 \to [0,1]$, that arise as limits of dense graph sequences. Such problems are central to two parts of the mathematical literature: extremal graph theory, which studies graph parameter optimisation under given restrictions, often for those graphs with a large number of vertices, and the large deviation theory of dense random graphs, which characterises the structure of rare events through constrained graphon optimisation. We represent graphons by implicit neural networks and optimise graphon objectives by gradient descent.
arxiv:2610.32147.authors: Taeyoung Kim, Jineon Baek, Joonkyung Lee, Hongseok Yang

arxiv:2610.32192.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
arxiv:2610.32192.summary: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$.

arxiv:2610.32219.title: A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
arxiv:2610.32219.summary: Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators.
arxiv:2610.32219.authors: Lin Chen, Tingwei Hu, Yuchen Mao, Guochuan Zhang

arxiv:2610.32239.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
arxiv:2610.32239.summary: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions.
arxiv:2610.32239.authors: Yansong Feng, Hao Jiang, Guancheng Li, Tianyi Li, Lili Tang

arxiv:2610.32269.title: Conway polynomials of $Th(p,q)$ and $Th(q,p)$: a proof of Takemura's conjecture
arxiv:2610.32269.summary: Takemura conjectured that the Conway polynomials $\sum a_\ell z^\ell$ of the Turk's head link $Th(p,q)$ and $\sum b_\ell z^\ell$ of $Th(q,p)$ satisfy $a_\ell=b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv0,1\pmod 4$ and $a_\ell=-b_\ell$ for $\ell\equiv2,3\pmod4$, and proved it for $q=2,3$. We prove it for all $p,q\ge1$, knots and links. Equivalently, $\nabla_{Th(q,p)}(z)=c\,\nabla_{Th(p,q)}(iz)$ with $c=1$ if $\gcd(p,q)$ is odd and $c=-i$ if it is even.

arxiv:2610.32306.title: Dynamics of a Harvested Predator-Prey Model with a Generalized Holling Type~III Response Capturing Group Defense
arxiv:2610.32306.summary: We investigate a predator-prey model with constant prey harvesting and a generalized Holling type III functional response, focusing on the biological and dynamical consequences of allowing the parameter $b$ to be negative. In this regime, predation efficiency declines at high prey densities, potentially reflecting group defense. This change permits an additional coexistence equilibrium and introduces new bifurcation mechanisms affecting population persistence.
arxiv:2610.32306.authors: Wael El Khateeb, Farjana Akter, Chanaka Kottegoda, Muner Mustafa Abou Hasan

arxiv:2610.32320.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
arxiv:2610.32320.summary: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.

arxiv:2610.32342.title: Angle cocycles, Euler characteristic, and simplicial volume of smooth manifolds
arxiv:2610.32342.summary: A celebrated conjecture of Gromov states that for closed aspherical manifolds, the vanishing of simplicial volume implies the vanishing of the Euler characteristic. We prove Gromov's conjecture for closed convex projective manifolds and, more generally, for closed orientable smooth manifolds admitting an immersed straightening. Generalising the straightening of simplices in properly convex domains in real projective space, we introduce the notion of immersed straightening and prove that, for every integer $d\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that every closed orientable smooth $d$-manifold $M$ admitting an immersed straightening satisfies $|\chi(M)|\le C_d||M||$.
arxiv:2610.32342.authors: Michelle Bucher, Stefano Francaviglia, Grazia Rago

arxiv:2610.32351.title: Cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$
arxiv:2610.32351.summary: A graph is edge-transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its edge set. This paper is devoted to a systematic study of cubic edge-transitive graphs of order $\ell p^2$, where $p$ is a prime and $\ell$ is an even integer. We first show that either $\Gamma$ is the unique cubic edge-transitive graph of order $18$, or its full automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(\Gamma)$ contains a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ which is isomorphic to either $Z_{p^2}$ or $Z_{p}^2$.
arxiv:2610.32351.authors: Xue Wang, Jun-Jie Huang, Da-Wei Yang

arxiv:2610.32353.title: Saturation in three-uniform Berge hypergraphs: the five-star spectrum and the $K_4$ saturation number
arxiv:2610.32353.summary: For a graph \(G\), a hypergraph is Berge-\(G\)-saturated if it contains no Berge copy of \(G\), but adding any missing hyperedge creates one. We determine the complete saturation spectrum of three-uniform Berge five-stars for every order. For \(n\ge7\), every integer from \(\lceil4n/3\rceil-3\) to \(2n-5\) occurs; the additional values depend only on \(n\) modulo five.
arxiv:2610.32353.authors: XuanYu Cao, Yuan Lai, Chunxiang Wang

arxiv:2610.32384.title: Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties
arxiv:2610.32384.summary: We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group. The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts. Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray.

arxiv:2610.32391.title: Global injectivity and real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$
arxiv:2610.32391.summary: In this paper, we study the global injectivity of local diffeomorphisms in $\mathbb{R}^n$, extending the criterions of Braun and Llibre in [{\it Pacific J. Math.} {\bf 333} (2024) 1--15] from the planar radial case to arbitrary dimension. Then we extend the results of Llibre and Mello in [{\it Bull.
arxiv:2610.32391.authors: Xinhao Hu, Jaume Llibre, Yilei Tang

arxiv:2610.32399.title: The Malt'sev condition for groups is not categorical
arxiv:2610.32399.summary: In this paper we prove that the Mal'tsev condition expressing the existence of group operations is not equivalent to a categorical property. More precisely, using pseudo-invertible idempotents, we construct two varieties $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}(f)$ which are equivalent as categories, and such that $\mathcal{V}$ admits group operations, whereas $\mathcal{V}(f)$ does not. We also show that those Mal'tsev conditions which are equivalent to a categorical property have a trivial spectrum.

arxiv:2610.32400.title: Quivers with Involutions and Shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$Quantum groups via Coulomb Branches
arxiv:2610.32400.summary: We give a formula for quasi-minuscule monopole operators in $K$-theoretic quantized Coulomb branch algebras of cotangent type. We then study signed quivers with involutions, with orthogonal or symplectic gauge factors at the involution-fixed vertices. We construct a GKLO-type homomorphism from the corresponding shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum group to an algebra of $q$-difference operators and prove that it factors through the quantized Coulomb branch algebra.
arxiv:2610.32400.authors: Yaolong Shen, Changjian Su, Zichang Wang, Rui Xiong

arxiv:2610.32402.title: Stable Set Reconfiguration in Dense Digraphs
arxiv:2610.32402.summary: In a directed graph, a stable (or acyclic) set is a set which does not induce a directed cycle. Given a directed graph and two acyclic sets of the same size, the Acyclic-Set-Reconfiguration with Directed Token Sliding (ASR) problem asks whether one can, by iteratively replacing a vertex by an adjacent one, transform the first set into the second one, while maintaining acyclicity during the transformation. In this work, we present a study of the complexity of ASR and provide an FPT algorithm for semi-complete digraphs, when parametrized by the size of the sets being reconfigured, the directed pathwidth (or equivalently, the directed treewidth) of the instance, and a newly introduced…
arxiv:2610.32402.authors: Sarah Houdaigoui, Nacim Oijid, Matthieu Petiteau, Alexandre Vigny

arxiv:2610.32404.title: The chromatic number of $\{\mathrm{ISK}_4, \textup{diamond}\}$-free graphs
arxiv:2610.32404.summary: An $\mathrm{ISK}_4$ is a graph that is isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$; a \textit{diamond} is $K_4$ minus one edge; and a \textit{bowtie} consists of two triangles sharing exactly one vertex. L\'ev\^eque, Maffray, and Trotignon~(2012) conjectured that every $\mathrm{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable. Chen, Chen, Cui, Feng, and Liu~(2021) proved this for $\{\textup{diamond},\textup{bowtie}\}$-free graphs.

arxiv:2610.32408.title: An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
arxiv:2610.32408.summary: In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $\chi (S^n_{R}) \leq (\xi_R + o(1))^n$, where $\xi_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-1/(4R^2)) $ and $\chi(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.
arxiv:2610.32408.authors: A. I. Bikeev, V. A. Voronov, A. M. Raigorodskii

arxiv:2610.32416.title: Motivic local density of isolated singularities of algebraic varieties
arxiv:2610.32416.summary: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated singularity of an algebraic variety, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. We compute the density as the residue in 1 of a Zeta function associated to normalized local volumes and we use a resolution of the singularity to get the formula.

arxiv:2610.32424.title: On the homeomorphism group of the Cantor set: monotone and measure preserving maps
arxiv:2610.32424.summary: Let $E$ be the Cantor set, $G=\operatorname{Homeo}(E)$, let $P\le G$ be the group of order preserving homeomorphisms and $L\le G$ the group of homeomorphisms preserving the Cantor--Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. We study how $G$ is built from these two subgroups. In 2003, Glasner and Weiss stated that $G=LP=PL$.

arxiv:2610.32426.title: Associative Lifts of CW Semigroups
arxiv:2610.32426.summary: Every nonempty connected finite-dimensional CW topological semigroup admits a continuous associative multiplication on its universal cover that lifts the multiplication of the base. Such a multiplication is unique up to a deck transformation: in fact, any two associative lifts are conjugate whenever they exist. We show that the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped in general: a connected, countable, infinite-dimensional CW topological semigroup is constructed for which continuous lifts of multiplication exist, but none is associative.

arxiv:2610.32445.title: Partial rigidity and q-additive functions
arxiv:2610.32445.summary: A system $(X,\mu, T)$ is partially rigid with constant $\delta>0$ if there exists an incresing sequence $(n_k)$ such that $\displaystyle \liminf_{k \to \infty } \mu(A \cap T^{-n_k}A) \geq \delta \mu(A)$ for every measurable $A \subset X$. The partial rigidity rate is the largest constant of partial rigidity. We characterize the partial rigidity rate of subshifts arising from $q$-additive functions $\pmod M$ in terms of quantities arising from B\'esineau's theorem.

arxiv:2610.32450.title: Reflection groups on smooth projective threefolds
arxiv:2610.32450.summary: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective threefold with $H^2(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)=0$ and unobstructed deformations. We define reflection groups $W_Y^{sm}$ and $W_Y^{big}$ canonically associated to $Y$, acting on the nef, resp. movable cone of a very general deformation of $Y$. If $-K_Y$ is nef, we show that $\mathrm{Nef}(Y)\cap\mathrm{Big}(Y)$ (resp.

arxiv:2610.32475.title: Exact bounded cohomology of measure-preserving homeomorphism groups of nonorientable hyperbolic manifolds
arxiv:2610.32475.summary: Let $M$ be a closed, connected, non-orientable hyperbolic manifold, and let $\mu$ be a good measure on $M$. Denote by $Homeo_0(M,\mu)$ the identity component of the group of $\mu$-preserving homeomorphisms. For every $d\geq2$, we prove that $\dim\overline{EH}_b^d\bigl(Homeo_0(M,\mu)\bigr)=\infty$, where $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denotes reduced exact bounded cohomology in degree $d$.

arxiv:2610.32484.title: The convergence-divergence criterion for the Ma\~n\'e cohomology lemma and Liv\v{s}ic theorem
arxiv:2610.32484.summary: We establish a new dynamical convergence-divergence criterion for the existence of Lipschitz functions with continuous sub-actions, over general dynamical systems. This unifies and generalises various versions of the Ma\~n\'e cohomology lemma, in the setting of uniformly expanding maps, and systems with indifferent fixed points. One consequence is that for any compact metric space $(X,\rho)$, and Lipschitz Ruelle-expanding map $T:X\to X$, a metric transform $\omega$ satisfies Dini's criterion $\int_0 \omega(s)s^{-1}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if every function that is Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$ has a continuous sub-action.
arxiv:2610.32484.authors: Oliver Jenkinson, Yiwei Zhang, Hang Zhao

arxiv:2610.32489.title: Marked length spectrum and area of surfaces with Anosov geodesic flow
arxiv:2610.32489.summary: More than twenty years ago, Croke and Dairbekov showed that a negatively curved metric $g_0$ on a closed surface has minimal area among all negatively curved Riemannian metrics $g$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $g_0$. We show that the curvature assumption on the second metric can be removed and extend this result to reversible Finsler metrics. More precisely, we prove that a reversible Finsler metric $F_0$ on a closed surface whose geodesic flow is Anosov has minimal area among all reversible Finsler metrics $F$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $F_0$.

arxiv:2610.32499.title: An incidence approach to cross-intersection in semilattices
arxiv:2610.32499.summary: We present an incidence-based method for product bounds on cross-intersecting families in finite graded meet-semilattices. The two families may lie in different rank or type fibres and may have different design strengths. The criterion separates global incidence parameters from two directional local counts and yields the sharp product bound, with equality only for full stars with a common centre.

arxiv:2610.32507.title: Higher \v{C}ech derived functors via Galois theory
arxiv:2610.32507.summary: We explore sufficient conditions for the higher \v{C}ech derived functors of a Birkhoff reflector to agree with its ordinary, Barr-Beck comonadic homology. Using categorical Galois theory together with a spectral-sequence argument, we prove that this is the case for the reflector from any semi-abelian variety onto a subvariety: for every $n\geq 1$, the $n$th \v{C}ech derived functor of the reflector coincides with its $(n+1)$st comonadic homology object. More generally, the comparison holds for any Birkhoff reflector of a semi-abelian category equipped with a comonad satisfying Quillen's conditions.
arxiv:2610.32507.authors: Florent Afsa, Tim Van der Linden

arxiv:2610.32523.title: Jacobian layers and higher Milnor sequences: rigidity, stabilization, and log-concavity
arxiv:2610.32523.summary: Let $f$ be an isolated hypersurface singularity and let $J(f)$ be its Jacobian ideal. We study the higher Milnor numbers $\mu_k(f)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_n/\mathfrak m^kJ(f).$ Our main result concerns an ordinary semi-homogeneous singularity $f=f_r+f_{r+1}+\cdots$, where the projective hypersurface defined by $f_r$ is smooth. We prove that $\mu_k(f)=\mu_k(f_r) \qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.$ This gives the equal-weight case of a conjecture of Shi, Yau, and Zuo.
arxiv:2610.32523.authors: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Mingyi Zhang

arxiv:2610.32527.title: The upper bounds on occupancy fraction and variance fraction for linear regular uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.32527.summary: The hard-core model can be used to understand the number of independent sets in graphs in extremal graph theory. The occupancy and variance fractions are the expectation and variance, respectively, of the independent-set size, normalized by the number of vertices. We provide upper bounds on the occupancy and variance fractions of linear $d$-regular $r$-uniform hypergraphs for small positive fugacities.

arxiv:2610.32577.title: Noetherian local rings without perfectoid towers
arxiv:2610.32577.summary: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. We prove that if a $p$-torsionfree ring $R$, defined by homogeneous equations over $W(k)$, admits a perfectoid tower arising from $(R,(p))$, then its special fiber is $F$-liftable. We also give explicit examples admitting no such tower, including examples with $F$-liftable special fibers.

arxiv:2610.32580.title: New approaches to the Erd\H{o}s Distinct Subset Sums Problem
arxiv:2610.32580.summary: We present a new method of reproving the best known lower bound of the Erd\H{o}s distinct subset sums problem. Although our lower bound is asymptotically the same as in Dubroff, Fox and Xu, it is slightly better for the case when \(n\) is odd. Besides, we also provide a new lower bound on the second largest element \(a_{n-1}\).

arxiv:2610.32593.title: Deformations of cohomology classes and spectral sequences
arxiv:2610.32593.summary: We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre. This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria.

arxiv:2610.32623.title: Energy Discontinuity of the Lyapunov Exponent for Quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger Operators with Gevrey Potentials
arxiv:2610.32623.summary: We construct quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators with Gevrey potentials for which the Lyapunov exponent is discontinuous in the spectral energy. More precisely, let \(\alpha\in\R\setminus\mathbb Q\) satisfy the Diophantine condition \(\|k\alpha\|_{\T}\geq\gamma |k|^{-\tau}\) for all \(k\in\Z\setminus\{0\}\), with \(\gamma>0\) and \(\tau\geq1\). For every Gevrey index \(\mathfrak s>1+\tau\) and every sufficiently large coupling \(\lambda\), we construct a real-valued potential \(v_\lambda\in G^{\mathfrak s}(\T,\R)\) and a sequence of energies \(E_j\downarrow0\) such that \[ L_{v_\lambda}(0)\geq(1-\varepsilon_\lambda)\log\lambda, \qquad \sup_{j\geq1}…

arxiv:2610.32644.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of 3-graphs
arxiv:2610.32644.summary: We prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"{e}te, and Yu that for a $3$-graph $H$, the off-diagonal Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the "depth-$t$ iterated blowup" $\textsf{B}_t$ for an integer $t\geq 0$. Here, the $3$-graphs $\textsf{B}_t$ are defined recursively: $\textsf{B}_0$ has one vertex, and $\textsf{B}_t$ for $t\geq 1$ is obtained from the disjoint union of three copies of $\textsf{B}_{t-1}$ by adding all transversal hyperedges.
arxiv:2610.32644.authors: Lior Gishboliner, Sepehr Hajebi, Xiangyu Li

arxiv:2610.32647.title: Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
arxiv:2610.32647.summary: Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$. We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank.
arxiv:2610.32647.authors: Takayuki Hibi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

arxiv:2610.32677.title: Sharp asymmetric vertex-Ramsey properties of graphs
arxiv:2610.32677.summary: In 1992, \L uczak, Ruci\'{n}ski and Voigt showed that for any graph $H$, a parameter $m_1(H)$ - called the 1-density - governs the threshold at which the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ inherits the vertex-Ramsey property. In 2000, Friedgut and Krivelevich showed this threshold is sharp for graphs satisfying a natural balancedness condition. In 1996, Kreuter showed that for any graphs $H_1, \ldots, H_r$ with $m_1(H_1) \geq \cdots \geq m_1(H_r)$, a parameter dependent only on $H_1$ and $H_2$ governs the threshold at which $G(n,p)$ inherits the `asymmetric' vertex-Ramsey property.
arxiv:2610.32677.authors: Robert Hancock, Joseph Hyde, Mael Kupperschmitt

arxiv:2610.32680.title: Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups
arxiv:2610.32680.summary: We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$. Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation. It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups.
arxiv:2610.32680.authors: Sutirtha Datta, Jyotirmoy Ganguly, Rohit Joshi

arxiv:2610.32694.title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $\Xi$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
arxiv:2610.32694.summary: We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios.

arxiv:2610.32706.title: Simple homotopy types of smooth four-manifolds with finite fundamental group
arxiv:2610.32706.summary: We construct closed smooth $4$-manifolds with finite fundamental group which are homotopy equivalent but not simple homotopy equivalent, even after taking a connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$. Our explicit examples have remarkably large fundamental groups; in particular, the smallest examples we obtain have fundamental groups of order roughly $10^{10^{42}}$.

arxiv:2610.32717.title: Total eight-colorings of maximal planar graphs of maximum degree six
arxiv:2610.32717.summary: We prove that every finite simple maximal planar graph of maximum degree at most six admits a total eight-coloring. We first show that every proper vertex four-coloring of a subcubic graph extends to a total five-coloring. A curvature inequality for boundary walks then gives a matching decomposition of four-connected triangulations with degrees five and six, extending their prescribed vertex four-colorings to total eight-colorings.

arxiv:2610.32723.title: Counting curves with bounded intersection
arxiv:2610.32723.summary: This paper counts curves, and multicurves, on hyperbolic surfaces, providing explicit upper bounds that depend polynomially on length and exponentially in terms of an upper bound on self-intersection.

arxiv:2610.32737.title: A probabilistic construction of maximum $h$-scattered subspaces
arxiv:2610.32737.summary: Let $1\le h\le n-2$ and $g=\gcd(n,h+1)$. We prove that, for every prime power $q$, a maximum $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ exists whenever $(h+1)\mid rn$ and $$r\ge\frac{h+1}{g}\bigl(h(n-h-2)+1\bigr).$$ In particular, for fixed $n$ and minimum distance $\delta\in\{2,\ldots,n-1\}$, $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-linear MRD codes of length $N$ exist for every $q$ and every sufficiently large $N$ such that $n$ divides $(n-\delta+1)N$, with a bound on $N$ depending only on $n$ and $\delta$. We take the $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-span of the columns of a random matrix $A$ over the algebra $R=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$, for a suitable $s$.

arxiv:2610.32739.title: Bistability with equal and independent removal in small bimolecular networks
arxiv:2610.32739.summary: We classify two-species mass-action networks with at most three internal directed reactions on $\{X,Y,2X,X+Y,2Y\}$, positive inflows, and linear removal of both species. Among the 681 networks up to species exchange, exactly 27 admit two distinct positive hyperbolic attracting equilibria. The same 27 admit bistability with equal removal rates and with independently chosen positive removal rates.

arxiv:2610.32745.title: The totally nonnegative wonderful compactification of G is a ball
arxiv:2610.32745.summary: Let $\overline{G}$ denote the wonderful compactification of a semisimple algebraic group $G$ of adjoint type. We use contractive flows to show that the totally nonnegative part of every $G \times G$ orbit closure of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In particular, the totally nonnegative part of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed ball.

arxiv:2610.32751.title: Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem
arxiv:2610.32751.summary: We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.

arxiv:2610.32761.title: The restricted Hurwitz action on cameral decompositions of Coxeter elements
arxiv:2610.32761.summary: Given a dual Coxeter system (W, T) of rank n, the Hurwitz action of the braid group on the reduced T-decompositions of a Coxeter element is transitive. When we choose a geometric representation of W, the reflections with respect to the n walls of one given chamber form a generating set S that we call cameral. An ordering of S is called a cameral decomposition and the product a cameral Coxeter element, which depends only on the quiver obtained by orienting the Coxeter diagram with vertices S according to the ordering.

arxiv:2610.32771.title: Veering triangulations of once-punctured torus bundles are unique
arxiv:2610.32771.summary: We show that each hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundle has exactly one veering triangulation. We also find manifolds for which the exact number of veering structures is known and is greater than one. Finally, we give new examples of manifolds without veering triangulations.
