arxiv:2610.32782.title: On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
arxiv:2610.32782.summary: Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.

arxiv:2610.32787.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
arxiv:2610.32787.summary: We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$.

arxiv:2610.32789.title: Triangle-Free Sets in Exact-Distance Hamming Graphs
arxiv:2610.32789.summary: Let $T_q(n,r)$ be the largest size of a vertex set inducing a triangle-free subgraph of the graph on $[q]^n$ whose edges join words at Hamming distance $r$. We study this quantity for fixed alphabet size and fixed distance, with particular emphasis on the ternary cube. Alphabet restriction transfers the binary fixed-distance theorem of Balogh, Chen, and Li to give $T_q(n,2h)=O_h(q^n/n^h)$.
arxiv:2610.32789.authors: Bence Csajb\'ok, Padmini Mukkamala, Zolt\'an L\'or\'ant Nagy

arxiv:2610.32798.title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
arxiv:2610.32798.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges.
arxiv:2610.32798.authors: Siyue Liu, Taihei Oki, Chao Xu

arxiv:2610.32814.title: Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics
arxiv:2610.32814.summary: We consider the left translation action of an element $a$ on a finite-volume semisimple homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(a)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb{R}$. Assuming exponential mixing, we prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for compactly supported smooth test functions. As an application, we prove effective uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy.

arxiv:2610.32820.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
arxiv:2610.32820.summary: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures.
arxiv:2610.32820.authors: Xinyu Bai, Wanshan Lin, Xueting Tian

arxiv:2610.32824.title: A Short Proof of Zhang's Conjecture on Stack-Sortable Permutations
arxiv:2610.32824.summary: We give a short proof of Zhang's conjecture that the number of stack-sortable permutations of length $n + 1$ which end in their smallest element is equal to the $n$-th Motzkin number.

arxiv:2610.32831.title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
arxiv:2610.32831.summary: We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan. We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan. We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.

arxiv:2610.32832.title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
arxiv:2610.32832.summary: We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus. Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a<b<c<d$, with $h=1$ when no such occurrence exists. We show that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q^h+q^{h+1}$ if exactly one of the patterns $3412$ and $4231$ occurs, and $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q+q^h$ if both patterns occur.
arxiv:2610.32832.authors: Gaston Burrull, Zhitong Alex Li, Shixuan Zeng

arxiv:2610.32875.title: The Tur\'an number of Berge paths in connected hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.32875.summary: A Berge path in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of distinct vertices and edges $v_1,e_1, v_2, \ldots, e_{k-1}, v_{k}$ such that $v_i, v_{i+1} \in e_i$ for all $i \in [k-1]$. Gy\H{o}ri, Katona, and Lemons determined the maximum number edges in $r$-uniform, $n$-vertex hypergraphs without Berge paths on $k$ vertices. The extremal examples for their bounds are disconnected hypergraphs in which each component has either too few edges or too few vertices to contain such a Berge path.

arxiv:2610.32879.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
arxiv:2610.32879.summary: Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $\eta\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\le\eta\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons.

arxiv:2610.32897.title: Linear transformations of tropical matrices preserving individual values of the cyclicity index
arxiv:2610.32897.summary: The cyclicity index is used to study the periodic behavior of powers of tropical matrices. It is determined by the structure of the critical subgraph of a matrix, which consists of the cycles with the largest average weight. In this paper bijective linear transformations of tropical matrices that preserve an individual value $k\neq 2$ of this invariant are studied.
arxiv:2610.32897.authors: Alexander Guterman, Alexander Vlasov, Svetlana Zhilina

arxiv:2610.32900.title: Rank 3 curve semistable Higgs bundles: the nilpotent case
arxiv:2610.32900.summary: A Higgs bundle on a smooth complex projective variety is curve semistable if its pullback to every smooth projective curve is semistable. A 2008 conjecture asserts that this is equivalent to slope semistability for some polarization plus vanishing discriminant. One direction is known, the converse holds in rank two, and Huang recently gave a rank-four counterexample.

arxiv:2610.32917.title: Stationary bistable fronts on a periodic necklace graph: existence, stability and multiplicity
arxiv:2610.32917.summary: We study stationary fronts for a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with the McKean reaction on a periodic necklace metric graph. For profiles that agree on each pair of parallel edges, the problem reduces to a scalar equation on the real line with a periodic, piecewise constant diffusion coefficient. The diffusion contrast of the necklace is not small, so the coefficient cannot be treated as a small perturbation of a constant.
arxiv:2610.32917.authors: Yoichiro Mori, Toshiyuki Ogawa, Chanoknun Sintavanuruk

arxiv:2610.32928.title: Vertex operator algebra realizations of untwisted Haagerup--Izumi centers
arxiv:2610.32928.summary: For every odd integer $N\geq3$, we construct an untwisted Haagerup--Izumi fusion category $\mathcal H_N$ on the negative spherical branch and a simple, self-contragredient, regular, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra $E_N$ of central charge $-16N$, together with an equivalence of modular fusion categories: \[ \operatorname{Rep}(E_N)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_N). \] The VOA $E_N$ is rational, has exactly $N^2+3$ irreducible modules, and is lower bounded and integer graded, with least conformal degree $-(N-1)/2$. The proof begins with a CFT-type cyclic Virasoro extension of central charge $-5N$, whose regularity we establish.

arxiv:2610.32952.title: The Verra involution on special cubic fourfolds
arxiv:2610.32952.summary: We present a detailed study of the Hodge theory, geometry and derived categories of Verra fourfolds, and their relationship with twisted K3 surfaces and cubic fourfolds. We classify Brauer classes of Verra type on K3 surfaces of degree 2, and use this to derive an explicit counting formula for Fourier--Mukai partners of a large class of Verra fourfolds. We develop the basic theory of cohomology of Verra fourfolds and apply it to prove a derived Torelli theorem for a large class of Verra fourfolds.
arxiv:2610.32952.authors: Augustinas Jacovskis, Reinder Meinsma, Riccardo Moschetti

arxiv:2610.32954.title: Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
arxiv:2610.32954.summary: A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles.
arxiv:2610.32954.authors: J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen, St\'ephane Bessy, Amadeus Reinald

arxiv:2610.32975.title: Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic
arxiv:2610.32975.summary: This paper studies foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic. We provide an explicit description of all smooth foliations, linear and turbulent, and establish criteria for being $p$-closed. We explicitly determine the moduli spaces of such foliations.

arxiv:2610.33023.title: Non-adjacent triples of cells in a triangular grid: proofs of three conjectured generating functions
arxiv:2610.33023.summary: Let $\Tn$ be the triangular grid of side $n$, with its $n^2$ unit cells, and let two cells be side-adjacent if they share an edge and point-adjacent if they share a vertex. We count the orbits of $3$-element sets of pairwise non-adjacent cells under the rotation group $C_3$ and under the full symmetry group $D_3$ of $\Tn$. Three of the four resulting sequences are OEIS A397730, A397731 and A397732, for each of which the only formula on record is a generating function conjectured by Sean A.\ Irvine on 14 July 2026.

arxiv:2610.33028.title: Equidistribution of mesh patterns of length 2 on involutions
arxiv:2610.33028.summary: We classify all 1024 length-two mesh patterns on involutions into exactly 287 equidis- tribution classes, consisting of 262 trivial classes and 25 nontrivial classes. Since many bi- jections on arbitrary permutations do not preserve the involution condition, our proofs use several involution-preserving bijections, including conjugation and local adjacent-transposition operations, transposition of the RSK recording tableau, prefix-rank swap bijections and marked-occurrence bijections. In particular, we establish the equidistribution of INV-099, a nontrivial class closely related to the unrestricted Class 69, by adapting the marked- occurrence bijection of Zhang and Zhao through a symmetric…

arxiv:2610.33032.title: Sages and Their Anonymous Slips
arxiv:2610.33032.summary: Before the game, the sages agree on a finite set of symbols and on a rule for choosing one of them. They are then seated in an unknown order, either in a row or around a circle with a common clockwise direction. Each sage sees only the adjacent sage or sages and secretly writes one symbol.

arxiv:2610.33037.title: Characteristic Chow Polynomials of Layered-Permutation Intervals
arxiv:2610.33037.summary: We study characteristic Chow polynomials of principal intervals in generalized subword order, equivalently of pattern-containment intervals below layered permutations. A terminal-chain recurrence and canonical rightmost embeddings yield a recursive rational generating function for every fixed number of layers, governed by a universal denominator. In the two-layer case we obtain an explicit kernel, prove canonical interlacing when one layer has size at most four, and prove eventual interlacing at every fixed width by a Laguerre limit.

arxiv:2610.33041.title: The minimum number of wheel-saturating edges
arxiv:2610.33041.summary: Let $G$ be an $H$-free graph and $e$ be a non-edge of $G$. We say $e$ is an $H$-saturating edge of $G$, if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. We denote by $f_H(n,m)$ the minimum number of $H$-saturating edges of an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph with exactly $m$ edges.

arxiv:2610.33042.title: Nonintersecting Unit Diagonals in Odd Square Arrays
arxiv:2610.33042.summary: Let $D(n)$ be the maximum number of unit-square diagonals in an $n\times n$ square array such that no two selected diagonals share an endpoint and no unit square contains both diagonals. We prove that, for every odd positive integer $n$, $D(n)=n(n+1)/2+\lfloor(n+1)/6\rfloor$. The matching lower bound was established by Boyland, Roth, Pint\'er, Lauk\'o, Schoenfield, and Wasielewski.

arxiv:2610.33050.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
arxiv:2610.33050.summary: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone.

arxiv:2610.33053.title: On the minimality of the compact right-angled 120-cell
arxiv:2610.33053.summary: We prove that a compact right-angled polytope in hyperbolic 4-space has at least 120 facets, with equality only for the right-angled 120-cell. This answers a question of Potyagailo and Vinberg. As a consequence, the right-angled 120-cell is the unique compact right-angled 4-polytope of minimal volume and f-vector.

arxiv:2610.33064.title: Second largest eigenvalue thresholds for the vertex-connectivity of regular graphs
arxiv:2610.33064.summary: Let $\lambda_2(G)$ and $\kappa(G)$ denote the second largest adjacency eigenvalue and the vertex-connectivity of a graph $G$. For a non-complete $r$-regular graph $G$, Fiedler's inequality $\lambda_2(G)\ge r-\kappa(G)$ shows that $\lambda_2(G)<r-t$ forces $\kappa(G)\ge t+1$. The best such bound is known for $t=1$, by Zhang and Wang, and for $t=2$ with $r\ge4$, by Zhang.

arxiv:2610.33114.title: Some new criteria for the uniqueness of limit cycles in Rayleigh--Lienard systems
arxiv:2610.33114.summary: In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for Rayleigh--Li\'enard systems with damping of positive odd degree in the velocity are established. Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by the damping signs. Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping and restoring functions is required.
arxiv:2610.33114.authors: Hebai Chen, Dongmei Xiao, Rui Zhang

arxiv:2610.33131.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
arxiv:2610.33131.summary: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention.
arxiv:2610.33131.authors: Jan Kristian Haugland, Nadia S. Larsen, Tron Omland, Henrikke G. Rustad

arxiv:2610.33151.title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
arxiv:2610.33151.summary: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci.
arxiv:2610.33151.authors: Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song

arxiv:2610.33165.title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index
arxiv:2610.33165.summary: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes.

arxiv:2610.33170.title: Flocking with finite communication speed: a Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach
arxiv:2610.33170.summary: We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates.

arxiv:2610.33183.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories
arxiv:2610.33183.summary: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.

arxiv:2610.33192.title: Extensions of a family of Linear Cycle Sets whose underlying group is a product of two cyclic groups
arxiv:2610.33192.summary: We use the linear cycle set cohomology in order to compute extensions of a non trivial linear cycle sets whose underlying additive group is a product of two cyclic groups.
arxiv:2610.33192.authors: Jorge Guccione, Juan Jos\'e Guccione, Christian Valqui

arxiv:2610.33216.title: Absorption probabilities of random walks without symmetry or general position
arxiv:2610.33216.summary: Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed.

arxiv:2610.33218.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
arxiv:2610.33218.summary: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.

arxiv:2610.33219.title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
arxiv:2610.33219.summary: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al.

arxiv:2610.33226.title: Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$
arxiv:2610.33226.summary: In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field.

arxiv:2610.33228.title: On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
arxiv:2610.33228.summary: We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.

arxiv:2610.33280.title: On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots
arxiv:2610.33280.summary: For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsv\'ath-Szab\'o contact invariant. We prove that if the Ozsv\'ath-Stipsicz-Szab\'o concordance invariant Upsilon has slope $\Upsilon'_K(t)=-g(K)$ for some $t\in[0,\frac{2}{n+1})$, where $g(K)$ is the genus of $K$, then $b(K)>n$. This extends a result of He, Hubbard, and the author on the Upsilon invariant and right-veering monodromies.

arxiv:2610.33283.title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
arxiv:2610.33283.summary: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms.

arxiv:2610.33287.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
arxiv:2610.33287.summary: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures.

arxiv:2610.33322.title: A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture
arxiv:2610.33322.summary: We prove Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture. A D-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a D-coloring with 9 colors if $\Delta=4$, 10 colors if $\Delta=5$, and $2\Delta-1$ colors if $\Delta\ge 6$.

arxiv:2610.33328.title: The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area
arxiv:2610.33328.summary: It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.

arxiv:2610.33344.title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
arxiv:2610.33344.summary: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets.

arxiv:2610.33364.title: Automorphisms and Hodge isometries of surfaces with $K^2=p_g=1$
arxiv:2610.33364.summary: Let $S$ be a minimal complex surface of general type with $K_S^2=p_g(S)=1$. By a theorem of Catanese, the canonical model of $S$ is a complete intersection of two sextics in $\mathbf{P}(1,2,2,3,3)$ whose equations admit a normal form, and the global Torelli theorem fails for these surfaces. We describe $\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ in terms of the coefficients of the normal form, prove that $|\operatorname{Aut}(S)|\leq 72$, and classify the surfaces attaining the bound: two surfaces with singular canonical model and a one-parameter family $X_r$ of smooth surfaces.
arxiv:2610.33364.authors: Jorge Duque Franco, Alvaro Liendo, Pedro Montero

arxiv:2610.33382.title: Classical cumulants from the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra
arxiv:2610.33382.summary: We realize classical cumulants and their fixed-point equations in the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra introduced by Ebrahimi-Fard and Patras, placing classical, free, Boolean, and monotone cumulants in a common algebraic framework. A concatenation perturbation of the functionals yields left and right half-shuffle equations on ordinary words without changing the coproduct or either half-coproduct. Both equations are equivalent to the classical moment--cumulant formula and uniquely determine the classical cumulants.

arxiv:2610.33407.title: A quasi-polynomial $\chi$-bound for $P_6$-free graphs
arxiv:2610.33407.summary: In this paper we prove that every graph $G$ with no induced six-vertex path satisfies $\chi(G)\le \omega(G)^{c\log_2\omega(G)}$ for $c=45/\log_2(4/3)<109$. The best previous bound was exponential in $\omega(G)$. Our result is the first quasi-polynomial bound for $P_6$-free graphs and generalizes the bound for $P_5$-free graphs by Scott, Seymour, and Spirkl [Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. {IV}. {A} near-polynomial bound for excluding the five-vertex path. {\em Combinatorica}, 43(5):845--852, 2023].
arxiv:2610.33407.authors: Shenwei Huang, Yidong Zhou, Yuwen Zhou

arxiv:2610.33417.title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
arxiv:2610.33417.summary: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+\lambda^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $\lambda$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.
arxiv:2610.33417.authors: Qiongling Li, Beibei Liu, Weixu Su, Zhe Sun

arxiv:2610.33418.title: An exact compression-and-lifting procedure and D-optimal designs of orders 198 and 170
arxiv:2610.33418.summary: We develop a compression-and-lifting procedure for constructing D-optimal complementary pairs on finite abelian groups of odd order. The procedure separates the Fourier conditions preserved by compression from those needed to recover the original binary sequences. For groups with a cyclic factor of order nine, integer matching conditions separate compatible classes of local sign assignments.

arxiv:2610.33427.title: An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense signed random combinatorial matrices
arxiv:2610.33427.summary: Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$.
arxiv:2610.33427.authors: Yuxiao Shi, Zeyan Song, Kexin Yu, Tingzhou Yu

arxiv:2610.33468.title: Delambre--Gauss Formulas in Complex Hyperbolic Space
arxiv:2610.33468.summary: We establish a Delambre--Gauss matrix identity for oriented right-angled hexagons in the complex hyperbolic plane. The six complex length parameters of a hexagon determine two alternating \(3\times3\) matrices whose product is central in (\mathrm{SU}(2,1)\). The resulting nine entry-wise equations extend the Delambre-Gauss formula of Tan, Wong, and Zhang in 4-dimensional hyperbolic geometry to this complex hyperbolic setting.

arxiv:2610.33497.title: Proof of the Langberg-M\'edard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
arxiv:2610.33497.summary: Let $\mathcal{N}=(V,A,S, R)$ be a directed network, where $D=(V,A)$ is a digraph, $S=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of senders, and $R=\{r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each $1\le j \le k$, there exist $k$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in $D$, one from each $s_i$ to $r_j$, then the underlying undirected network of ${\cal N}$, with unit capacities, admits a feasible $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-$(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k)$ multiflow of value $1$ for each pair $(s_i,r_i)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,k$. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and M\'edard in 2009.
arxiv:2610.33497.authors: Kai Cai, Guangyue Han, Mengxi Yang, Wenan Zang

arxiv:2610.33519.title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
arxiv:2610.33519.summary: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow.

arxiv:2610.33534.title: Some chromatic height computations for homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology
arxiv:2610.33534.summary: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.

arxiv:2610.33543.title: On the enriched approximate completeness
arxiv:2610.33543.summary: We generalize to the enriched setting the classical theorem of Freyd, that the free cocompletion ${\mathscr PA}$ of a category ${\mathscr A}$ is complete if and only if ${\mathscr A}$ is approximately complete. The work of Day and Lack, arXiv:math/0610439, has laid the foundations for such a generalization and has had multiple applications in homotopy theory and in category theory. Our result allows us to expand on some of these applications.

arxiv:2610.33570.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
arxiv:2610.33570.summary: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$.

arxiv:2610.33572.title: Remarks on covariant differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s sphere
arxiv:2610.33572.summary: An $SU_q(2)$-covariant first-order differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s two-sphere is constructed. The module of one-forms is explicitly given in terms of modules of sections of charge $\pm 2$ line bundles associated to the quantum Hopf fibration.

arxiv:2610.33573.title: A note on Rota-Baxter affgebras
arxiv:2610.33573.summary: An affinization of a concept of a Rota-Baxter operator or Rota-Baxter affgebras are discussed. Rota-Baxter Lie affgebras and their relation to Rota-Baxter Lie algebras are treated in more detail. In particular it is shown that every Rota-Baxter Lie affgebra is isomorphic to a Rota-Baxter Lie affgebra with a Lie algebra fibre over which the affine Rota-Baxter operator is linear.

arxiv:2610.33596.title: A structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems
arxiv:2610.33596.summary: Recently, the author refuted several conjectures about the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences. The goal of this paper is to provide a counterpart for the conjectures of Frantzikinakis--Kuca and of Leibman. The significance of this manuscript is twofold: firstly, we provide a structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions (in the sense of Frantzikinakis--Kuca), and a corresponding structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds (in the sense of Leibman).

arxiv:2610.33601.title: Searching for binary orientable sequences
arxiv:2610.33601.summary: An aperiodic binary orientable sequence is a finite sequence of zeros and ones for which, for some integer $n$, all the subsequences of $n$ consecutive symbols, read either forwards or backwards, are distinct. Analogously, a periodic binary orientable sequence is an infinite periodic sequence of zeros and ones for which, for some integer $n$, all the subsequences of $n$ consecutive symbols, read either forwards or backwards, are distinct within a single period of the sequence. Such sequences have potential application in position-location applications.

arxiv:2610.33602.title: GKZ Systems and Gauss-Manin Connections of Families of Projective Hypersurfaces
arxiv:2610.33602.summary: Periods of projective hypersurfaces satisfy GKZ hypergeometric systems, which may have solutions that do not arise as periods. For deformations of Fermat hypersurfaces, we describe the Gauss-Manin connection in terms of images of contiguity operators between GKZ systems. These images are also realized as Fourier transforms of minimal extensions of Kummer modules.

arxiv:2610.33620.title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
arxiv:2610.33620.summary: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.

arxiv:2610.33657.title: Improved Global Boundedness Criteria via Refined Bootstrap Estimates for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis-May-Nowak System
arxiv:2610.33657.summary: We study a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system with nonlinear diffusion growing at least as $s^{m-1}$ at high densities and derive improved criteria for global existence and uniform boundedness. For the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic system, we establish global boundedness when $m>3-\frac{4}{n}$ for $n\in\{2,3\}$ and when $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. For the fully parabolic system, the same conclusion holds under $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$.
arxiv:2610.33657.authors: Xueli Bai, Fang Li, Suying Liu, Xuxuan Luo

arxiv:2610.33675.title: Which posets are spectra of Noetherian rings? The case of height at most one
arxiv:2610.33675.summary: A finite poset is the prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring exactly when it has no chain of three elements, that is, it is the poset of a finite bipartite graph. This answers Conjecture 5.3 of Alkass. The substance is a construction: minimal elements become curves y=g_i(x), maximal elements points, edges the incidences, arranged by interpolation.

arxiv:2610.33676.title: Extremal diagonal-coherent binary codes: shortened Hamming cores, deep holes, and the 64 I-Ching hexagrams
arxiv:2610.33676.summary: Each of the 64 hexagrams of the I-Ching, or Book of Changes, is a stack of six Yin-Yang lines and is therefore a binary vector of length 6; the eight hexagrams formed by repeating a single trigram span a doubled-trigram subspace $\Delta$. We ask which binary $[6,3,3]$ codes are compatible with this trigram structure. We show that a $[6,3,3]$ code meets $\Delta$ in at most four codewords, that the four are then forced to be the doubled trigrams Earth, Fire, Wind and Lake, and that exactly two codes attain this bound: the shortened Hamming code $\mathcal C_A$ and its dual.

arxiv:2610.33678.title: The chromatic number of a random graph with $o(n^{3/2})$ edges
arxiv:2610.33678.summary: Let $G(n,m)$ be the Erdos-Renyi random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges and let $\delta>0$. Alon and Krivelevich [Combinatorica 1997] proved that for any sequence $m\leq n^{3/2-\delta}$ there \emph{exists} an integer sequence $q=q(n)$ such that the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals either $q$ or $q+1$ with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for this sequence $q(n)$ and confirm their result under a less restrictive assumption that $m=o(n^{3/2})$.
arxiv:2610.33678.authors: Amin Coja-Oghlan, Mikhail Isaev, Mihyun Kang, Pavel Zakharov

arxiv:2610.33692.title: On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs
arxiv:2610.33692.summary: A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory.

arxiv:2610.33699.title: Noninteger completely monotonic degrees of Stirling remainders and their derivatives
arxiv:2610.33699.summary: For Stirling expansions truncated after at least two Bernoulli terms, we disprove the three real-degree conjectures recorded by Mahmoud and Qi for the signed remainders of the logarithm of the gamma function and their derivatives. We give a unified proof of the corresponding integer-degree formula, recovering known cases and resolving Zhu's conjectures for higher derivatives in this range. Every real completely monotonic degree lies strictly between the predicted integer and the next integer.

arxiv:2610.33710.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
arxiv:2610.33710.summary: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers.

arxiv:2610.33724.title: Movable Curves and Ample Normal Bundles
arxiv:2610.33724.summary: We prove that the movable cone of a smooth complex projective variety is the closed cone generated by possibly singular curves with ample coherent normal sheaves, answering a question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell. For smooth curves, we establish the analogous equality in several geometric settings and give explicit constructions on blowups.

arxiv:2610.33736.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
arxiv:2610.33736.summary: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.

arxiv:2610.33738.title: Polynomial Residual Networks are Generically Identifiable
arxiv:2610.33738.summary: We prove identifiability results for constant-width residual networks with polynomial activations and bias terms. For activations of degree at least five with generic coefficients, the fiber over a generic parameter is a singleton. For activations of degree at least three with no linear term after a suitable translation of the input, the generic fiber is given by translating biases and then scaling weights and translated biases by real roots of unity.
arxiv:2610.33738.authors: Isabel Dahlgren, Giovanni Luca Marchetti, Kathl\'en Kohn

arxiv:2610.33752.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
arxiv:2610.33752.summary: In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=\pi^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2\pi z)/(2\pi)$.

arxiv:2610.33754.title: Ramification in $\mathbf{E}_{n}$-algebras
arxiv:2610.33754.summary: We study $\mathbf{E}_n$-algebras with ramification in their $\pi_0$ and in particular show that the existence of ramification places strong limitations on their chromatic behavior. In particular, we show that $\pi_0$ of nonzero $K(1)$-local $\mathbf{E}_4$-$\mathrm{KU}$-algebras cannot have a map from the ring of integers in a ramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$, and we show that a $p$-complete $\mathbf{E}_2$-ring with a map from a perfectoid ring into its $\pi_0$ is an associative $\mathbf{Z}_p$-algebra.

arxiv:2610.33772.title: Combinatorial models for Quasicrystals and Schur-Weyl Duality
arxiv:2610.33772.summary: Quasicrystals were defined by Cain and Malheiro and Maas-Gari\'epy to model the decomposition of Schur polynomials into fundamental quasisymmetric functions. We define a new combinatorial model for crystal graphs of type $A_{n-1}$, called parsed content words, for which the decomposition into quasicrystals is particularly evident. We use the model to describe a combinatorial interpretation of Schur-Weyl duality and recover the classical combinatorial proof of the well-known expansion of homogeneous symmetric functions into Schur functions within our framework.
arxiv:2610.33772.authors: Glenn Appleby, Mary Claire Simone, Tamsen Whitehead McGinley

arxiv:2610.33782.title: Magnetic billiards:duality and magnetic Radon property
arxiv:2610.33782.summary: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$.

arxiv:2610.33791.title: Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
arxiv:2610.33791.summary: Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$.
arxiv:2610.33791.authors: Rupam Barman, Archit Deb, Sayantan Ghorai

arxiv:2610.33803.title: Packing colourings of claw-free subcubic graphs
arxiv:2610.33803.summary: We prove that every claw-free subcubic graph admits a \packA-packing colouring, confirming a conjecture of Mortada, El Zein and Al Hajjar. The proof combines a reduction to line graphs of subdivided loopless cubic multigraphs with local colouring extensions. We also give a negative answer to their question on \packB-packing colourings by constructing an infinite family of connected bridgeless claw-free cubic counterexamples.

arxiv:2610.33823.title: Explicit equations of three pairs of fake projective planes
arxiv:2610.33823.summary: We find explicit polynomial equations in their bicanonical embeddings into $\mathbb C\mathbb P^9$ for the pairs of fake projective planes labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2\},D_3), (C18,p=3,\{2\},(dD)_3)$ and $(C18,p=3,\{2\},(d^2D)_3)$ in the Cartwright-Steger classification. We do this by starting with the equations of the commensurable fake projective plane labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2I\})$ that were found in arXiv:2512.03213.

arxiv:2610.33829.title: Stationary Random Iterations of Lipschitz Maps: A Generalized Displacement Condition for the Existence of Invariant Structures
arxiv:2610.33829.summary: We study random iterations generated by infinitely many Lipschitz maps on non-compact complete separable metric spaces. We generalize classical displacement conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of invariant structures. We prove two main results.
arxiv:2610.33829.authors: Bella Figliaggi, Edgar Matias, Tiago Pereira

arxiv:2610.33830.title: On tame amenable flows and generalized Newelski's conjecture
arxiv:2610.33830.summary: We are developing some topological dynamics below a given ambit. We define and study Bohr compactifications below ambits and other related objects. We describe a natural epimorphism from the Ellis group of an ambit to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit.

arxiv:2610.33850.title: Solving Large SDPs from Flag Algebra Problems
arxiv:2610.33850.summary: The flag algebra method is a general tool in extremal combinatorics, which has been useful in tackling open problems concerning graphs, hypergraphs, permutations, point sets, and other structures. The method establishes combinatorial inequalities via sums of squares, which are usually obtained by a semidefinite relaxation of the original combinatorial problem. A typical application of the method in graph theory starts with fixing a parameter $n$ followed by constructing a semidefinite program based on the (subgraph) structure of all $n$-vertex graphs.

arxiv:2610.33854.title: Between the Semi-Random Process and G(n,p)
arxiv:2610.33854.summary: We study a random graph process that connects the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph with the semi-random process. In each round, a uniformly random vertex is revealed together with a uniformly random candidate set of $s$ possible partners, and Builder chooses one of them. We study how this limited adaptivity $s$ changes the hitting times of monotone graph properties and how the familiar logarithmic ``coupon--collector'' delays in random graphs are reflected in this setting.

arxiv:2610.33858.title: The $\rm{v}$-number of $t$-closed neighborhood ideals
arxiv:2610.33858.summary: We give a combinatorial characterization of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal associated to a graph $G$, and investigate its relation with other invariants such as the $t$-domination number and the smallest size of a ball of radius $t$ in the graph $G$. We present several new cases where it is satisfied that the $\rm{v}$-number is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity. We analyze the behavior of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal with respect to the parameter $t$.
arxiv:2610.33858.authors: Delio Jaramillo-Velez, Hiram H. L\'opez, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e, Nart Shalqini

arxiv:2610.33864.title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
arxiv:2610.33864.summary: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions.

arxiv:2610.33867.title: Dancing circles
arxiv:2610.33867.summary: Recent results on diffeomorphisms of $4$-manifolds make essential use of families of embeddings of $1$-manifolds into $4$-manifolds. We survey what is currently known about such families.

arxiv:2610.33869.title: On Lewis's homotopy in distance-regular graphs
arxiv:2610.33869.summary: In 2000, Lewis introduced a nested sequence of normal subgroups of the fundamental group of a distance-regular graph $\Gamma$. While the full homotopy group itself is simply a free group, it is interesting to determine the smallest integer $k$ such that every closed walk in $\Gamma$ can be built, up to homotopy, from closed walks of "essential length" $k$ or less. Lewis proved that $k\le 6$ for any $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $\Gamma$ that is not a pseudoquotient.
arxiv:2610.33869.authors: MollyAnn Burkey, William J. Martin, Freud Oulon

arxiv:2610.33875.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
arxiv:2610.33875.summary: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is not homeomorphic to a line and, provided that it has codimension at least $2$, cannot have a single end at infinity.
arxiv:2610.33875.authors: Francisco Braun, Zbigniew Jelonek, Maria Michalska

arxiv:2610.33890.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
arxiv:2610.33890.summary: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$.

arxiv:2610.33903.title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
arxiv:2610.33903.summary: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets.

arxiv:2610.33913.title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
arxiv:2610.33913.summary: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$.
arxiv:2610.33913.authors: M. Matushko, A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov

arxiv:2610.33914.title: Improved Bounds on Proportional Choice Numbers
arxiv:2610.33914.summary: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\chi_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. We consider two previously posed questions regarding proportional choice numbers: (1) Is there a constant $C$ such that $\chi_{pc}(P_n) \leq C$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$? and (2) Is it the case that for any graph $G$, $\chi_{pc}(G) \leq \Delta(G)+1$ where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$?

arxiv:2610.33919.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
arxiv:2610.33919.summary: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. For the converse, an endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one gives rise to a family of holonomic $A_2$-modules over finite fields. One needs to lift this family to an $A_2$-module in characteristic zero with the prescribed arithmetic support.

arxiv:2610.33948.title: Delta Characters and Ranks of Minimal Subisocrystals of Abelian Schemes
arxiv:2610.33948.summary: Using the framework of delta characters on arithmetic jet spaces, we construct a canonical sequence of filtered isocrystals associated to an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a $p$-adically complete discrete valuation ring. These isocrystals map injectively via a canonical morphism into the first (rational) crystalline cohomology group $\mathbf{H}^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A)$ of the abelian scheme $A$, directly generalizing a prior construction due to Borger and Saha. Pandit showed that the canonical morphism is a map of isocrystals.

arxiv:2610.33963.title: Nilpotent Lie algebras of nilpotence class at most three via graphs
arxiv:2610.33963.summary: In this work, we associate with each finite simple graph $G$ a nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}_G$ of class at most three, whose underlying vector space has a basis indexed by the vertices, edges, and paths of length two of $G$. Its nilpotency class is exactly three if and only if $G$ contains a path of length two. We compute the dimensions of its lower central series and describe its center.
arxiv:2610.33963.authors: Andrea L. Gallo, Denis E. Videla

arxiv:2610.33971.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
arxiv:2610.33971.summary: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over…

arxiv:2610.33976.title: Explicit weighing matrices $W(n,k)$ for all $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ with $4 \le n \le 108$, and all $1 \le k \le n$
arxiv:2610.33976.summary: We present an explicit weighing matrix $W(n,k)$ for every order $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ with $4\le n\le 108$ and every weight $1\le k\le n$: 1512 matrices in total, each checked in exact integer arithmetic. Of these, 961 come from classical constructions (identity, direct sums, Kronecker products, Paley matrices and skew-Hadamard doubling) and 551 are Goethals-Seidel matrices, found by exhaustive search (24 matrices, $n\le 24$) or by simulated annealing on the periodic autocorrelation cost (527 matrices, $n\ge 28$). The note is self-contained as far as the methods are concerned: it presents all the construction methods used and the algorithm that selects among them, explains the algorithm step…

arxiv:2610.33978.title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
arxiv:2610.33978.summary: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known.
arxiv:2610.33978.authors: Feng Deng, Jing Jian Li, Hao Yu

arxiv:2610.33990.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
arxiv:2610.33990.summary: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2\xi_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}\xi_0^2\xi_1+\xi_0\xi_4-\xi_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent.

arxiv:2610.34022.title: Derived products and completion defects of inverse limits
arxiv:2610.34022.summary: We compute derived products and inverse limits in Grothendieck categories by exact coresolutions. For the product of $r$ doubled affine lines over $B[s]$, where $B$ is any nonzero commutative ring,the exact dimensions of products, epimorphic countable limits, and arbitrary countable limits are $r$, $r$, and $r+1$. We identify the top derived functors for every $B$-module of coefficients.
arxiv:2610.34022.authors: Rui Zeng (Sichuan Normal University), Guocheng Dai (Sichuan Normal University)

arxiv:2610.34038.title: Extremal 3-uniform hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles
arxiv:2610.34038.summary: Let $f_r(n)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph in which all disjoint pairs of edges have distinct unions. In 1977, Erd\H{o}s posed the problem of determining $f_r(n)$ and, in particular, asked whether $f_3(n)=O(n^2)$. F\"uredi later proved that $\binom{n-1}{r-1}+\left\lfloor (n-1)/r\right\rfloor \le f_r(n)<\frac72\binom{n}{r-1}$ for $r\ge3$ and $n\ge2r$.

arxiv:2610.34050.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
arxiv:2610.34050.summary: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.
arxiv:2610.34050.authors: Hao Guo, Chenxi Wang, Guoliang Yu

arxiv:2610.34065.title: Spectral Tur\'an problems for complete bipartite expansions in linear hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.34065.summary: An $r$-uniform hypergraph is linear if any two edges share at most one vertex. For a family $\mathcal F$ of $r$-graphs, let $\text{ex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,\mathcal F)$ denote, respectively, the maximum number of edges and the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $\mathcal F$-free linear $r$-graph. In this paper, we show that for $t\ge s\ge3$, $\text{spex}^{\text{lin}}_r(n,K_{s,t}^{+})\le \frac{(t-s+1)^{1/s}}{r-1}n^{1-1/s}+o(n^{1-1/s})$, where $K_{s,t}^{+}$ is the $r$-graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{s,t}$ by enlarging each edge with $r-2$ new vertices.

arxiv:2610.34068.title: Thermodynamic formalism for partially hyperbolic endomorphisms with critical set
arxiv:2610.34068.summary: We study the thermodynamic formalism of a broad class of partially hyperbolic, non-uniformly expanding endomorphisms with critical set, and show that they admit unique equilibrium states for all H\"older potentials of small variation. In particular, our results yield uniqueness of equilibrium states for Viana maps with small variation H\"older potentials, for non-uniformly expanding interval maps with finitely many critical points and hyperbolic H\"older potentials, and for Benedicks-Carleson quadratic maps with arbitrary H\"older potentials.

arxiv:2610.34076.title: Hausdorff and Packing Measures for $\beta$-L{\"u}roth Infinite Iterated Function Systems
arxiv:2610.34076.summary: We study the Hausdorff and packing measures of attractors generated by infinite $\beta$-L\"uroth iterated function systems. Let $I\subset\mathbb N$ be infinite and let $\dim_H E_I=h$. For a regular system, we first give conditions for the positivity of $\mathcal H^h(E_I)$ and the finiteness of $\mathcal P^h(E_I)$ in terms of first-level L\"uroth intervals.

arxiv:2610.34114.title: Minimum Distance Spectral Radius of Tree with Given Maximum Degree
arxiv:2610.34114.summary: In this article, the unique graph with minimum distance spectral radius among trees with given order $n$ and maximum degree $\varDelta$ is determined, where $2\varDelta+1 \leq n \leq \varDelta^{2} +1$ for $\varDelta \geq 3$. This article is a part proof of the conjecture proposed in $\cite{ref1}$.

arxiv:2610.34115.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi Group
arxiv:2610.34115.summary: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. The proof combines the Diophantine-approximation method of Ziyang Gao and the author (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22285) with Lefschetz fibrations. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.

arxiv:2610.34118.title: A planar signed graph with circular chromatic number five
arxiv:2610.34118.summary: A circular $r$-coloring of a signed graph maps its vertices to a circle of circumference $r\ge2$, with the endpoints of negative edges at circular distance at least $1$ and those of positive edges at most $r/2-1$; the circular chromatic number is the infimum of such $r$. We construct a simple planar signed triangulation on $85$ vertices with circular chromatic number exactly $5$. This improves the lower bound on the supremum of the circular chromatic numbers of simple planar signed graphs from $14/3$ to $5$, giving a partial answer to a question posed by Naserasr, Wang, and Zhu.

arxiv:2610.34119.title: A nonstandard selfinjective algebra of Euclidean type
arxiv:2610.34119.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$. We realize the four-dimensional selfinjective algebra $\Omega(1)$ as an admissible infinite cyclic orbit algebra of the repetitive Kronecker category. Thus an algebra long stated to be nonstandard is of Euclidean type in the orbit-algebra sense.

arxiv:2610.34155.title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
arxiv:2610.34155.summary: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps.
arxiv:2610.34155.authors: Suverchla Arora, Meenakshi Rana, Shruti Sharma, Nilanjan Bag

arxiv:2610.34160.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
arxiv:2610.34160.summary: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences.

arxiv:2610.34189.title: J\'onsson cardinals, Magidor cardinals, and the number of omitted colors
arxiv:2610.34189.summary: Let $\lambda$ be a Magidor cardinal and let $\alpha\in[\alpha_M,\lambda)$. We show that $\lambda\rightarrow[\lambda]^{\aleph_0-bd}_{\alpha,<\alpha}$. We prove the consistency of a similar statement for J\'onsson cardinals.

arxiv:2610.34193.title: Crossed modularity of twisted VOA modules
arxiv:2610.34193.summary: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. Using the $G$-crossed braided fusion structure of twisted modules constructed in \cite{Crossed}, we prove that the conformal twist $e^{2\pi iL(0)}$ gives a crossed ribbon structure and that the crossed category is modular in Kirillov's sense. Consequently, its equivariantization is a modular tensor category.

arxiv:2610.34196.title: The \(\mathcal A_\alpha\)-Spectral Tur\'an Problem for \(s\)-Clique Tensors of \(K_{r+1}\)-Free Graphs
arxiv:2610.34196.summary: For fixed $r\geq3$ and $0<\alpha<1$, we study the maximum $\alpha$-$s$-clique spectral radius among $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graphs. Here $\mathcal A_{\alpha,s}(G)=\alpha\mathcal D_s(G)+(1-\alpha)\mathcal A_s(G)$, where $\mathcal A_s(G)$ and $\mathcal D_s(G)$ are the adjacency and degree tensors of the $s$-clique hypergraph of $G$. For $s=r$, put $c_r=((r-1)/r)^{r-1}$.

arxiv:2610.34201.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions II: quadratic differential equations
arxiv:2610.34201.summary: We investigate differential equations defined through elements of a nonassociative five-dimensional real algebra $\mathcal A_\gamma$, and show that every system of quadratic differential equations $\dot p=F(p)$ on $\mathbb R^5$ can be written as a differential equation over such a non-flexible quadratic algebra. We then study quadratic differential equations and their solutions over the whole family $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ of algebras while varying $\gamma$ across the parameter interval $[0,1]$, exploiting the fact that by definition, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra and that $\mathcal A_1=\mathbb{P}$ is the real Pentarnion algebra. We construct…

arxiv:2610.34202.title: A Five-Dimensional Nonassociative Algebra: elliptic integrability and bracketing-dependent dynamics
arxiv:2610.34202.summary: We introduce a five-dimensional nonassociative real algebra $\mathbb{P}$ whose one-generated subalgebras are complex while its left, middle, and right nuclei are all $\mathbb{R}$. This contrast permits an unambiguous one-element functional calculus but makes polynomial ordinary differential equations sensitive to bracketing. We classify the homogeneous quadratic words containing one fixed coefficient $B$ and two copies of $p$ that preserve $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{1,B,p\}$.

arxiv:2610.34209.title: Finiteness of ergodic measures of maximal entropy for certain skew product systems
arxiv:2610.34209.summary: Consider a $C^{1+\beta}$ skew product $F$ over a topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphism $f$, with fiber dynamics driven by a $C^{1+\beta}$ $\mathbb{R}^k$-action $\{\rho_{\bf t}\}$ on a closed manifold $Y$ through a $C^{1+\beta}$ cocycle $\tau$. Suppose that the fiber action preserves an ergodic smooth measure of maximal entropy $m_{\operatorname{MME}}$. Under a nondegeneracy condition called joint nontriviality, and assuming that each element $\rho_{\bf t}$ is either of class $C^\infty$ or hyperbolic, we prove that $F$ admits only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy.

arxiv:2610.34225.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
arxiv:2610.34225.summary: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions.

arxiv:2610.34228.title: Bistable fronts in periodic media: phase reduction and realization of circle flows
arxiv:2610.34228.summary: We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts.
arxiv:2610.34228.authors: Weiwei Ding, Xing Liang, Linfeng Xu

arxiv:2610.34243.title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
arxiv:2610.34243.summary: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence.

arxiv:2610.34254.title: General-position sets and linear hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.34254.summary: We prove that every linear hypergraph on $N$ vertices with edge sizes $O(\sqrt N)$ and $O(N^2\log N)$ triples contained in its edges has a subset of size $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ meeting each edge in at most two vertices. As an application, every set of $N$ planar points with at most $\sqrt N$ collinear points contains $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ points in general position. This proves a conjecture of Payne and Wood and gives the optimal quadratic bound for a geometric Ramsey problem posed by Gowers.
arxiv:2610.34254.authors: Thang Pham, Le Quang-Ham, Boqing Xue

arxiv:2610.34265.title: Network of limit sets in dynamical systems
arxiv:2610.34265.summary: Points within a topological dynamical systems can be separated into transient and recurrent points. Most of the asymptotic properties of the dynamics is borne by the closure of the collection of recurrent points. This article presents a representation scheme for dynamics using the connectivity information in terms of the recurrent set.

arxiv:2610.34273.title: Asymptotic Rank of Complete Graph Tensors
arxiv:2610.34273.summary: Graph tensors extend the matrix multiplication tensor by placing a two-party identity tensor on every edge of a graph and keeping one tensor leg at every vertex. We study the asymptotic rank of the tensor associated with the complete graph. For every integer $n\geq 2$, over the complex numbers, we prove \[ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor \leq \log_2\widetilde R\bigl(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n)\bigr) \leq \frac{n^2}{4}.

arxiv:2610.34288.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
arxiv:2610.34288.summary: The Characterization Problem asks whether a finite abelian group with Davenport constant at least four is determined, up to isomorphism, by its system of length sets. This is a central inverse problem in non-unique factorization theory: it asks whether the possible numbers of irreducible factors retain enough information to recover the underlying class group. For rings of integers of algebraic number fields, an affirmative answer means that the ideal class group can be recovered from these factorization lengths alone.

arxiv:2610.34291.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
arxiv:2610.34291.summary: We prove that for all $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the Lee ball $B_n(r)$ does not tile $\Z^n$ by translations, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets and completing the existence classification of perfect Lee codes in $\Z^n$. The proof combines translation-invariant averaging, boundary contact identities, and integer moment inequalities with coefficient comparisons in stable symmetric functions. Consequently, we obtain finite local obstructions, strict Banach density gaps for packings and coverings, and the nonexistence of exact measurable Lee-ball towers.
arxiv:2610.34291.authors: Bocong Chen, Jing Huang, Gaojun Luo

arxiv:2610.34300.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
arxiv:2610.34300.summary: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one.

arxiv:2610.34301.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
arxiv:2610.34301.summary: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(e\pi n)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_{\mu}(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $\psi$…

arxiv:2610.34306.title: Constellations for Lyapunov exponents
arxiv:2610.34306.summary: We study the maximal Lyapunov exponent of random products of positive matrices, and prove that it can be calculated to arbitrary precision with arithmetic work polynomial in the number of requested digits. In nondegenerate settings, the complexity of our method depends on the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics---which we characterize---and not on the Euclidean dimension of the ambient space in which the dynamics live. As numerical applications, we determine the Hausdorff dimension of random intersections of Sierpi\'nski gaskets, and Viswanath's constant---the growth rate of the random Fibonacci sequence.

arxiv:2610.34307.title: Sharp bounds for Duke--Erd\H{o}s--R\"odl problems on cycle-connected subgraphs
arxiv:2610.34307.summary: For $k\ge2$, a graph is $C_{2k}$-connected if every two distinct edges lie together on an even cycle of length at most $2k$ in that graph. Let $f_k(n,m)$ be the largest number of edges in a $C_{2k}$-connected subgraph that every $n$-vertex graph with $m$ edges must contain. In this paper, we study two cycle-connected problems raised by Duke, Erd\H{o}s and R\"odl.

arxiv:2610.34323.title: The measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups
arxiv:2610.34323.summary:
In this article we show that all the nonamenable Baumslag-Solitar groups with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree, i.e., $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ with $|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p|
eq |q|$, are measure equivalent to each other, thereby completing the measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups: each $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ belongs to one of three measure equivalence classes according to whether it is amenable ($|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$), virtually isomorphic to $\mathbf{F}_n 	imes \mathbf{Z}$ ($|p|=|q|
eq 1$), or is nonamenable with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree ($|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p| 
eq |q|$). More generally, we obtain the similar classification of the generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups of…
arxiv:2610.34323.authors: Damien Gaboriau, Antoine Poulin, Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob, Konrad Wr\'obel

arxiv:2610.34324.title: Optimal solution ranks in the Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation
arxiv:2610.34324.summary: For every $n$ and $r$ with $1\le r$ and $\binom{r+1}{2}\le n$, we construct a connected unweighted graph on $n$ vertices whose Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation has a unique optimal solution of rank $r$. The main examples are the Kneser graphs $K(m,2)$, whose unique optima have rank $m-1$. A six-vertex wheel supplies rank three, and attaching pendant vertices preserves both rank and uniqueness.

arxiv:2610.34328.title: On first-order limiting probabilities for small permutation classes
arxiv:2610.34328.summary: Given a small permutation class $\mathcal{P}$, we consider the set of possible limits of the probability $\mathbb{P}\big(\mathbf{\sigma}_n \models \Psi\big)$ that a uniformly chosen random permutation $\mathbf{\sigma}_n\in \mathcal{P}_n$ satisfies a fixed first-order sentence in Theory of Two Orders (TOTO). In the case of small permutation classes with polynomial growth, we show this limit set is finite, and characterize the set explicitly. In particular, we prove that many natural small permutation classes of polynomial growth arising from permutation matrices satisfy a $0$-$1$ convergence law, and have an infinite model.
arxiv:2610.34328.authors: Victor Falgas-Ravry, Klas Markstr\"om, Eero R\"aty, Fiona Skerman

arxiv:2610.34332.title: Automatic cocommutativity for the quantum-group comonad
arxiv:2610.34332.summary: We prove that the cofree Hopf algebra on a cocommutative bialgebra is again cocommutative, and in fact coincides with the latter's largest Hopf subalgebra. This answers a question of Ardizzoni-Menini-Saracco and provides a proof for a statement to the same effect in the literature, whose original justification contains an apparent gap. The result relies on (and is in fact equivalent to) the observation that cocommutative bialgebra quotients of arbitrary Hopf algebras are automatically Hopf.

arxiv:2610.34361.title: A general algebraic characterization of extremal $\Delta$-trees and $k$-cyclic graphs for degree-homogeneous VDB indices
