To this end we define a motivic analog of the Steenrod power operations, using the theory of normed motivic spectra as developed by Bachmann--Hoyois and their application for the definition of motivic colimits as developed by Bachmann-Elmanto-Heller.

arxiv:2610.35911.title: A vanishing-cycle obstruction to smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds
arxiv:2610.35911.summary: We prove a homological obstruction to smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees six and seven. On a crepant resolution that is small over the nodes and blows up the cone vertices, any smoothing forces a relation among link classes bounding in the local Milnor fibers. The relation is nonzero at every node and degree-seven point, and at each degree-six point smoothed through the one-dimensional component.

arxiv:2610.35913.title: Nonvanishing implies abundance
arxiv:2610.35913.summary: We prove that the nonvanishing conjecture implies the abundance conjecture.

arxiv:2610.35914.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
arxiv:2610.35914.summary: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus.

arxiv:2610.35915.title: Smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and del Pezzo cone points
arxiv:2610.35915.summary: We give a necessary and sufficient homological criterion for smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, or over a smooth quadric surface. For some choice of local smoothing components, the criterion requires a relation on a crepant resolution among link classes whose associated local parameters avoid every discriminant. The complexified relation space describes first-order deformations modulo locally trivial ones.

arxiv:2610.35916.title: Finite Symplectic Automorphisms of Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-Type Act Trivially on Discriminant Groups
arxiv:2610.35916.summary: We give an alternative proof of Mongardi's result that every finite group of symplectic automorphisms of a hyperk\"ahler manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type acts trivially on the discriminant groups of its second cohomology lattice and its coinvariant lattice. The proof combines sphere-packing bounds, Vinberg's reflection chambers and structure results on even $2$-elementary lattices.
arxiv:2610.35916.authors: Jie Fu, Shihao Wang, Zhiwei Zheng

arxiv:2610.35918.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
arxiv:2610.35918.summary: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

arxiv:2610.35920.title: Geometric priors for single-patch neural Calabi--Yau metrics on the quintic: a conservative fixed-$\psi$ Ablation study
arxiv:2610.35920.summary: We investigate how geometric priors shape neural approximations of the complex Monge--Amp`ere equation on the quintic Calabi--Yau threefold. This fixed-$\psi$ diagnostic compares four single-patch ans"atze: a coordinate SIREN potential model, a direct-metric Cholesky baseline, an algebraic section ansatz, and a section-plus-neural hybrid. In a 96-run learning-rate and frequency archive, section-based models reach validation $\sigma=4.14$--$4.16%$, whereas SIREN and Cholesky remain at $41.29%$ and $44.27%$.

arxiv:2610.35922.title: On Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves and degeneracy loci formulas
arxiv:2610.35922.summary: In this research article, we make an in-depth investigation of the computations for Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves germs in the plane and space cases using the framework established by Ohmoto and the Restriction Method introduced by Rim\'anyi, and we also propose a geometric way for such computations using degeneracy loci Chern classes formulas proven by Fulton, which seems a promising way to generalize the Thom Polynomial expression for the stabilization of such singularities in $\mathbb{C}^N$, depending exclusively on $N$ as a parameter.

arxiv:2610.35923.title: On Open Borel Orbits in Conormal Bundles to Schubert Cells
arxiv:2610.35923.summary: Let $C(v)$ denote a Schubert cell in the flag variety $\operatorname{GL}_n/B$, and let $X(w)$ be a Schubert variety containing $C(v)$. Mellit has conjectured that, if $X(w)$ is smooth, the existence of an open $B$-orbit in the conormal bundle to $C(v)$ in $X(w)$ is equivalent to $C(w_0w)$ being contained in the smooth locus of $X(w_0v)$. We prove a stronger version of this conjecture, requiring only that $X(w)$ is factorial.

arxiv:2610.35943.title: Combinatorial description of the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality
arxiv:2610.35943.summary: We prove an explicit correspondence between the irreducible finite dimensional representations of the mirabolic quantum group $MU(n)$ and those of the mirabolic Hecke algebra $MH_d$ given by the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality. In particular, this resolves a generalization of a conjecture by the second author. The proof is via a careful analysis of the $MU(n)$-weight spaces and the eigenvalues of the Jucys Murphy elements of $MH_d$ on the mirabolic tensor space.

arxiv:2610.35944.title: When Polynomial Multiplication Counts Geometry: Schubert Polynomials and Monk's Rule
arxiv:2610.35944.summary: We give a geometric introduction to Schubert polynomial multiplication through point-line flags in the complex projective plane. Moving a prescribed point onto a prescribed line gives a family with local equation $au=\lambda$, whose limiting curve has two components. The incidence equations and their local multiplicities give a two-term divisor product, using the standard intersection product on classes of algebraic cycles.

arxiv:2610.35968.title: On the frieze patterns by Conway and Coxeter
arxiv:2610.35968.summary: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s.

arxiv:2610.35970.title: Average eccentricity in k-connected tournaments
arxiv:2610.35970.summary: The average eccentricity $\avec(D)$ of a strong digraph $D$ is the mean eccentricity of all vertices in $D$. A tournament $T$ is an orientation of a complete graph. In this paper, we prove that the average eccentricity satisfies $2 \le \avec(T) < \frac{n}{2k} + \frac{11}{2} + \frac{k}{8n}$ for a $k$-connected tournament $T$ of order $n$.

arxiv:2610.35976.title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
arxiv:2610.35976.summary: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.

arxiv:2610.35988.title: A generalization of pseudocomplementation in semilattices, lattices and posets with 0
arxiv:2610.35988.summary: Pseudocomplemented lattices satisfy a lot of nice properties and were studied by a number of algebraists. However, even when a poset P with 0 is not pseudocomplemented, we can assign to every element a of P the set $a^p$ of all maximal elements being orthogonal to a. This assignment $^p$ is a non-trivial operator provided P satisfies the so-called Ascending Chain Condition (ACC).

arxiv:2610.36029.title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
arxiv:2610.36029.summary: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^\omega(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $\omega\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,\gamma,\epsilon)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin…

arxiv:2610.36069.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
arxiv:2610.36069.summary: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

arxiv:2610.36072.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
arxiv:2610.36072.summary: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

arxiv:2610.36119.title: Fukaya categories of surfaces with DG coefficients
arxiv:2610.36119.summary: Given a compact surface $S$ admitting a Liouville form, a finite set $Q \subset S$, a line field on $S$, and a local system of dg-categories on $S \setminus Q$ together with a section of the monodromy functor around each interior $q \in Q$, we construct a Fukaya category. We give examples where such Fukaya categories are quasi-equivalent to derived categories of projective completions of line bundles and of iterated blow-ups of the affine plane; and to wrapped Fukaya categories of cotangent bundles of spheres. We define two versions of the Fukaya category, a topological, which is constructed combinatorially from a full arc system, and a geometric, which includes all Lagrangian branes…

arxiv:2610.36120.title: Existence of uniformly most reliable two-terminal graphs with distance constraints
arxiv:2610.36120.summary: A two-terminal graph is a simple graph equipped with two distinguished vertices, called terminals. Let $T_{n,m}$ be the class consisting of all non-isomorphic two-terminal graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. Let $G$ be any two-terminal graph in $T_{n,m}$, and let $d$ be any positive integer.

arxiv:2610.36127.title: Trace-minimal graphs maximizing the number of spanning trees
arxiv:2610.36127.summary: A classical problem in spectral graph theory is to determine, among all simple graphs with a fixed number of vertices and edges, those that maximize the number of spanning trees. Such graphs are called $t$-optimal. Petingi and Rodr\'iguez [Discr.

arxiv:2610.36130.title: Uniform local models of quasi-unipotent $p$-adic differential equations
arxiv:2610.36130.summary: We construct uniform analytic models of quasi-unipotent differential modules over Robba rings. For modules of rank at most $r$ and highest ramification break at most $b$, the inner radius of the model annulus depends only on $r,b$ and the residue characteristic $p$. At each radius, the model admits a basis, possibly depending on the radius, in which the connection matrix is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,b,p$.

arxiv:2610.36132.title: Hankel determinants for the $(n+2)$-shifted $q$-metallic numbers
arxiv:2610.36132.summary: Let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $q$-deformation (in the sense of Morier-Genoud & Ovsienko) of the metallic number $\phi_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$. This is a power series with integer coefficients. We prove that the Hankel continued fraction of the $(n+2)$-shifted series $\Phi_n^{(n+2)}$ is eventually periodic, and that the corresponding Hankel determinant sequence $\Delta^{(n+2)}$ is $2n(n+1)$-periodic if $n$ is even, $2n(n+1)$-antiperiodic if $n$ is odd, and that it takes only the values $-2,-1,0,1,2$.

arxiv:2610.36136.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
arxiv:2610.36136.summary: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).
arxiv:2610.36136.authors: Herbert Gangl, Paul E. Gunnells, Dan Yasaki

arxiv:2610.36165.title: A new infinite family of covers of complete graphs that admit a half-transitive action of a Suzuki simple group
arxiv:2610.36165.summary: We construct a new infinite family of antipodal $2(q-1)$-covers of complete graphs $K_{q^2+1}$ of diameter $3$, where $q=2^{2e+1}\ge 8$, admitting a half-transitive action of the Suzuki simple group $Sz(q)$. We further show that each constructed cover admits an involutory automorphism interchanging the two $Sz(q)$-orbits on arcs, which yields that its full automorphism group is arc-transitive.

arxiv:2610.36179.title: Mutation-acyclicity in rank four is decidable but not semialgebraic
arxiv:2610.36179.summary: We prove that mutation-acyclicity of quivers on four vertices is decidable. If a four-vertex quiver $Q$ is mutation-acyclic, then some sequence of mutations takes it to an acyclic quiver without any arrow multiplicity exceeding $\operatorname{max}\{\operatorname{ht}(Q),m(Q)\}$, where $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ is the largest arrow multiplicity of $Q$ and $m(Q)$ is the Markov invariant of Fomin and Neville evaluated on the totally proper wiggle class of $Q$. A search within a computable form of this bound decides mutation-acyclicity of four-vertex quivers with $O(h^{24})$ states for input height $h\ge1$.
arxiv:2610.36179.authors: Kymani T. K. Armstrong-Williams, Edward Hirst, Blake Jackson, Kyu-Hwan Lee

arxiv:2610.36207.title: On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets
arxiv:2610.36207.summary: A Sidon set is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that if $0\neq a-b=c-d$ and $a,b,c,d\in\mathcal{A}$, then $(a,b)=(c,d)$. Our main result is an improved and explicit bound on the diameter of a Sidon set: if $\mathcal{A}$ is a Sidon set with $k\ge 1$ elements, then \[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2 \left(\frac{1}{1 + 0.945/\sqrt{k}}-\frac{0.945}{\sqrt k}\right) -1;\] in particular, $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\ge k^2-1.89 k^{3/2}$. This implies that if $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[1,N]$ is a Sidon set, then $|\mathcal{A}| \le N^{1/2}+0.945 \, N^{1/4}+0.447$.
arxiv:2610.36207.authors: Daniel Carter, Kevin O'Bryant, Terence Tao

arxiv:2610.36211.title: Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces
arxiv:2610.36211.summary: Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.

arxiv:2610.36212.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
arxiv:2610.36212.summary: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator.

arxiv:2610.36216.title: Computer-assisted proofs of periodic solutions of state-dependent delay equations beyond perturbative regimes
arxiv:2610.36216.summary: Rigorous existence results for periodic solutions of state-dependent delay differential equations (SDDEs) are scarce outside perturbative regimes, where the equation is close to an ordinary or constant-delay differential equation. We develop a computer-assisted framework that proves the existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs directly. The numerical approximation is a trigonometric polynomial, and a true periodic solution nearby is obtained by a Newton--Kantorovich argument in the space of $C^1$ periodic functions.
arxiv:2610.36216.authors: Jan Bouwe van den Berg, Maxime Breden, Matthieu Cadiot, Kevin E. M. Church, Jean-Philippe Lessard

arxiv:2610.36231.title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles
arxiv:2610.36231.summary: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and ${\mathcal E}^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using the latter and some recent examples of [A1] in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$.

arxiv:2610.36251.title: Rank two cohomology jump loci on projective varieties
arxiv:2610.36251.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective variety. We give a structure theorem for irreducible components of the reduced rank-two cohomology jump loci on $X$. More precisely, for such a component $Z$, if the general point of $Z$ is projectively virtually abelian or projectively rigid, then either $Z$ is a symmetric square of an algebraic torus, or a quotient of a torus by an involution, or its normalization $Z^{\nu}$ is a torus.

arxiv:2610.36259.title: Filling knots and essential geodesic systole
arxiv:2610.36259.summary: We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023].

arxiv:2610.36273.title: Characterizing $3$-graphs with Degenerate Codegree Tur\'an Density
arxiv:2610.36273.summary: Determining the Tur\'an densities $\pi(F)$, uniform Tur\'an densities $\pi_{\therefore}(F)$, and codegree Tur\'an densities $\gamma(F)$ of $3$-graphs $F$ is a notoriously difficult problem in combinatorics. A landmark result by Erd\H{o}s characterized the $3$-graphs whose Tur\'an density is zero. Half a century later, Reiher, R\"{o}dl, and Schacht characterized the $3$-graphs whose uniform Tur\'an density is zero.
arxiv:2610.36273.authors: Dylan King, Sim\'on Piga, Marcelo Sales, Bjarne Sch\"{u}lke

arxiv:2610.36276.title: Edge complexity of complete bipartite and complete multipartite graphs
arxiv:2610.36276.summary: We study edge complexity, the minimum Fourier $\ell^1/\ell^2$ ratio of a graph's adjacency matrix over cyclic vertex labelings. For $K_{m,n}$, with $1\leq m\leq n$, we reduce the problem to minimizing the Fourier $\ell^1$-norm of indicators of $m$-element subsets of $\mathbb Z_{m+n}$. We prove the sharp bound $\operatorname{FR}_{\min}(K_{m,n})\geq\frac{4n^2}{(m+n)\sqrt{2mn}}$, with equality precisely when $m\mid n$, and classify all labelings attaining it.
arxiv:2610.36276.authors: S. Ferguson, V. Gupta, A. Iosevich, J. Iosevich, C. Kelly, G. Smith, S. Yang

arxiv:2610.36277.title: BV structure on the Hochschild cohomology of Liu-Schulz algebras in characteristic two
arxiv:2610.36277.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $2$, let $\rho\in K^\times$, and let $R_\rho$ be the corresponding Liu-Schulz algebra. We give a complete description of the Gerstenhaber bracket and the BV structure on the Hochschild cohomology ring $\operatorname{HH}^*(R_\rho)$.

arxiv:2610.36279.title: Boundary and Interior of Root Sets of Power Series
arxiv:2610.36279.summary: In this paper we study the set $\mathcal{M}_M$ of roots of power series with coefficients in $\{0, \pm 1, ..., \pm M \}$ and constant coefficient $1$. We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of $\mathcal{M}_M$. Moreover we establish a dimension formula and show the corresponding Hausdorff measure is finite and positive for a family of attractors parameterized by boundary parameters $\lambda \in \partial \mathcal{M}_M \setminus \mathbb{R}$.

arxiv:2610.36290.title: Cops and Robbers on Graphs without Long or Short Holes
arxiv:2610.36290.summary: In 2019, Sivaraman conjectured that every $P_k$-free graph has cop number at most $k-3$ for $k\geq 5$. Chudnovsky, Norin, Seymour, and Turcotte proved $P_5$-free graphs have cop number at most $2$. For $k\geq 6$ Sivaraman's conjecture remains widely open.

arxiv:2610.36291.title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
arxiv:2610.36291.summary: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$.

arxiv:2610.36292.title: Complete Expanding Interval Maps are Mixing
arxiv:2610.36292.summary: We give a new and elementary\footnote{That is: without functional analysis.} proof that certain smooth, complete, expanding maps from the interval to itself are mixing.
arxiv:2610.36292.authors: E. L. O'Neil, F. M. Tangerman, J. J. P. Veerman

arxiv:2610.36314.title: Sheaves on polynomials and polynomial sheaves
arxiv:2610.36314.summary: We show that several Dold-Kan type equivalences can be understood as a passage from constructible sheaves on symmetric products (i.e. spaces of polynomials) to polynomial sheaves in the sense of Goodwillie-Weiss calculus, by means of a natural analytic expansion functor. This geometric perspective provides access to standard tools from sheaf theory such as the six functor formalism and $t$-structures. For example, the equivalence between filtered objects and coherent chain complexes in a stable $\infty$-category receives a geometric incarnation as Verdier duality between $!$-sheaves and $*$-cosheaves on an $\infty$-dimensional simplex.
arxiv:2610.36314.authors: Tobias Dyckerhoff, Till Heine, Simon Schneider

arxiv:2610.36323.title: Integer points for iterated Weierstrass elliptic functions
arxiv:2610.36323.summary: Iterated Weierstrass P functions exhibit relationships between period lattices and the dynamics. We connect the dynamical properties to the occurrence of integer and rational points on associated real elliptic curves. Defining a complex number z to be an integer point if both P(z) and P'(z) are integers, we restrict to P when the lattice is real and its invariants g2 and g3 are integers.

arxiv:2610.36331.title: The unknotting problem for surfaces in the 4-sphere
arxiv:2610.36331.summary: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a closed, connected, orientable, locally flat PL surface in $S^4$ of genus at least 18 (resp. 19) is TOP (resp. PL) unknotted. We prove analogous results for non-orientable surfaces, and for surfaces in any compact PL 4-manifold.

arxiv:2610.36342.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
arxiv:2610.36342.summary: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories.
arxiv:2610.36342.authors: Emmanuel S. Ameh, Samuel E. Otto

arxiv:2610.36354.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
arxiv:2610.36354.summary: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is…
arxiv:2610.36354.authors: Karen Butt, Alena Erchenko, Tristan Humbert

arxiv:2610.36372.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
arxiv:2610.36372.summary: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology.

arxiv:2610.36377.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
arxiv:2610.36377.summary: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.

arxiv:2610.36387.title: Homological lifts of Arnold strangeness
arxiv:2610.36387.summary: We construct homological lifts of Arnold's strangeness $\operatorname{St}$ for long and closed plane curves. For long curves, we introduce a new $q$-variable quantization polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$, an edge state sum, designed for categorification and construct a triply graded homology that recovers $\operatorname{St}_q$. We prove strictness by exhibiting long curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology.

arxiv:2610.36390.title: Tropical spin Hurwitz numbers
arxiv:2610.36390.summary: We introduce a tropical framework for the study of spin Hurwitz numbers and their completed cycles analogues. We use degeneration techniques to obtain an interpretation of spin Hurwitz numbers via tropical covers. We employ the tropical methods to obtain new closed formulae for spin Hurwitz numbers in special cases.
arxiv:2610.36390.authors: Lou-Jean Leila Cobigo, Marvin Anas Hahn

arxiv:2610.36394.title: Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings
arxiv:2610.36394.summary: Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries.
arxiv:2610.36394.authors: Saul D. Freedman, Melissa Lee, Dragan Maru\v{s}i\v{c}, Toma\v{z} Pisanski

arxiv:2610.36397.title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
arxiv:2610.36397.summary: Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ \tau_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[…

arxiv:2610.36403.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
arxiv:2610.36403.summary: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schr\"odinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a…
arxiv:2610.36403.authors: David Damanik (Rice University), Long Li (Texas A&M University), Nicolae Strungaru (MacEwan University)

arxiv:2610.36417.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in eight dimensions over the field with two elements
arxiv:2610.36417.summary: Fuglede's conjecture in a finite abelian group says that a nonempty subset tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral, meaning that the space of complex-valued functions on the subset has an orthogonal basis consisting of restrictions of group characters. We prove the conjecture in the eight-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. In fact, every spectral set and every tile in this space has a tiling complement which is a linear subspace.

arxiv:2610.36451.title: Quasi-periodic tree sets and structure trees
arxiv:2610.36451.summary: We expand our discussion of the almost stability theorem of Dicks and Dunwoody in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.

arxiv:2610.36461.title: Linear Programming Upper Bounds for the Coil-in-the-Box Problem
arxiv:2610.36461.summary: Let $S_n$ denote the maximum length of a coil in the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$, i.e., a simple cycle whose induced subgraph has no additional chords. We combine classical square-counting identities and structural properties of maximum coils with new valid combinatorial inequalities into a parameterized linear program whose optimal value provides an upper bound for $S_n$. For $n\ge13$, we construct two analytic dual feasible solutions.
arxiv:2610.36461.authors: Kevin M. Byrnes, Eric T. Harley, Florin Spinu

arxiv:2610.36472.title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
arxiv:2610.36472.summary: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line.
arxiv:2610.36472.authors: Shimal Harichurn, Isabella Khan, Andr\'as N\'emethi, Josef Svoboda

arxiv:2610.36483.title: Log-concavity of longest increasing subsequence
arxiv:2610.36483.summary: We prove a conjecture proposed by Chen that, for every fixed $n$, the sequence $(a_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave, where $a_{n,k}$ counts permutations of $[n]$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$.

arxiv:2610.36495.title: Quartic Keller Maps and Tameness in Three Variables
arxiv:2610.36495.summary: We study invertibility and tameness for polynomial maps of affine three-space of total degree at most four. We prove that every complex Keller map in this degree range is a polynomial automorphism and, independently, that every complex polynomial automorphism of total degree at most four is tame. The invertibility argument combines homogeneous factorization of the leading part, invariant rings of conic pencils, and residue obstructions on cubic fibers.

arxiv:2610.36522.title: Constructions for Nearly Diagonal Book Ramsey Numbers
arxiv:2610.36522.summary: The Ramsey number $R(G_1,G_2)$ is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that for every graph $H$ on $n$ vertices, either $H$ contains a copy of $G_1$ or the complement $\overline H$ contains a copy of $G_2$. Ramsey numbers involving the book graphs $B_n$, which consist of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge, have attracted recent attention, especially in the ``nearly diagonal'' case $R(B_{n-1},B_n)$. Rousseau and Sheehan showed the upper bound $R(B_{n-1},B_n) \le 4n-1$ nearly fifty years ago, but no general matching lower bound construction is known.

arxiv:2610.36532.title: A Homological Approach to Dynamics
arxiv:2610.36532.summary: This note describes a novel approach to systematically characterize dynamics based on finite information. We present an algebraic framework for dynamics from which it is possible to deduce more traditional descriptors associated with the qualitative structures of the geometric theory of dynamical systems. The purpose of this paper is to indicate how this approach can be used to obtain interpretable characterizations of dynamics that are robust with respect to perturbations, in the context of models of multiscale and data-driven systems.
arxiv:2610.36532.authors: William Kalies, Konstantin Mischaikow, Robert Vandervorst

arxiv:2610.36547.title: On an exponent-preserving duality for Coxeter multiarrangements of type $B_2$
arxiv:2610.36547.summary: In the theory of hyperplane arrangements, the study of logarithmic derivation modules is one of the most important subjects. If the module is free over a graded ring, the multiset of degrees of its homogeneous basis is called exponents. We utilize some basic theory of linear algebra to study the exponents of multiarrangements.

arxiv:2610.36560.title: Periodic Solutions and Exponential Attractivity in Hopfield-Type Neural Networks with Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive and Nonimpulsive Cases
arxiv:2610.36560.summary: We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by $\gamma(t)=\zeta_k$ on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, where $t_k\leq\zeta_k\leq t_{k+1}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Depending on the position of $\zeta_k$, the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type.
arxiv:2610.36560.authors: Ricardo Torres Naranjo, Samuel Castillo Apolonio

arxiv:2610.36565.title: Equivalence between rationality and modular invariance under $C_2$-cofiniteness
arxiv:2610.36565.summary: We prove that for a simple and $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, the rationality is equivalent to the modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of its irreducible modules. This proves a conjecture given by Dong-Ren in \cite{DongRen}, which is also the inverse theorem of Zhu's modular invariance theorem \cite{Zhu}.
arxiv:2610.36565.authors: Hao Wang (School of Mathematics, Northwest University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China), Jiang Yang (School of Mathematical Sciences, Guangxi Minzu University, Nanning, Guangxi, China)

arxiv:2610.36566.title: Helly theorems for lattice of flats of a matroid
arxiv:2610.36566.summary: A basis of a matroid is adapted to a flat if it contains a basis of the flat. We prove that a family of flats in a rank r matroid has a common adapted basis whenever every subfamily of at most r+1 flats does. The ground set and the family may be infinite; only the rank must be finite.

arxiv:2610.36586.title: Degree-truncated DP-colouring of $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs
arxiv:2610.36586.summary: A graph $G$ is degree-truncated DP-$k$-colourable (respectively, degree-truncated $k$-choosable) if it is DP-$f$-colourable (respectively, $f$-choosable), where $f(v)=\min\{k,d_G(v)\}$ for every vertex $v$. Hutchinson proved that every $2$-connected maximal outerplanar graph other than the triangle is degree-truncated $5$-choosable. Lo, Wang, Zhou and Zhu strengthened this result by proving that every $2$-connected $K_{2,4}$-minor-free graph other than cycles and complete graphs is degree-truncated DP-$5$-colourable.

arxiv:2610.36605.title: Integral Forms of Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and Quantum Frobenius
arxiv:2610.36605.summary: For twisted quantum affine algebras, we compare Lusztig's restricted integral form with the integral form generated by group-like toral elements and divided powers of real Drinfeld current modes. The two forms coincide over $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ outside type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$. In type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$, the smallest ordinary localization over which they coincide is $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][\Phi_{4r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n=1$, and $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][\Phi_{8r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n\geq2$, where $\Phi_k(q)$ are cyclotomic polynomials.

arxiv:2610.36620.title: Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data
arxiv:2610.36620.summary: We extend the Bakry--\'Emery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,\lambda,\mu)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{\lambda+2}\] when $\mu>2$ and $k\ge3\lambda^2/\mu$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(\lambda+4)$ to a logarithmic bound.

arxiv:2610.36632.title: Non-degeneracy of Hopf triplets
arxiv:2610.36632.summary: We study the relationship between semisimplicity and non-degeneracy for finite-dimensional Hopf triplets over a field of characteristic zero. The non-degeneracy condition appears in the construction of \(4\)-manifold invariants from Hopf triplets, and it was not known whether non-semisimple examples satisfying this condition exist. We prove that a Hopf triplet is non-degenerate if and only if it is semisimple.

arxiv:2610.36638.title: Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities
arxiv:2610.36638.summary: For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplus\Lambda^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra…

arxiv:2610.36644.title: Reflection equations and Littlewood identities for spin Hall-Littlewood and $q$-Whittaker functions
arxiv:2610.36644.summary: We describe two-parametric Littlewood identities for inhomogeneous stable spin Hall-Littlewood and inhomogeneous spin $q$-Whittaker symmetric functions. These identities generalize the Littlewood identity found by Warnaar (2006) for the ordinary Hall-Littlewood polynomials. However, instead of Rogers-Szeg\"o coefficients used by Warnaar, coefficients in our identities are given by products of Al-Salam-Chihara polynomials.

arxiv:2610.36648.title: An upper bound of 61 for the Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$
arxiv:2610.36648.summary: We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 61. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers.

arxiv:2610.36656.title: Cluster type smooth Fano threefolds
arxiv:2610.36656.summary: We prove that most rational smooth Fano threefolds are compactifications of $\mathbb{G}_m^3$. More precisely, we study which smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type, i.e., for which smooth Fano threefolds $X$ one can find a boundary $B\in |-K_X|$ and an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow X\setminus B$. We prove that many important classes of smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type.
arxiv:2610.36656.authors: Eduardo Alves da Silva, Fernando Figueroa, Jos\'e Ignacio Y\'a\~nez, Joaqu\'in Moraga

arxiv:2610.36675.title: New upper bounds for average kissing numbers
arxiv:2610.36675.summary: A packing of balls in Euclidean space is a set of balls with non-overlapping interiors. For a finite packing of balls, its average contact number is the average number of balls tangent to a ball in this packing, that is, twice the total number of tangencies divided by the number of balls. The average kissing number of the space is defined as the supremum of average contact numbers over all finite ball packings.

arxiv:2610.36688.title: Jack multiple zeta function
arxiv:2610.36688.summary: For conjugate shapes $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_\lambda(x;\alpha)$ and $J_{\lambda'}(x;1/\alpha)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes.

arxiv:2610.36736.title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture
arxiv:2610.36736.summary: Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $\delta_i(g)=X_i$ and $\delta^\alpha(g)=(\partial^\alpha h^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition.

arxiv:2610.36749.title: Negative edge correlation in complete bipartite graphs
arxiv:2610.36749.summary: We prove strict pairwise negative correlation under both the uniform forest measure and the uniform connected-subgraph measure on the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$ for all $m,n\geq2$. Under the connected-subgraph measure, any two distinct edges of a fixed copy of $K_{2,2}$ remain strictly negatively correlated after conditioning on the subgraph induced by the remaining vertices.

arxiv:2610.36802.title: Decompositions of birational toric morphism between threefolds
arxiv:2610.36802.summary: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a birational morphism between smooth projective threefolds, Koll\'ar asked that if $f$ could be decomposed into smooth blow-downs and smooth flops. In this paper we show that the toric version is true.

arxiv:2610.36815.title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
arxiv:2610.36815.summary: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.
arxiv:2610.36815.authors: Yuxuan Chen, Armen Shirikyan, Shengquan Xiang

arxiv:2610.36821.title: The Edge Geodesic Transversal Problem
arxiv:2610.36821.summary: For a given connected graph $G(V,E)$, the geodesic transversal problem finds a set $S$ of vertices of $G$ with minimum cardinality such that every maximal geodesic of $G$ contains at least one vertex of $S$. The cardinality of such a smallest set $S$ is called the gt-number of $G$ and is denoted as $gt(G)$. In this paper, we introduce the \textit{Edge geodesic transversal problem} as the edge-based extension of the geodesic transversal problem.
arxiv:2610.36821.authors: R. Prabha, B. Sandhiya, Paul Manuel

arxiv:2610.36842.title: The numerical range of limits of real rational functions
arxiv:2610.36842.summary: Given two nonzero polynomials $f, g \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ vanishing at the origin $0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we study the numerical range of the limit $$ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}, $$ denoted by $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$, which is defined as the set of all possible limits of the rational function $\displaystyle\frac{f}{g}$ as $x$ tends to $0$. When $n = 2$ and $g$ has a non-isolated zero at $0$, we describe all possible forms of $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$ and provide an effective algorithm to compute this set based on Puiseux expansions. This is a follow-up to our recent results~\cite{Dinh2025}, in which we only considered the case when $0$ is an isolated zero of $g$.
arxiv:2610.36842.authors: Si Tiep Dinh, Feng Guo, Hong Duc Nguyen, Tien Son Pham

arxiv:2610.36843.title: A minimising principle for interval covers of zigzag persistence modules
arxiv:2610.36843.summary: Zigzag persistence modules serve as an essential tool in topological data analysis. The fundamental theorem of persistent homology states that any zigzag persistence module decomposes into a direct sum of simple building blocks called interval modules. We consider an interval cover, a possibly redundant family of interval submodules spanning every vertex space of a finite zigzag persistence module.
arxiv:2610.36843.authors: Junyan Chu, Shizuo Kaji, Meiyan Kang

arxiv:2610.36883.title: Maximum Energy of Integral Circulant Graphs with Same-Parity Exponents
arxiv:2610.36883.summary: The energy of a finite graph is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Let n be p to the power a times q to the power b, where p and q are distinct primes at least five and a and b, both positive integers, have the same parity. Among all nonempty sets D of proper divisors of n, the energy of the corresponding integral circulant graph is maximised by exactly two divisor sets: the divisors p to the power i times q to the power j with i plus j odd, and the divisors with i plus j even after removing p to the power a times q to the power b.

arxiv:2610.36893.title: Geometric structures, orbit closures and invariant measures in moduli spaces
arxiv:2610.36893.summary: Building on the seminal work of Eskin, Mirzakhani and Mohammadi in the context of dynamics on moduli spaces, we introduce linear loci and linear measures to provide a relatively basic description of orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces. We use this to discuss geometrical properties of orbit closures and invariant measures from the perspective of geometric structures.

arxiv:2610.36895.title: The unilateral 2-linkage problem
arxiv:2610.36895.summary: We study a new variant of the classical linkage problem for digraphs, which we call {\bf unilateral linkages.} A digraph $D$ is {\bf unilaterally $\bm{k}$-linked} if it satisfies that for every choice of $2k$ distinct vertices $s_1,s_2,\ldots{},s_k,t_1,t_2,\ldots{},t_k$ there are vertex disjoint directed paths $P_1,\ldots{},P_k$ in $D$ such that $P_i$ is either an $(s_i,t_i)$-path or a $(t_i,s_i)$-path for each $i\in [k]$. This is a relaxation of the property of $D$ being $k$-linked, where we insist that each $P_i$ must go from $s_i$ to $t_i$. Clearly every $k$-linked digraph is also unilaterally $k$-linked.
arxiv:2610.36895.authors: J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen, Xiaoying Chen, Panpan Cheng, Jin Yan

arxiv:2610.36903.title: The Kothe Radical in Novikov Algebras
arxiv:2610.36903.summary: We study the Kothe radical (the upper nil radical) in the variety of Novikov algebras. We prove that the class of weakly right nilpotent Novikov algebras coincides with the class of r-nil algebras and forms a radical class. We establish that the Kothe radical is a hereditary radical in the variety of Novikov algebras.

arxiv:2610.36908.title: On finite covers of projective spaces, generic outside of codimension three
arxiv:2610.36908.summary: In the article, we generalize to an arbitrary dimension results obtained by the author and S.Yu. Nemirovski that related to Chisini's conjecture claimed that if $B$ is the discriminant of two generic covers $f_i:X_i\to \mathbb P^2$, $i=1,2$, and $\max (\deg f_1,\deg f_2) \geq 5$, then $f_1$ and $f_2$ are equivalent covers.

arxiv:2610.36912.title: A characterization of equality in the edge-localized Bollob\'{a}s-Nikiforov inequality
arxiv:2610.36912.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge2$. Let $e(G)$ and $\omega(G)$ denote its number of edges and clique number, respectively. Let $\lambda_1(G)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n(G)$ be its adjacency eigenvalues.

arxiv:2610.36913.title: Topology of rational equivalence closures and Lawson homology
arxiv:2610.36913.summary: Rational equivalence need not be closed in the Chow topology, and its closure can have infinitely generated homotopy groups. For a connected reduced complex projective variety, we prove that this closure is locally contractible and that its quotient in the algebraically trivial cycles is a finite or countable weak product of circles. The quotient map admits a global continuous section.

arxiv:2610.36920.title: Exploring Neural Dynamics with Time Delays: A Numerical and Bifurcation Analysis Approach
arxiv:2610.36920.summary: The Wilson-Cowan model is a classic example of a ``neural mass model'' - a simplified yet powerful way to describe the activity of large networks of neurons. It is particularly interesting because, even in its relatively simple form, it can produce a surprising variety of behaviours, from steady rhythms to complex oscillations. A key factor influencing these dynamics is the presence of time delays, reflecting the time it takes for signals to travel between neurons.
arxiv:2610.36920.authors: Martin R Nelson, Jonathan J Crofts

arxiv:2610.36942.title: Homotopy operations on higher Lie algebras
arxiv:2610.36942.summary: We determine the multiplicative structures of the homotopy operations on derived Lie algebras, derived restricted Lie algebras and partition Lie algebras, as well as the relation between these. Under Koszul duality, this follows from a calculation of the homotopy operations on derived rings, p-truncated algebras and divided power algebras over $\mathbb{F}_p$.

arxiv:2610.36964.title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
arxiv:2610.36964.summary: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum.

arxiv:2610.36966.title: Compact generation and perfect objects in homotopy categories of exact model structures
arxiv:2610.36966.summary: Compact generation allows large triangulated categories to be studied through suitably small objects. For homotopy categories arising from exact model structures, a natural question is how this intrinsic notion of smallness relates to finite presentation in the underlying exact category. In this paper, we investigate this relation for hereditary projective model structures generated by finitely presented Gorenstein projective objects.

arxiv:2610.36975.title: Bethe Cycles, Frobenius Identities, and Quantum/Classical Duality
arxiv:2610.36975.summary: We study Frobenius action on the trigonometric Ruijsenaars--Schneider system associated with cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties. The construction continues the program initiated by Etingof and Varchenko and developed in quantum $K$-theory by the author and Smirnov. We explain how the monodromy eigenvectors recently constructed by Tarasov and Varchenko fit the quantum/classical duality between Bethe equations and tRS level sets.

arxiv:2610.36993.title: Factorizations by column blocks and Schubert polynomials as products of key polynomials
arxiv:2610.36993.summary: We classify the Schubert polynomials that are products of key polynomials and explicitly determine their finest key factorization. Their indexing permutations are precisely those avoiding ten classical patterns of length six, which form the minimal pattern basis. More generally, the connected components of the column interaction graph give the unique finest factorization of a dual flagged Weyl character into nonconstant diagram characters.
arxiv:2610.36993.authors: Xuanying Han, Shunli Ma, Sophie C. C. Sun

arxiv:2610.37002.title: Klt varieties with semipositive anticanonical bundle : symmetric tensors, holonomy and structure
arxiv:2610.37002.summary: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. The study of the holonomy of such varieties yields generalizations of several results. We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi.

arxiv:2610.37010.title: Resolving a Problem of Lv and Koolen on the Smallest Eigenvalue of Distance-Regular Graphs
arxiv:2610.37010.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a distance-regular graph with valency $k$, diameter $D\ge3$, and eigenvalues $k=\theta_0>\theta_1>\cdots>\theta_D$. Put $b\coloneqq b_1/(\theta_1+1)$, and let $1=u_0>u_1>\cdots>u_D$ be the standard sequence associated with $\theta_1$. Lv and Koolen asked whether the negative of the smallest eigenvalue of a distance-regular graph can be bounded above in terms of its diameter $D$ and the parameter $b$ alone.
arxiv:2610.37010.authors: Zhen-Mu Hong, Fu-Tao Hu, Chenhui Lv

arxiv:2610.37016.title: Finite Tensor 2-Categories
arxiv:2610.37016.summary: We propose a definition of a finite linear 2-category, as a 2-categorical analogue of the notion of a finite abelian category of Etingof-Ostrik. We go on to prove that finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives are precisely the Morita 2-categories of (all) algebras in a finite multitensor category. Thus, finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives can be viewed as `non-semisimple' generalizations of the finite semisimple 2-categories of Douglas-Reutter.
arxiv:2610.37016.authors: Thibault D. D\'ecoppet, Mateusz Stroi\'nski, Tony Zorman

arxiv:2610.37017.title: From amplituhedra to flagtopes
arxiv:2610.37017.summary: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$.
arxiv:2610.37017.authors: Grant T. Barkley, Steven N. Karp, Kaitao Xie

arxiv:2610.37032.title: Bridgeland stability and Gieseker stability I: Limit stability
arxiv:2610.37032.summary: We study the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability conditions on smooth projective varieties. For each fixed ray in a suitable angular sector, we prove that an object of $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$ is Bridgeland (semi)stable in the corresponding hearts for all sufficiently large radii if and only if it is a pure $H$-Gieseker (semi)stable sheaf. In this sector, we identify the category of coherent sheaves as the limiting heart in the sense of eventual membership.

arxiv:2610.37053.title: A sparse canonical Rado theorem
arxiv:2610.37053.summary: Canonical Ramsey theory studies structured colour patterns in colourings with arbitrarily many colours. Lefmann's canonical Rado theorem extends the canonical van der Waerden theorem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham to partition-regular linear systems. Recently, Alvarado, Kohayakawa, Morris, Mota and Ortega proved a sparse canonical van der Waerden theorem for random set $[n]_p$.
arxiv:2610.37053.authors: Zhenzhen Lou, Guangfu Wang, Man Wu, Zhifei Yan

arxiv:2610.37057.title: Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
arxiv:2610.37057.summary: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

arxiv:2610.37075.title: All Strict Calabi--Yau Threefolds of Height One Lift to Characteristic 0
arxiv:2610.37075.summary: We prove that every strict Calabi--Yau threefold of Artin--Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a projective lift to W(k). No assumption is made on the torsion in its crystalline cohomology, and p is arbitrary. Using the crystalline period map of Brantner and Taelman, we show that the obstruction to extending a lift over W_n(k) is the Bockstein of a torsion coordinate of its period point, and that this coordinate can always be made to vanish by varying the lift.

arxiv:2610.37119.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
arxiv:2610.37119.summary: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemer\'edi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

arxiv:2610.37125.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
arxiv:2610.37125.summary: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known.

arxiv:2610.37136.title: On additive bases of finite abelian groups
arxiv:2610.37136.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, and let $c_0(G)$ be the least integer $t$ such that every regular sequence over $G$ of length at least $t$ is an additive basis. Additive bases have been extensively studied in additive combinatorics, and the exact value of $c_0(G)$ has been determined for many groups of rank at least three and some groups of rank two (in which case groups of the form $C_p\oplus C_{pn}$ turn out to be exceptional). In this paper, we continue the study of $c_0(G)$ and obtain the following results.

arxiv:2610.37163.title: Maximal geometric quotients of flag varieties
arxiv:2610.37163.summary: We introduce the notion of maximal geometric quotient, namely a geometric quotient of a polarized pair under a torus action which has a birational contraction to any other GIT quotient. For the action of the maximal torus on a complete flag variety, we show that a maximal geometric quotient exists and it is a Mori dream space, and its Cox ring is isomorphic to the Cox ring of the flag variety. We discuss birational properties of the maximal geometric quotients, their relations with the Chow quotients and explain how to construct them for maximal torus actions on flag varieties.
arxiv:2610.37163.authors: Lorenzo Barban, Michele Bianco, Luis E. Sol\'a Conde

arxiv:2610.37167.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
arxiv:2610.37167.summary: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$.

arxiv:2610.37173.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
arxiv:2610.37173.summary: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, K\"uhn and Osthus from 2016.

arxiv:2610.37184.title: Representations of shifted quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras II: Non simply-laced types and cluster expansions
arxiv:2610.37184.summary: We extend our previous results on cluster structures in the Grothendieck rings of categories $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for shifted quantum affine algebras to the non-simply laced types. We also show that, for all types, the formal power series expressions of the cluster monomials in terms of classes of positive prefundamental representations can be regarded as limits of cluster expansions, thus establishing their positivity.
arxiv:2610.37184.authors: Christof Geiss, David Hernandez, Bernard Leclerc

arxiv:2610.37207.title: A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture
arxiv:2610.37207.summary: We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with "negative enough" Euler form.

arxiv:2610.37208.title: Counting and Sampling Git Graphs
arxiv:2610.37208.summary: Version Control Systems, like Git and Mercurial, represent the history of a project as a Directed Acyclic Graph, capturing divergences and merges throughout development. A widely adopted workflow, the feature branch workflow, imposes a particularly simple structure: a single main branch and features branches evolving in parallel without interfering with one another. This work presents an enumerative study of these Git graphs.

arxiv:2610.37246.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
arxiv:2610.37246.summary: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics.
arxiv:2610.37246.authors: Peter Hegarty, Damiano Ognissanti, Edvin Wedin

arxiv:2610.37273.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
arxiv:2610.37273.summary: We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula. As an application, we prove that the small quantum cohomology of the type-$E$ generalized Grassmannians $E_7/P_2,E_7/P_4,E_7/P_5,E_8/P_6$ is generically semisimple.

arxiv:2610.37291.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
arxiv:2610.37291.summary: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups.
arxiv:2610.37291.authors: Li Luo, Rui Song, Yang Yang

arxiv:2610.37315.title: The maximum size of intersecting $k$-graphs with covering number $k$
arxiv:2610.37315.summary: Let $m(k)$ be the maximum size of an intersecting $k$-graph with covering number $k$. In the present paper, it is proved that for all $k>e^{32}$, \[ m(k)\ge k^k\exp\bigl(-50\sqrt{k\log k}\bigr). \] Together with Zakharov's upper bound \cite{Z}, this implies $m(k)=k^k\exp\bigl(-k^{1/2+o(1)}\bigr)$.
arxiv:2610.37315.authors: Peter Frankl, Jian Wang, Yaoran Yang, Yutong Zhang

arxiv:2610.37317.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
arxiv:2610.37317.summary: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves.

arxiv:2610.37351.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
arxiv:2610.37351.summary: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations.
arxiv:2610.37351.authors: Annika Burmester, Steven Charlton, Abhiram Kidambi, Felix Lotter, Rosa Prei{\ss}

arxiv:2610.37372.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
arxiv:2610.37372.summary: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment.
arxiv:2610.37372.authors: Andr\'es S\'anchez, Leon A. Valencia, Jorge M. Ramirez Osorio

arxiv:2610.37392.title: The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure
arxiv:2610.37392.summary: In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with…

arxiv:2610.37395.title: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model
arxiv:2610.37395.summary: The spatial chromatic model (SCM) is a novel entity-oriented spatial data model proposed in recent years. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM.

arxiv:2610.37396.title: Finite group actions on the non-minimal nilpotent orbit closures in type A
arxiv:2610.37396.summary: We study quotients of the closures of the nilpotent orbits of type A by finite groups of inner automorphisms. Assuming the nilpotent orbit is not minimal, we show that the Q-factorial terminalizations of quotients of nilpotent orbit closures are precisely the quotients of the symplectic resolutions of the orbit closures. This identifies the Mori fan of each Q-factorial terminalization of the quotient with the Mori fan of a symplectic resolution of the orbit closure.
arxiv:2610.37396.authors: Gwyn Bellamy, Misha Feigin, Pavel Shlykov

arxiv:2610.37399.title: Representation and abelianization growth, particularly along expanding sequences
arxiv:2610.37399.summary: We study two obstructions to a finite group $G$ having a generating $d$-tuple whose Cayley graph has spectral gap at least $\epsilon$. Lubotzky and Weiss proved that such a gap forces $\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, the largest order of the abelianization of a subgroup of index at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk))$, while de la Harpe, Robertson and Valette proved that it forces $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)$, the number of irreducible complex representations of degree at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk^2))$. We show that the first bound implies the second, and in fact implies it with $k^2$ replaced by $k\log k$.

arxiv:2610.37401.title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
arxiv:2610.37401.summary: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.
arxiv:2610.37401.authors: Alexandra Blessing Neam\c{t}u, Hongjun Gao, Haoyuan Li

arxiv:2610.37408.title: High powers of grids in random geometric graphs and thresholds for wide spanning structures
arxiv:2610.37408.summary: Using results of Leighton and Shor and of Shor and Yukich, we present a connection between $d$-dimensional bandwidth and (sharp) thresholds in $d$-dimensional random geometric graphs: namely, that the sharp threshold for a given graph property in random geometric graphs is determined by its $d$-dimensional bandwidth, and vice versa, whenever the $d$-dimensional bandwidth of this property grows sufficiently fast (at least polylogarithmically) with the order of the graphs. This connection provides a number of corollaries, such as new information about the sharp thresholds for containing different spanning subgraphs in $1$-dimensional random geometric graphs, as well as asymptotically tight…

arxiv:2610.37417.title: Nonexistence of Hadamard difference sets in groups of order $4p^2$ with $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, $p\ge 7$
arxiv:2610.37417.summary: We show that the Frobenius group $\langle x,y,z\mid x^p=y^p=z^4=1,\ xy=yx,\ zxz^{-1}=y,\ zyz^{-1}=x^{-1}\rangle$ of order $4p^2$ contains no $(4p^2,2p^2-p,p^2-p)$ difference set if $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$ is a prime with $p \geq 7$. Together with results of McFarland, Iiams and Liebler this shows that no group of order $4p^2$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and $p \geq 7$ contains a Hadamard difference set.

arxiv:2610.37421.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Codimension-Two Reduction, and Transverse Products
arxiv:2610.37421.summary: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, and product constructions. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy.

arxiv:2610.37423.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
arxiv:2610.37423.summary: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$.

arxiv:2610.37439.title: Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature
arxiv:2610.37439.summary: We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure.

arxiv:2610.37460.title: Rank reduction in orthosymplectic types
arxiv:2610.37460.summary: This note establishes a rank reduction for RLL-realization of quantum affine supergroups of orthosymplectic type. In the rational limit, this provides a more conceptual proof of the analogous result for orthosymplectic superYangians from arXiv:2311.18818. We also determine the exact scalar prefactor appearing in the evaluation of the universal $R$-matrix, refining the main result of arXiv:2408.16720.

arxiv:2610.37463.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
arxiv:2610.37463.summary: We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.

arxiv:2610.37468.title: Multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds and the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials
arxiv:2610.37468.summary: We establish uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for polynomials of Zakeri type, where all free critical points are on the boundary of an invariant Siegel disk of bounded type. This generalizes the unicritical result~\cite{DL:wZ}. As an application, we show the optimality of the Brjuno condition under the Zakeri restriction: as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno, the Siegel disk evolves into the Cremer Hedgehog.
arxiv:2610.37468.authors: Dzmitry Dudko, Yusheng Luo, Runze Zhang

arxiv:2610.37477.title: The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
arxiv:2610.37477.summary: This article primarily investigates the Assouad dimension of graphs of continuous functions. Initially, the Assouad spectrum of the graph of a H\"older and count-H\"older continuous function has been derived. It has been shown that the Assouad dimension of the graph of a continuous function $f:[a,b]\to \mathbb{R}$ with the count-H\"older condition is at least \( 1 + \sup \left\{ \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}L_f(y) : y \in \mathscr{R}_f[a,b]\right\} \) where $\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}$ denotes the upper box dimension, $L_f(y)$ is the level set of $f$ at level $y$, and $\mathscr{R}_f[a,b]$ is the range of $f$ on $[a,b]$.
arxiv:2610.37477.authors: Binyan Yu, Bilel Selmi, Jia Liu, Yongshun Liang

arxiv:2610.37479.title: Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles
